item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the SOTA review and bundling plan (`docs/plans/sota-and-bundling.md` rev 7 and `docs/plans/remote-and-multi-user.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`; plan reviewed by two independent critic passes). Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5 on 2026-10-25 by source trace and/or an executed probe (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 310 tests ... OK`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #21._

## Summary
After this PR:

**`triage`** ranks workable open issues with a transparent heuristic that shows every input:
- **demand:** reactions, participants, comments, inbound duplicates and mentions;
- **leverage:** items it blocks, sub-issue gap, milestone due date;
- **risk:** reopen count, hotspot and revert history of its files, and a regression flag;
- **explicit:** issue type, label weights and issue-field values.

Each excluded issue states why: blocked, assigned, has an open linked PR, or locked.

**`bundle`** proposes 2–3-issue bundles **for one agent to work in sequence**. Each bundle carries:
- per-pair rationale and its file set (direct, linked and analog);
- the tests that historically co-changed with those files;
- open-PR collisions and dependency order;
- a risk summary and a `why_not_bigger` explanation;
- a stable `bundle_id`.

By default, bundles shown together never share files.

**`brief N`** returns a token-budgeted work packet. GitHub-authored text is marked untrusted. CI and review state appear only under `--live`, read live and never stored.

The bundled skill also gains the recipe for picking and bundling work.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **`open` cannot rank anything.** It returns no labels, assignees, linkage or demand signals, sorts only by recency, and the CLI passes no limit. [VERIFIED: `zaxbygraph open --limit 5` → exit 2 `unrecognized arguments: --limit 5`.]
   [query.py#L429-L437](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L429-L437)
   ```py
   def open_items(
       conn: sqlite3.Connection,
       repo: str | None = None,
       limit: int | None = None,
       offset: int = 0,
   ) -> list[dict]:
       repo = _fold_repo(repo)
       sql = """
           SELECT repo, number, kind, title, author, updated_at, html_url
   ```
2. **`churn` counts unmerged PRs,** so it is not a hotspot signal. [VERIFIED by probe: a closed, unmerged PR (`merged_at` NULL) is counted in `churn`.]
   [query.py#L415-L419](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L415-L419)
   ```py
       sql = """
           SELECT path, COUNT(*) AS prs,
                  SUM(additions) AS additions, SUM(deletions) AS deletions
           FROM pr_files
       """
   ```
3. **No ranking, bundling or work-packet command exists.** [VERIFIED by grep over `src/zaxbygraph/`.]

**Evidence-based constraints** (each source retrieved and confirmed this session):
- CooperBench (arXiv 2601.13295) finds about 30% lower success when agents split coupled work, so a bundle is for **one** agent.
- AgenticFlict (2604.03551) finds 27.67% of 107K agent PRs conflict, and Co-Coder (2606.00953) gains from cohesion-aware partitioning with hub isolation, so **cross-bundle file disjointness is the default**.
- ChainSWE (2607.02606) finds per-bug success falls up to 70% along dependent chains, so **the size cap is 3, with dependency order kept**.

> **argv convention note.** CONTRIBUTING:139 names `python -m pytest <file> -q`, and issues #1–#7 used `python -m unittest tests.<module>...`; both fail at base with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fixtures'` for the 23 test modules that `from fixtures import` (VERIFIED: `python -m pytest tests/test_store.py -q` → collection error; `python -m unittest tests.test_store` → ImportError). Every argv here therefore uses the form that works at base, `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p <file> -k <test> -b`, whose absence signature is `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5). [Workstream C] PR 1 of 1 repairs the documented forms.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN `triage` runs on a fixture THE SYSTEM SHALL order open issues exactly by the documented formula over the echoed weights, and return every raw feature and gate reason; before #27 lands, A06-dependent features are `null` with `requires`.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_triage_bundle.py" -k test_triage_matches_hand_computed_formula -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_triage_bundle.py
  - why: There is no command at base.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN an issue has `blocked_by_open > 0`, an assignee, an open linked PR, or is locked THE SYSTEM SHALL exclude it by default and name the gate.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_triage_bundle.py" -k test_triage_gates_named -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_triage_bundle.py
  - why: There is no command at base.
- [ ] AC3: WHEN `bundle --size 2-3 --count K` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL return at most K bundles of 2–3 members built greedily (ties by number), with no file shared across bundles unless `--allow-shared-files` is passed.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_triage_bundle.py" -k test_bundles_disjoint_and_sized -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_triage_bundle.py
  - why: There is no command at base.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN a bundle is returned THE SYSTEM SHALL include the per-pair rationale, a direct/linked/analog file split, historically co-changed tests (config globs), open-PR collisions, the in-pool `blocked_by` order, the risk summary, `why_not_bigger`, and `bundle_id` = sha1 of the sorted members plus the config hash.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_triage_bundle.py" -k test_bundle_payload_complete -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_triage_bundle.py
  - why: There is no command at base.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN two pool members are a `duplicate_of`/`duplicate_keyword` pair, or score as `possible_duplicate` THE SYSTEM SHALL offer a merge candidate instead of bundling them, and list text-related but anchor-less pairs as `related_not_bundleable`.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_triage_bundle.py" -k test_duplicates_and_related_not_bundleable -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_triage_bundle.py
  - why: There is no command at base.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN `brief N --budget-tokens B` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL return a packet whose chars/4 estimate is ≤ B, with every GitHub-authored string wrapped as untrusted content.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_triage_bundle.py" -k test_brief_budget_and_trust_marking -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_triage_bundle.py
  - why: There is no command at base.
- [ ] AC7: WHEN `open --limit/--offset/--kind/--label` and `churn --merged-only` run THE SYSTEM SHALL honour them, with `open` rows carrying labels, assignees and linked open PRs.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_triage_bundle.py" -k test_open_and_churn_surface -b`
  - expect: FAIL: `open --limit` exits 2 (`unrecognized arguments`), and churn counts the unmerged PR.
  - files: tests/test_triage_bundle.py
  - why: RED at base per claims 1–2.
- [ ] AC8: WHEN the bundled skill is read THE SYSTEM SHALL document the status → triage → bundle → verify workflow, with candidates-not-facts wording.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_triage_bundle.py" -k test_skill_documents_bundle_workflow -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_triage_bundle.py
  - why: There is no recipe at base.
- [ ] AC9: WHEN default triage weights and the label-weight map format are chosen THE SYSTEM SHALL ship those defaults, documented and echoed in every payload.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(PRODUCT_DECISION)
  - argv: n/a
  - expect: n/a
  - files: n/a
  - why: substitute evidence: the maintainer records the default weights and the label-map format on this issue before closure.

## Scope
**In:** `triage` (two-stage: cheap features for all issues, analogs for the top K only), `bundle`, `brief` (`--live` CI/review read through `gh`, never stored), the `open`/`churn` surface fixes, `bundle --exclude`, the skill recipe, docs.
**Out:** MCP tools (#32).

## Sequence
[Workstream B] Derived read tier: #28 -> #29 -> #30 (this issue is B-03). It consumes Workstream A's evidence; it never writes the store (AGENTS: derived read tier).

## Dependencies
- Depends on: #29, #24 (columns), #27 (link features; degraded behaviour is defined before it lands)

## Files expected to change
`src/zaxbygraph/derive.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/query.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/cli.py`, `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md`, `README.md`, new `tests/test_triage_bundle.py`.

*Anchor v2 (PR #47 review round): CHECK_WRONG amendment wave — the frozen C15 check gained the pytest-availability skip (matching C14), changing the shared tests/test_read_truth.py blob for every check id on that path. 16 AMEND rows appended with a closed reason and a fresh RED/GREEN replay; the acceptance-table semantics digest is CONSTANT with anchor v1 (comment 6533319358) and the checkpoint tree-id is unchanged. Verify with `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug 31-read-truth-env --receipt '<this literal>'`.*

**Recorded amendment to AC3 (follow-up issue #48, collated PR branch `fix/40-48-36-collated-followups`) — maintainer decision 2026-11-01**

AC3's text provided this branch explicitly: *"unless the maintainer amends issue #31 AC3 to fail-loud, in which case this issue closes with that amendment recorded and AC4 applies unchanged."*

**AC3 as amended (fail-loud, recorded justification):** when `ZAXBYGRAPH_PROXY_FORGE_HOST` is set to an unparseable or empty value, the loopback rewrite is disabled and a `git/`-prefixed loopback origin **fails to parse with a loud error** — which, since the collated PR's AC4 work, **names the variable and its disabled state** in the message rather than silently resolving the remote to a literal loopback store key. The zmem literal-key parity behavior is **not** shipped.

**Justification (the swarm-critic position, adopted by the maintainer after the user did not respond to the decision request; the SolCritic literal-key position is recorded as considered-and-declined):** for a durable local evidence store, a disabled proxy rewrite that silently re-keys the store (loopback underscore-folded host instead of the forge) would strand history under an ephemeral key and silently fork the corpus; failing loudly names the cause and keeps `--repo OWNER/REPO` usable. The four-states contract of #31 AC3 remains otherwise in force.

The executable surface of this amendment ships in the collated PR (the parse error naming the variable, frozen check C8; the counterfactual gate including the `.git`-suffixed shape).

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the SOTA review and bundling plan (`docs/plans/sota-and-bundling.md` rev 7 and `docs/plans/remote-and-multi-user.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`; plan reviewed by two independent critic passes). Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5 on 2026-10-25 by source trace and/or an executed probe (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 310 tests ... OK`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #21._

## Summary
After this PR:
- **Closure reads.** `file-history` and `what-closed` report keyword-derived closures (as a separate `keyword_closes` field, never merged into GitHub-reported `closes`), so a REST-only store stops answering "closed nothing".
- **Environment checks on reads.** Read paths enforce the SQLite floor and probe for FTS5 with a clear message.
- **Proxy remotes resolve.** Remote and cloud sessions whose origin is a loopback git proxy resolve the repo, with the same normalization rule zmem uses.
- **Bounded reads.** `item` can cap comments, and CLI reads can bound staleness with `--max-age`.
- **CI and docs.** CI covers the Python versions people actually run, the skill carries a version stamp tested against the CLI, and the documented check commands work.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **Keyword closures are invisible to `file-history` and `what-closed`.** [VERIFIED by probe: on a REST-sourced store where PR #2 says `Fixes #1`, the only edge is `closes_keyword` (`source=keyword`), `file_history` returns `closed_issues: []` and `what_closed(1)` returns `prs: []`.]
   [query.py#L843-L848](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L843-L848)
   ```py
               closes = conn.execute(
                   f"SELECT dst_id{source_col} FROM edges "
                   "WHERE repo = ? AND src_type = 'item' AND src_id = ? "
                   "AND rel = 'closes' AND dst_type = 'item'",
                   (repo, str(n)),
               ).fetchall()
   ```
2. **The SQLite floor is enforced only on the write path, and FTS5 is never probed.** [VERIFIED by probe: `open_existing` made 0 calls to `assert_sqlite_supported`.]
   [db.py#L35-L37](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L35-L37)
   ```py
   def connect(db_path: Path) -> sqlite3.Connection:
       assert_sqlite_supported()
       db_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   ```
3. **Loopback proxy remotes do not parse.** [VERIFIED by probe: `_parse_remote_info('http://local_proxy@127.0.0.1:41233/git/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph')` → `None`, so every repo-less command fails "could not parse origin remote". zmem documents and handles this shape (`ZMEM_PROXY_FORGE_HOST`, zaxbysauce/zmem `docs/CLOUD.md`).]
   [repo.py#L152-L154](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/repo.py#L152-L154)
   ```py
       info = _parse_remote_info(proc.stdout)
       if info is None:
           raise RepoError(f"could not parse origin remote: {_redact_url(proc.stdout.strip())!r}")
   ```
4. **`item` truncates bodies but returns every comment.** [VERIFIED: `item 1 --max-comments 2` → exit 2 `unrecognized arguments`; [cli.py#L636-L656](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L636-L656).]
5. **CI runs only Python 3.11 and 3.12.** [VERIFIED:]
   [ci.yml#L18](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/.github/workflows/ci.yml#L18)
   ```yaml
           python-version: ["3.11", "3.12"]
   ```
6. **The documented check commands fail at base.** Both `python -m pytest <file> -q` (CONTRIBUTING:139) and `python -m unittest tests.<module>` fail to import 23 test modules (`No module named 'fixtures'`). [VERIFIED by running both.] The skill has no version stamp (VERIFIED by grep), while `zaxbygraph --version` reports `0.4.0`.

> **argv convention note.** CONTRIBUTING:139 names `python -m pytest <file> -q`, and issues #1–#7 used `python -m unittest tests.<module>...`; both fail at base with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fixtures'` for the 23 test modules that `from fixtures import` (VERIFIED: `python -m pytest tests/test_store.py -q` → collection error; `python -m unittest tests.test_store` → ImportError). Every argv here therefore uses the form that works at base, `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p <file> -k <test> -b`, whose absence signature is `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5). [Workstream C] PR 1 of 1 repairs the documented forms.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN a PR's only closure of #N is `closes_keyword` THE SYSTEM SHALL report N under `keyword_closes` in `file-history` and `what-closed`, leaving `closed_issues`/`prs` for GitHub-reported `closes` only.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_read_truth.py" -k test_keyword_closes_reported_separately -b`
  - expect: FAIL: `closed_issues == []` and `prs == []`; no `keyword_closes` key (probe-observed).
  - files: tests/test_read_truth.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 1.
- [ ] AC2: IF SQLite is below the floor, or FTS5 is unavailable THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL fail every read command with the explicit floor or FTS5 message, not a bare SQL error.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_read_truth.py" -k test_read_path_enforces_floor_and_fts5 -b`
  - expect: FAIL: `open_existing` succeeds with the floor check patched to fail (0 calls observed).
  - files: tests/test_read_truth.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 2.
- [ ] AC3: WHEN the origin remote is `http://<user>@127.0.0.1:<port>/git/<org>/<repo>` (or `localhost`/`::1`/`[::1]`) THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve `github.com/<org>/<repo>`, honour `ZAXBYGRAPH_PROXY_FORGE_HOST` (unset, valid, unparseable, empty) exactly as zmem's four states, and pass a shared normalization test-vector file.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_read_truth.py" -k test_loopback_proxy_remote_resolves -b`
  - expect: FAIL: `_parse_remote_info(...)` is `None` (probe-observed).
  - files: tests/test_read_truth.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 3.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN `item N --max-comments K` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL return at most K comments (first, last, and maintainer comments preferred) plus `comments_omitted`.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_read_truth.py" -k test_item_max_comments -b`
  - expect: FAIL: exit 2, `unrecognized arguments: --max-comments`.
  - files: tests/test_read_truth.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 4.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN a CLI read is passed `--max-age D` and the store is older than D THE SYSTEM SHALL run the locked incremental sync first and report `freshness.refreshed: true`; without the flag, reads never write.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_read_truth.py" -k test_max_age_refreshes_only_when_asked -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_read_truth.py
  - why: There is no flag at base.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN the CI workflow is parsed THE SYSTEM SHALL list Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 and 3.14 on both Windows and Linux.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_read_truth.py" -k test_ci_matrix_versions -b`
  - expect: FAIL: matrix is `["3.11", "3.12"]`.
  - files: tests/test_read_truth.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 5.
- [ ] AC7: WHEN `python -m pytest tests/test_store.py -q` or `python -m unittest tests.test_store` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL collect and pass, and CONTRIBUTING's argv note SHALL name a form that works.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_read_truth.py" -k test_documented_check_forms_import -b`
  - expect: FAIL: `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fixtures'`.
  - files: tests/test_read_truth.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 6.
- [ ] AC8: WHEN the docs test runs THE SYSTEM SHALL find `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md` stamped with a version equal to the package `__version__`.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_read_truth.py" -k test_skill_version_stamp_matches_cli -b`
  - expect: FAIL: the skill has no version stamp.
  - files: tests/test_read_truth.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 6.
- [ ] AC9: WHEN the SQLite floor guard runs on current SQLite THE SYSTEM SHALL still reject old versions on the write path.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_query.py" -k test_sqlite_floor_guard_rejects_old_sqlite -b`
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_query.py
  - why: GREEN at base.
- [ ] AC10: WHEN worktrees and MCP roots resolve the repo THE SYSTEM SHALL keep resolving the same store.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_mcp.py" -k test_worktree_and_roots_resolve_same_db -b`
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_mcp.py
  - why: GREEN at base; the proxy rewrite must not change normal remotes.

## Scope
**In:** all of the above, plus the README and skill wording that keeps `closes` and `closes_keyword` distinct (AGENTS).
**Out:** distribution (PyPI, MCP Registry), which is gated in #32.

## Sequence
[Workstream C] Read truth and environment: #31 only (this issue is C-01). Parallel-safe: it can merge any time. If #22 merges first, rebase on its `query.py` read-path rewrites.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: none
- Schema after: none
- Gated on: none

## Files expected to change
`src/zaxbygraph/query.py` (soft conflict with #22), `src/zaxbygraph/db.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/repo.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/cli.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `tests/__init__.py` (or `tests/conftest.py`), `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md`, `README.md`, new `tests/test_read_truth.py`.

## Definition of done
All ACs pass on every CI leg, and `## Closure evidence` is in the PR body.

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the SOTA review and bundling plan (`docs/plans/sota-and-bundling.md` rev 7 and `docs/plans/remote-and-multi-user.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`; plan reviewed by two independent critic passes). Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5 on 2026-10-25 by source trace and/or an executed probe (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 310 tests ... OK`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #21._

## Summary
After this PR, every MCP tool:
- declares an `outputSchema` (permissive, `additionalProperties: true`);
- returns the envelope as `structuredContent` alongside the existing text block;
- carries `annotations` (`readOnlyHint: true` on everything except `sync`).

These are features of 2025-06-18, which the server already advertises. The server also adds `similar_items`, `triage`, `bundle`, `brief` and `churn` tools, and negotiates protocol 2025-11-25.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **Every tool result is a text block only.** [VERIFIED by probe: `tools/list` has 11 tools, none with `outputSchema` or `annotations`; results carry no `structuredContent`.]
   [mcp_server.py#L1133-L1140](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py#L1133-L1140)
   ```py
           _result(
               stdout,
               req_id,
               {
                   "content": [{"type": "text", "text": json.dumps(env, ensure_ascii=False)}],
                   "isError": env.get("error") is not None,
               },
           )
   ```
2. **The server tops out at protocol 2025-06-18.** [VERIFIED by probe: `initialize` requesting `2025-11-25` is answered `2025-06-18`.]
   [mcp_server.py#L65-L66](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py#L65-L66)
   ```py
   _PROTOCOL_VERSIONS = ("2025-06-18", "2025-03-26", "2024-11-05")
   _LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = _PROTOCOL_VERSIONS[0]
   ```
3. **There is no `churn` tool,** although the CLI has one. [VERIFIED: the tool list is `file_history, get_item, graph_status, open_items, path, pr_overlap, related, search, sql, sync, what_closed`.]
4. **Structured output and annotations are already part of 2025-06-18.** [VERIFIED from the official MCP changelogs (the modelcontextprotocol GitHub repo).] Tool annotations date to 2025-03-26.

**Considered, not filed:**
- **Moving bad-argument errors to tool results.** The critic proposed it, but the server already returns bad tool arguments as `isError: true` tool results (probe: `get_item` with `number: "x"`). Only an unknown tool name is a JSON-RPC `-32602`, which the spec keeps as a protocol error.

> **argv convention note.** CONTRIBUTING:139 names `python -m pytest <file> -q`, and issues #1–#7 used `python -m unittest tests.<module>...`; both fail at base with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fixtures'` for the 23 test modules that `from fixtures import` (VERIFIED: `python -m pytest tests/test_store.py -q` → collection error; `python -m unittest tests.test_store` → ImportError). Every argv here therefore uses the form that works at base, `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p <file> -k <test> -b`, whose absence signature is `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5). [Workstream C] PR 1 of 1 repairs the documented forms.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN `tools/list` is called THE SYSTEM SHALL return an `outputSchema` and `annotations` for every tool, with `readOnlyHint: true` on all but `sync`.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_mcp_typed.py" -k test_tools_declare_schema_and_annotations -b`
  - expect: FAIL: `any_outputSchema False`, `any_annotations False` (probe-observed).
  - files: tests/test_mcp_typed.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 1.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN any tool call succeeds or fails THE SYSTEM SHALL return `structuredContent` equal to the parsed text block, and the result SHALL validate against the tool's `outputSchema`.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_mcp_typed.py" -k test_structured_content_matches_text -b`
  - expect: FAIL: there is no `structuredContent` key.
  - files: tests/test_mcp_typed.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 1.

## Problem (claims to verify)

2. **The server requires the `initialize` handshake and implements `ping`.** Both are removed in 2026-07-28. [VERIFIED: [mcp_server.py#L1088-L1110](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py#L1088-L1110).]

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the SOTA review and bundling plan (`docs/plans/sota-and-bundling.md` rev 7 and `docs/plans/remote-and-multi-user.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`; plan reviewed by two independent critic passes). Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5 on 2026-10-25 by source trace and/or an executed probe (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 310 tests ... OK`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #21._

## Summary
After this PR:
- **`snapshot publish`** pushes a verified store snapshot as a single-commit orphan. It runs under the sync lock, takes a `Connection.backup()` copy, vacuums it, gzips it, splits it under 100 MB and writes a manifest of hashes.
- **Where the snapshot lives.** Either a non-`heads` ref in the repo itself, so access matches the repo's, or a private store repo. `gh` stays the only credential.
- **`snapshot pull`** verifies every hash, runs `quick_check`, refuses a newer schema, and never replaces a newer local store. It records snapshot provenance, and `--verify-sample N` optionally re-fetches N random items to compare `content_hash`.
- **After the pull**, a normal incremental `sync` fetches only the delta.
- **One writer, many readers.** One machine or one scheduled Action using `GITHUB_TOKEN` (not a PAT) publishes. Everyone else only pulls.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **No mechanism exists to move a verified store between machines.** `doctor --consolidate` copies only between local paths, and the README forbids committing `history.db`. [VERIFIED: [doctor.py#L1-L40](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L1-L40); README "Do not commit `history.db`".]
2. **A remote session starts with a cold sync of the full history.** [VERIFIED: resolution creates no store on read, and only `sync` creates one ([db.py#L121-L137](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/b47913eeeb90095b8a15998eae34413523853fa5/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L121-L137)).] Once #31 resolves proxy remotes, the cost a remote session pays is entirely the cold sync.

**Design premise to settle during implementation.** Whether GitHub accepts pushes to a custom `refs/zaxbygraph/*` namespace is not verified. AC6 settles it. The fallback is a `zaxbygraph-snapshot` branch.

> **argv convention note.** CONTRIBUTING:139 names `python -m pytest <file> -q`, and issues #1–#7 used `python -m unittest tests.<module>...`; both fail at base with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'fixtures'` for the 23 test modules that `from fixtures import` (VERIFIED: `python -m pytest tests/test_store.py -q` → collection error; `python -m unittest tests.test_store` → ImportError). Every argv here therefore uses the form that works at base, `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p <file> -k <test> -b`, whose absence signature is `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5). [Workstream C] PR 1 of 1 repairs the documented forms.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN `snapshot publish` targets a local bare repo THE SYSTEM SHALL push one orphan commit holding the gzip parts and a manifest (`zaxbygraph.snapshot.v1`, `user_version`, `repo`, `host`, watermark, `corpus_sha256`, `db_sha256`, `gz_sha256`, parts, publisher), replacing the previous commit.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_snapshot.py" -k test_publish_single_orphan_commit -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_snapshot.py
  - why: There is no command at base.
- [ ] AC2: IF the store reports `complete: false` or a non-null `last_error` THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse to publish.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_snapshot.py" -k test_publish_refuses_incomplete -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_snapshot.py
  - why: There is no command at base.
- [ ] AC3: IF a pulled part or database fails its sha256, fails `quick_check`, or has `user_version` newer than this build THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL refuse it and leave the local store untouched.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_snapshot.py" -k test_pull_refuses_tampered_or_newer -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_snapshot.py
  - why: There is no command at base.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN the local store's watermark is newer than the snapshot's THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the local store unless `--force` is passed, and SHALL otherwise install atomically under the sync lock and record provenance in `status`.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_snapshot.py" -k test_pull_keeps_newer_local -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_snapshot.py
  - why: There is no command at base.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN a snapshot is published and pulled THE SYSTEM SHALL yield equal `corpus_sha256` on both sides, on both the Windows and Linux legs.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_snapshot.py" -k test_round_trip_hash -b`
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_snapshot.py
  - why: There is no command at base.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN GitHub is asked to accept a push to `refs/zaxbygraph/snapshot` THE SYSTEM SHALL use it as the default location if accepted, and fall back to a `zaxbygraph-snapshot` branch if refused.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(EXTERNAL_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE)
  - argv: n/a
  - expect: n/a
  - files: n/a
  - why: substitute evidence: a recorded `git push` / `git ls-remote` transcript against a scratch repository, attached to this issue before closure (checks never call GitHub, per CONTRIBUTING).
- [ ] AC7: WHEN the README remote-use section is reviewed THE SYSTEM SHALL document the travel and team recipes, the single-writer rule, and the rule that zaxbygraph snapshot refs and zmem sync repos never share a repository or push credential.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(DOCS_ONLY)
  - argv: n/a
  - expect: n/a
  - files: n/a
  - why: substitute evidence: reviewer approval of the README section on the PR.

## Scope
**In:** `snapshot publish`/`pull`, the manifest, `--verify-sample`, provenance in `status`, the README section, and an example scheduled workflow (docs only).
**Out:** a remote MCP server over HTTP (RECORD in the epic).

## Sequence

- Depends on: #28 (`corpus_sha256`), #31 (proxy-remote resolution)
- Schema after: none
- Gated on: AC6 (external verification)

New `src/zaxbygraph/snapshot.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/cli.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/query.py` (`status` provenance), `README.md`, new `tests/test_snapshot.py`.

## Scope

**In:** the C2 and C6 check amendments to runtime/position-capture forms (one checkpoint AMEND, reason `CHECK_WRONG`, with fresh RED/GREEN replays of all six discriminating checks, re-anchored receipt, and amendment approval per the trace contract); C4's `CORPUS_SMALL`/`CORPUS_LARGE` moved to 1000/2000 in the same AMEND; one count-freshness bullet in AGENTS.md's invariants.
**Out:** every other row of PR #35's "Considered, not filed" table (they stay closed under their recorded re-evaluate triggers): `PRAGMA optimize` for doctor/migrations (deferred — the probed scan shape is the historic OR query, no longer shipped), the `what_closed` repo=None branch (dead code; delete/reconcile when query.py is next touched), reviews_fts (cut by the plan critic), the C4 conn-leak nit (rides a future AMEND only if one is already happening for other reasons).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: WHEN the strengthened C2 runs against a store whose items table carries the title index, THE SYSTEM SHALL pass while asserting the EXPLAIN plan of the revert-title statement captured at runtime from a real ingest (connection trace), not a copied literal.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_ingest_scale.py -q -k test_title_lookup_plan_uses_title_index`
  - expect: OK at both ends (the check is a strengthening, not a defect fix); discrimination is demonstrated by the recorded mutant probe — a `LOWER(title)` rewrite of the shipped lookup turns the strengthened check RED while the copied-literal form stays GREEN (probe of record in the PR #35 review, test-infrastructure lane)
  - files: tests/test_ingest_scale.py
  - why: GREEN at base and head today under the copied-literal form; the amendment buys discrimination against runtime query drift, which the current form cannot see
- [ ] AC2: WHEN sync_repo runs, THE SYSTEM SHALL issue `PRAGMA optimize` on the write connection after the finish transaction's COMMIT statement, asserted positionally in the traced statement order.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_ingest_scale.py -q -k test_sync_runs_pragma_optimize`
  - expect: OK at both ends; discrimination demonstrated by the recorded mutant probe — a variant issuing the statement at the start of sync_repo turns the strengthened check RED while the presence-only form stays GREEN
  - files: tests/test_ingest_scale.py
  - why: GREEN at base and head today under the presence-only form; the amendment pins the placement the shipped design depends on (best-effort maintenance after the durable commit)
- [ ] AC3: WHEN C4's cost check runs with `CORPUS_SMALL = 1000` and `CORPUS_LARGE = 2000`, THE SYSTEM SHALL keep both ratios within their 1.25x threshold at head and RED under the pin-reverted mutant.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_ingest_scale.py -q -k test_per_item_cost_is_flat`
  - expect: OK at both ends at both corpus sizes; discrimination evidence of record — pin-reverted mutant ratios 1.961 (item-txn) and 1.8377 (whole-run) at 1k/2k vs head 1.0000/1.0006
  - files: tests/test_ingest_scale.py
  - why: GREEN at base and head at the current 2k/4k sizes; the shrink is a pure cost reduction with probed-equal discrimination (~97s suite wall saved across the CI matrix)
- [ ] AC4: THE SYSTEM SHALL state the count-freshness boundary in AGENTS.md's invariants, naming that `sync_state` counts are finish-time snapshots exact after every completed run and may lag after an interrupted run, cross-referencing docs/schema.md.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(DOCS_ONLY)
  - substitute evidence (review artifact): the AGENTS.md diff adding the invariant bullet, cross-referenced against docs/schema.md's "recomputed when a sync run finishes" paragraph (grep-verified at the anchor commit)
  - substitute evidence (verification): the merged PR's diff view showing the new AGENTS.md bullet
  - files: AGENTS.md
  - why: docs-only; the executable surface (schema_notes.py notes, docs/schema.md) already landed in 0edd793

## Design

1. C2 amendment: mirror C1's round-3 pattern — capture the runtime revert-title SELECT via `conn.set_trace_callback` during a real `sync_repo` ingest, EXPLAIN the captured statement on a stats-cleared fresh connection (C1's established oracle), assert an index seek binding `title=?`.
2. C6 amendment: assert the traced statement order — the finish transaction's COMMIT appears, and the first `pragma optimize` occurrence appears after it.
3. C4 corpus constants: `CORPUS_SMALL = 1000`, `CORPUS_LARGE = 2000` (one-line change; the probed separation holds).
4. All three land as ONE checkpoint AMEND batch (reason `CHECK_WRONG` per pair, fresh base+head replays of all six discriminating checks, re-anchored receipt published to this issue, amendment approved by the implementation reviewer) — never three separate refreezes.
5. AGENTS.md: one bullet under "Correctness of ingest" (or "Integrity of the data") stating the boundary, cross-referencing docs/schema.md; wording mirrors schema_notes.py.

## Files to change

`tests/test_ingest_scale.py` (C2, C6, corpus constants — checkpoint-anchored, AMEND required), `AGENTS.md` (one bullet), the trace's `repro/checkpoint.manifest` + re-anchored receipt (git-excluded).

## Local verification recipe

```
python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_ingest_scale.py" -b
python -m unittest discover -s tests -b
bash .agents/issue-traces/22-cold-sync-scale-indexed-reads/repro/replay-all.sh   # TMPDIR=/e/ZCode/tmp on this host
```

## Dependencies

Depends on: none (post-merge work on main; base = 93201e5025c3bf51255ed7ab725c5ceb703d3cb2).
Gated on: maintainer go-ahead recorded (in-session approval, see preamble).
Blocks: nothing.

## Constraints and invariants

- The checkpoint AMEND path is mandatory: editing the frozen file without AMEND rows + fresh replays + a re-anchored, republished receipt is an anti-tampering violation.
- Plans asserted must stay stats-independent (C1's fresh-connection oracle pattern) — real stores are stats-bearing after their first sync, and the stats-regime remains uncovered by design (PR #35's Considered-not-filed row).
- Windows is first-class: the suite and the amended checks must stay green on the Windows CI legs.
- No schema, no `user_version` change, no new runtime dependencies.

## Definition of done

All four ACs pass on the Windows and Linux CI legs; the amended checks' discrimination evidence (mutant probes) is quoted in the PR body; the trace's replay is 10/10 PASS at the final head with all identities rebound; the PR body says `Closes #<this issue>` and carries the fresh anchor receipt.

item.body:
*Provenance: post-publication swarm-pr-review and independent-critic round of PR #39.* Generated from that round (issue #25, schema v8 revisions), at the maintainer's direction to obtain independent-critic input on an ASK item. Every claim below was re-verified against origin/main at commit d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c on 2026-10-27 by source read and executed probes (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 424 tests ... OK`). One issue = one PR. Review artifacts referenced below live in the git-excluded `.zcode/pr-review/pr39-20261027/` and are quoted inline where load-bearing._

## Summary

After this PR, `doctor --consolidate` can no longer destroy revision evidence the adopted candidate never observed: adoption replaces an item's stored revision history only when the candidate holds revision rows for that item, every consolidation reports what it did to the slug's history, and the docs stop implying that history is carried through when it is deleted. The empty case (a pre-v8 candidate) falls out as the special case: nothing is deleted.

## Problem (claims to verify)

1. **`consolidate()` deletes the slug's revision rows unconditionally, before the copy.** [`VERIFIED`: source read at d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c; executed probe: adopting a zero-revision candidate into a store holding 2 revision rows for the slug leaves 0.] The adoption transaction deletes every `_COPY_TABLES` row for the slug, `revisions` included, then inserts the candidate's rows:

   [doctor.py#L201-L202](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L201-L202)
   ```py
       for table, autoinc_pk in _COPY_TABLES:
           dst.execute(f"DELETE FROM {table} WHERE repo = ?", (repo_l,))
   ```
   (VERIFIED at d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c: source read.)

   `_COPY_TABLES` gained `("revisions", "id")` in PR #39 (doctor.py#L49-L61).

2. **A candidate's empty `revisions` table is a schema artifact, not an observation, so its emptiness licenses nothing.** [`VERIFIED`: source read.] `migrate_v7_to_v8` creates the table empty and can never backfill:

   [db.py#L871](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L871)
   ```py
    _FTS_PORTER_STATEMENTS). No backfill is possible: prior text was never
   ```
   (VERIFIED at d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c: source read.)

   For every other adopted table the worst case of replace-the-slug is re-sync cost (GitHub regenerates the data). `revisions` is the one asymmetric table: it exists precisely because GitHub no longer serves displaced text, so the delete is a one-way door.

3. **The adopter never chooses the candidate, and no surface discloses the hazard.** [`VERIFIED`: source read.] `doctor()` auto-selects the winner by greatest `issues_since` among complete candidates ([doctor.py#L14-L18](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L14-L18) — a criterion with no correlation to revision coverage); the CLI recommends the exact command as cleanup (`run: zaxbygraph doctor --consolidate ...`); `inspect()`'s report carries `items/garbled/complete/issues_since` but no revision counts ([doctor.py#L126-L132](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L126-L132)); and the user's intent ("clean up my scattered DBs") says nothing about destroying recorded history. (VERIFIED at d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c: source read of doctor.py and cli.py.)

4. **The docs imply preservation where deletion happens.** [`VERIFIED`: source read.]

   [schema_notes.py#L51](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c/src/zaxbygraph/schema_notes.py#L51)
   ```py
        "id": "v8. Sequence order for one item's displaced-text history; assigned at insert and never updated. doctor --consolidate is the one sanctioned rewrite (fresh ids, per-item order preserved)",
   ```
   (VERIFIED at d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c: source read.)

   Nothing in docs/schema.md's revisions section or schema_notes.py tells a reader that adopting a history-less candidate erases their history.

5. **The only pin test codifies the disputed semantics, and no test covers the empty case.** [`VERIFIED`: source read + reviewer-executed mutant (dropping `("revisions", "id")` from `_COPY_TABLES` passes the full 424-test suite).] [tests/test_revisions.py#L1081-L1082](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c/tests/test_revisions.py#L1081-L1082) asserts `STALE-OLD`/`STALE-NEW` rows for number 1 are deleted by a candidate that holds no history for number 1 — precisely the semantics this issue proposes to change. The assertion must be reworked in the same PR.

**Prior-art reconciliation.** Replace-the-slug adoption predates this issue (issue #1's doctor); PR #39 extended it to `revisions` and added the ordered copy. This issue does not revert that extension — it narrows it per item so the extension stops destroying evidence the candidate cannot re-derive. The related recorded boundary in docs/schema.md ("an absence first seen degraded leaves nothing for a later complete fetch to tombstone") covers evidence the store never held; this issue covers evidence the store does hold and consolidation deletes. (VERIFIED at d33cfbc20033ef82154fb494e804d29baf32ec9c: source read.)

**Product-decision framing (carried from the ASK).** The maintainer decision this issue settles is the default polarity: preserve-by-default (this issue's ACs) vs pure replace-the-slug. If pure replace is preferred, the defensible shape is an explicit opt-in (e.g. a `--replace-revisions` flag or a fail-closed refusal naming that flag) — never silent replacement; that variant is Out of scope here and the ACs would be re-cut on request.

## Scope

**In:** `consolidate()`'s revisions handling — a per-item guard inside the existing transaction (replace an item's revision history only when the candidate holds revision rows for that item; preserve the store's rows otherwise; fresh ids and `ORDER BY id` sequence preserved for adopted rows); a disclosure line in the doctor result payload (report preserved-vs-adopted revision counts); doc updates in docs/schema.md (revisions write-rules), schema_notes.py (`revisions.id`), and the `consolidate()` docstring.
**Out:** within-item history union/merging when the candidate has *shallower* history for an item it does cover (residual loss recorded as a named boundary in the docs update; priced extension later); store-vs-candidate freshness gating for adoption generally (separate finding — `consolidate()` compares candidates only, never the store); any new CLI flag; reverting the `revisions` adoption itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: WHEN `doctor --consolidate` adopts a candidate holding zero revision rows for the slug into a store holding revision rows for it, THE SYSTEM SHALL leave all stored revision rows for the slug in place.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_revisions.py" -k test_empty_candidate_keeps_stored_history -b
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_revisions.py
  - why: at base the adoption deletes the slug's revision rows unconditionally (doctor.py#L201-L203), so the new test cannot exist and pass until the guard lands.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN the candidate holds revision rows for some of the slug's items and none for others, THE SYSTEM SHALL replace only the revision history of items the candidate has rows for and preserve the rest.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_revisions.py" -k test_partial_candidate_replaces_only_observed_items -b
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_revisions.py
  - why: the same unconditional delete (doctor.py#L201-L203) removes preserved rows at base; an all-or-nothing guard would also fail this check (the cliff the per-item scope exists to close).
- [ ] AC3: WHEN a candidate's revision rows are adopted, THE SYSTEM SHALL assign them fresh ids in the candidate's per-item sequence order and SHALL NOT touch other repos' revision rows.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_revisions.py" -k test_consolidation_adopts_revisions_fresh_ids_in_order -b
  - expect: OK (green at base and head, after reworking the current assertion set for per-item scope — the number-1 "STALE" rows survive at head).
  - files: tests/test_revisions.py
  - why: regression floor for the adoption mechanics this issue narrows (fresh ids, `ORDER BY id` sequence, cross-repo isolation).
- [ ] AC4: WHEN consolidation retains stored revision rows the candidate had no history for, THE SYSTEM SHALL report the preserved count (and the adopted count) in the doctor result payload.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_doctor.py" -k test_adoption_reports_preserved_revision_counts -b
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_doctor.py, src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py
  - why: the doctor report envelope (doctor.py report assembly) carries no revision fields at base, so the disclosure surface cannot exist until the fix adds it.
- [ ] AC5: THE SYSTEM SHALL document, in docs/schema.md's revisions write-rules, schema_notes.py's `revisions.id` note, and the `consolidate()` docstring, that adoption preserves per-item revision history the candidate never observed and that within-item depth loss (a shallower candidate for an item it covers) remains a recorded boundary.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(DOCS_ONLY)
  - substitute evidence: the PR's doc diff, reviewed at review time, showing each of the three surfaces names both the per-item preservation and the within-item depth-loss boundary
  - files: docs/schema.md, src/zaxbygraph/schema_notes.py, src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py
  - why: prose; substitute evidence is the doc diff reviewed at PR time, showing each of the three surfaces names both the per-item preservation and the within-item depth-loss boundary.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN the same candidate is consolidated twice, THE SYSTEM SHALL write no new revision rows and delete none after the first adoption.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_revisions.py -k test_consolidation_twice_is_row_neutral -b
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check does not exist at base (it extends the consolidation test's fixture at head).
  - files: tests/test_revisions.py
  - why: floor against a broken guard or dedupe (delete+copy must stay idempotent once preservation lands).

## argv convention

Every executable AC uses `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p <file> -k <test> -b`. Its absence signature is `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5), which is CPython ≥ 3.13 behavior — base legs pin `py -3.14` (the box/repo convention established in #25's trace; 3.11/3.12 exit 0 on zero matches). AC3/AC6 are green at both ends and pin the preserved mechanics.

## Definition of done

PR head: 1095476168e7f91eb27c0dc22aa6725c79c0e39e

Closes #26
Closes #27

Bundled per the maintainer's authorization ("I authorize more than one issue per PR as long as the PR remains reviewable and manageable"): both issues are Workstream A schema-lane slots (A-05 → A-06), share their file set and registry/docs surfaces, and #27 declares `Depends on: #26`. #40 was evaluated and deliberately NOT bundled (different subsystem — doctor/consolidation — and a Priority-severity fix deserving its own PR).

## Summary

Migration v9 (issue #26) and v10 (issue #27) make the store record the references an item's text already carries and the links GitHub itself reports:

- **v9 text-derived references**: `item_path_refs` (raw path strings — Python frames, `path:L:C` tokens, same-repo `blob/` URLs, backticked segments — with `origin` and a backticked flag) and `item_signatures` (exception + masked error line + frame function) are extracted from bodies, comments and reviews, replaced on re-ingest, and **backfilled from stored `raw_json`** so an incremental corpus is covered without a resync. Paths stay RAW — resolution against the file vocabulary is read-time (#29's lane), so rows never depend on sync order.
- **`branch_ref`**: a PR whose `head_ref` carries exactly ONE numeric token naming one stored *issue* links to it. A single token can never become ambiguous later, so no retraction path exists; an insert-only reverse pass closes the either-ingests-first order.
- **Reference positions**: `mentions`/`closes_keyword` evidence now carries the location (`title`, or `body@<offset>`, `comment:<id>@<offset>`, `review:<id>@<offset>`) via a same-length foreign-reference mask so offsets index the original text. Edge identity (the 7-column key) is untouched.
- **v10 GitHub-reported links**: `blockedBy`, sub-issue `parent`, `duplicateOf` and `closedByPullRequestsReferences(includeClosedPrs:false)` become `source='link'` edges (`blocked_by`, `child_of`, `duplicate_of`, `linked_pr`), replaced **per connection** only when that connection was fetched complete, union-only on overflow, never retracted by a degraded re-ingest (the delete-owned exemption gains `'link'`).
- **Commit messages**: `pr_commits` rows (complete-gated) are the canonical source for commit-message `closes_keyword` edges — re-derived from the RETAINED rows on every ingest, so a REST or overflowed re-ingest never retracts them; evidence names the commit sha; the `closes` relation stays reserved for GitHub-reported closures.
- **`duplicate_keyword`**: "duplicate of #N" text yields the keyword stream, never GitHub's `duplicate_of`.
- **Reopen events**: `REOPENED_EVENT` rides the timeline selection into `item_events` rows, replaced only when the timeline section was fetched complete; a plain-REST sync (presence `None`) touches nothing.
- **Capability probe v3**: cache key bump (stale v2 maps cannot know the new fields) plus `IssueTimelineItemsItemType` enum introspection — a host lacking `REOPENED_EVENT` degrades by omission instead of failing every page query.
- Compatibility: `doctor --consolidate` copies all four new tables; the `item_bundle` sidecar and replay carry the new sections with presence semantics; docs/schema.md and schema notes cover every new relation and table.


### Considered, not filed

Post-publication swarm-pr-review (6 base lanes + 7 micro families; 25 verified findings — 23 FIXED in a9b1b98, 2 REJECTED by execution) plus the gate ladder. Dispositions for everything NOT fixed:

| Item | Reason | Gate test failed | Re-evaluate when |
|---|---|---|---|
| branch digit-run heuristic can still emit a semantically false `branch_ref` for version-like branch names (`release/2026-fix` → issue 2026 if stored) | letter-adjacent runs now rejected (python3-support, v2), but a delimiter-adjacent year/slug remains shape-valid; tightening further (e.g. requiring an issue-style prefix) is a product call on the AC4 wording | fails gate 2 partially (false fact stored, but the evidence string names the head_ref so a reader can judge) and gate 3 (low-frequency) | a mis-resolved branch_ref misleads a real query, or AC4's pattern wording is tightened |
| Reverse `branch_ref` pass visits every stored PR per issue ingest — O(PRs × issues) row visits per sync | one-time-per-item cost behind a partial index, scale test green, and the alternative (SQL LIKE prefilter) re-derives candidates worse | fails gate 3 (perf, not correctness) | the 8k-corpus scale budget regresses, or a corpus with >10k PRs syncs slowly |
| v9 backfill materializes all items/comments/reviews via fetchall | one-shot migration memory spike on very large stores; idempotent and atomic per MIGRATIONS step | fails gate 3 | a store large enough that the one-time spike is operationally real |
| New tables (`item_path_refs`, `item_signatures`, `item_events`, `pr_commits`) have no query/CLI read surface | read-time resolution and scoring are #29's lane by plan; ABSORB notice posted on #29 with the new-evidence comment | fails gate 4 (tracked in #29) | #29 ships |
| `_strip_foreign` (pre-existing, base-inherited) retains a quadratic worst case on slash-free word runs | pre-existing behavior this PR did not touch; the new hot paths use the linear `_mask_foreign` instead | fails gate 4 (pre-existing, outside the new code) | profiled evidence ties it to a real sync stall |
| `test_title_evidence_parity`'s dict-level assertion message reads "relations or destinations diverge" on an evidence divergence | cosmetic wording; the per-key TITLE-EVIDENCE-PARITY loop reports correctly when reached | fails gate 2/3 | next time that test module is edited |

## Root Cause

The store derived evidence from exactly two text channels (`mentions`/`closes_keyword`) and two timeline streams (`closed`/`cross_referenced`), while four mechanically-derivable reference families in the same payloads were extracted by nothing and the GitHub-reported link connections were not selected at all. A new stream carried as `source='payload'` would have been destroyed by the next degraded re-ingest (`delete_owned_edges` exempted only `timeline`/`closing_ref`).

## Fix

Two additive migrations in workstream slot order (v9 → v10), exactly as the reviewed plan (`docs/plans` program, issue bodies) specifies. See Summary. Necessity and sufficiency are pinned by the frozen acceptance checks: each of the 15 maps to one mechanism, all 15 run RED/absent → GREEN at the shipped head, and 12 named revert-mutants are proven killed.

## Recurrence Prevention (defect class)

- Defect class: derived evidence drifting across source ownership, transport capability, completeness, replay, migration, and consolidation.
- Sweep result: 14 predicate hits, all dispositioned FIX (relation registration ×6, child-table registration ×4, serialized-contract round trips ×4); 0 left open.
- Guardrail: the relation-registry census now DRIVES every emitter (a new relation cannot ship unregistered), plus a structural drift test asserting every `(repo, number)`-keyed table in sqlite_master appears in `doctor._COPY_TABLES`. Demonstrated bites: MUT10 (cross-owner deletion), MUT11 (census unregistration), MUT12 (consolidation drop) each turn their guard RED.

## Tests

- Frozen acceptance checks (authored at arm's length, amended pre-implementation under CHECK_WRONG with an anchor chain v1→v3): 15/15 PASS at the shipped head (12 NEW-SURFACE ERROR→GREEN, 1 DISCRIMINATING RED→GREEN, 3 PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN).
- Full suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → **472 tests OK** (424 at base + 48 new across the ladder and the post-publication review round).
- Mutation probes: `repro/mutation_probes.py` → **12/12 KILLED**, tree clean (probe scripts live in the git-excluded trace directory by design; reproducible from the checked-in tests they pin).
- Deferred-work scan → clean.
- CI: windows + ubuntu × 3.11/3.12 (this PR's runs).

## Regression Protection

- The three pinned actor-collapse contracts (`test_last_write_wins`, `test_two_comments_one_commented_edge`, `test_review_collapse_keeps_last_state`) stayed UNCHANGED and green — `collapse_edges` merges evidence on `closes_keyword` collisions only; MUT8 (widened merge) kills them.
- Fresh-vs-migrated parity tests pin the backfill to live-extraction behavior (keyword edges, evidence strings, branch targets) on item, comment and review channels.
- Test drift review: two `test_revisions.py` recorded-map tests updated for the widened `_resolve_children` tuple (index shifts only); the probe-cache key helper bumped to v3; the fresh-born version assertion now derives from `CURRENT_USER_VERSION`.

## External Checkpoint Anchor

- Receipt published before implementation (human-confirmed; local validation cannot attest publication/timing): `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=26-27-text-refs-and-link-stream manifest=faae56b98d6bb6869184b30769568965551753d9 semantics=4679317e873efb7b846f12b495328ddd76bf61b2 tree=b320548f6f5860df71e5f99725de27f3b4ff5f92`
- External artifact location: https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/26#issuecomment-6451405669 (chain v1: comment 6450445573; v2: 6451163828 — semantics digest constant across all three)
- Independent verification: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug 26-27-text-refs-and-link-stream --receipt '<published literal>'` -> PASS (re-verified by the implementation reviewer and the final critic)
- Local copy/provenance: `.agents/issue-traces/26-27-text-refs-and-link-stream/02-reproduction.md` (non-authoritative discovery copy)

## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence

| Acceptance criterion (from intake) | Evidence (command + output, or test name) |
|---|---|
| 26-AC1 path refs with origin + backticked flag | C1 GREEN (`repro/C1.head.log`); `test_path_refs_extracted` |
| 26-AC2 foreign blob URL dropped | C2 GREEN; MUT6 kill |
| 26-AC3 exception + masked error_line | C3 GREEN; MUT5 kill |
| 26-AC4 branch_ref single-match discipline | C4 GREEN; MUT4 (first-token) + MUT10 (cross-owner deletion) kills |
| 26-AC5 reference position in evidence | C5 RED→GREEN; exact-offset pin; MUT1/MUT2 kills; migration parity via `test_backfill_parity_with_live_extraction` + `test_title_evidence_parity` |
| 27-AC1 blocked_by replaced when complete | C6 GREEN (`test_blocked_by_replaced_when_complete`) |
| 27-AC2 degraded re-ingest never retracts; overflow union-only | C7 GREEN; MUT3 kill |
| 27-AC3 child_of/duplicate_of, repo-qualified | C8 GREEN |
| 27-AC4 open linked PRs recorded | C9 GREEN (rel pinned to `linked_pr`) |
| 27-AC5 commit-message closes_keyword, never closes | C10 GREEN; MUT9 kill |
| 27-AC6 duplicate_keyword stream | C11 GREEN |
| 27-AC7 reopen events in item_events | C12 GREEN; MUT7 kill; `ReplayTimelinePresenceTests` |
| 26-AC6 + 27-AC8 registry classifies every relation | C13 GREEN; census drives every emitter; MUT11 kill |
| 26-AC7 + 27-AC8 docs table lists every relation | C14 GREEN (`docs/schema.md` relationships rows) |
| 27-AC9 closes collapse untouched | C15 GREEN; MUT8 kill |

## Invariant Audit

Against AGENTS.md (each verified at HEAD):

- Every edge `confidence='EXTRACTED'`: untouched — all new edges insert with `'EXTRACTED'`.
- Node types unchanged (actor/item/label/file/commit): all new edges are item→item; `branch_ref`/`blocked_by`/`child_of`/`duplicate_of`/`linked_pr`/`duplicate_keyword` endpoints are item numbers or repo-qualified ids (C8).
- Evidence is a payload, never part of identity: the 7-column key untouched (C5 pins one source-unfiltered row per pair); `closes` merge exception untouched (C15).
- `closes` reserved for GitHub-reported links, `closes_keyword` keyword-derived: commit messages emit `closes_keyword` with commit provenance, never `closes` (C10); AGENTS.md's delete-owned bullet updated to name the `link` stream and its per-connection replace-when-complete semantics.
- `closes_keyword`/`mentions` mutual exclusion within a payload: preserved live AND in the v9 backfill (round-1/2 review fixes + parity tests).
- Cross-repo keyword references dropped, never localized: same-length mask shared by every position-aware stream (C2, MUT6).
- Item-scoped children replaced on re-ingest: `item_path_refs`/`item_signatures` replace unconditionally; `item_events`/`pr_commits` are the documented completeness-gated exception (AGENTS.md note added).
- Watermark/ingest idempotence/one-transaction-per-item: untouched — all new writes run inside `ingest_item`'s caller-owned transaction; PKs make duplicate pagination idempotent.
- Read-only `sql` escape hatch: untouched.

## Risk and Rollback

- Risk level: medium (two additive migrations + a backfill pass over stored `raw_json`; scale test stays green).
- Rollback: revert the commit; forward-only migrations are additive and old binaries already refuse newer stores with the existing error.
- Residual risk: a pre-v9 branch_ref whose PR ingested before its target heals at the issue's ingest (reverse pass) or the PR's next re-ingest; GitHub-reported connections are not backfilled (never fetched pre-v10 — disclosed, plan-authorized).

## Gate ladder

- Plan critic (swarm-plan-critic Kimi K3.1 Pro): rounds 1–3 NEEDS_REVISION (15 + 6 + 1 required revisions, all applied; the round-3 BLOCKED item was resolved by the critic's own specified remedy and confirmed in a disclosed round 4), round 4 **APPROVE**.
- Implementation review (swarm-reviewer): rounds 1–4 NEEDS_REVISION (3 + 1 + 1 + 1 findings — backfill live-parity, replay timeline presence, kind filter, title evidence prefixes, duplicate-loop pin — every fix mutation-verified to bite by the reviewer), round 5 **APPROVE**.
- Final critic (swarm-critic): round 1 NEEDS_REVISION (backfill comment/review evidence prefixes, closes-collision merge, AGENTS.md link-stream bullet — all fixed with tests that kill the critic's own revert-mutants), round 2 **APPROVE**.
- Full sweep: `trace-check.sh` phases 0–4.6 → **0 FAILs**. Trace: `.agents/issue-traces/26-27-text-refs-and-link-stream/`.

## Waivers (or none)

None. The two scope-outs (issue #29 read-time path resolution; status-coverage markers dropped) were plan-authorized design decisions recorded in the approved plan, not deferrals.

New data is backfilled from stored `raw_json` so an existing corpus is covered without a resync, and a capability-probe bump (v3 + timeline-enum introspection) keeps hosts lacking the new fields degrading gracefully. **Changes:** - v9: new `item_path_refs`/`item_signatures` tables, `branch_ref` edges, and position-aware (`body@`/`title`) evidence for `mentions`/`closes_keyword`, plus a raw_json backfill kept in parity with live extraction. - v10: GitHub-reported `source='link'` edges (per-connection complete-gated replace, union-on-overflow, never retracted by a degraded re-ingest), commit-message `closes_keyword` re-derived from retained `pr_commits`, `duplicate_keyword` text stream, and `item_events` reopen rows. - Plumbing: `sync._resolve_children` expanded to carry links/pr_commits with presence semantics, `doctor` consolidation + replay sidecar updated, and docs/`AGENTS.md`/schema notes revised. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | src/​zaxbygraph/​extract.py | New path/signature/branch/link/commit extractors, position-aware masking, `collapse_edges` closes_keyword merge | | src/​zaxbygraph/​store.py | `write_text_refs`/`write_item_events`/`insert_pr_commits`/`rebuild_links`, `link` delete-owned exemption, reverse branch pass | | src/​zaxbygraph/​sync.py | `_resolve_children` carries links/pr_commits + completeness, probe cache key v3, capability serialization | | src/​zaxbygraph/​graphql.py | Link/commit selections, timeline enum introspection + degradation, commit-message composition | | src/​zaxbygraph/​db.py | `migrate_v8_to_v9` backfill, `migrate_v9_to_v10`, version pins to 10 | | src/​zaxbygraph/​schema.sql /​ schema_notes.py | New tables, head-ref partial index, column notes | | src/​zaxbygraph/​doctor.py /​ query.py | Consolidation copy tables + structural relations for new edges | | docs/​schema.md /​ AGENTS.md | Relation/table docs and link-stream invariant updates | | tests/​* | New acceptance + supporting checks; registry/migration/replay/probe-key updates | **Findings:** I raised one `bug` (missing `n != number` self-reference guard for `duplicate_keyword`, inconsistent with `mentions`/`closes_keyword` and the self-suppressing `duplicate_of` link stream; recurs in `edges_from_comment`, `edges_from_review`, and the `db.py` backfill) and one `maintainability` issue (unused `_foreign_text_positions` helper). The link/commit completeness gating, presence-vs-absence handling, GraphQL brace balance, and backfill/live parity otherwise looked internally consistent.
Review effort: Balanced

**1 existing issue remains and 5 new issues found across 11 files (changes from recent commits).**
Prompt for AI agents (unresolved issues) ```text Check if these issues are valid — if so, understand the root cause of each and fix them. When an issue isn't valid or won't be fixed in this PR, reply in its thread with the reason and then resolve the thread. If appropriate, use sub-agents to investigate and fix each issue separately. P3: `text[end + 1 :].isdigit()` checks the whole tail of the text, so the `#N` suffix of a foreign URL is only masked when nothing but digits follows it. Match the digit run after the '#' instead. P2: Each foreign span rebuilds the entire string, making masking O(text length × span count) for bodies with many cross-repo links. Emit the masked slices in one pass to keep extraction linear. P3: This row now includes title and commit-message sources, but the 'What closes_keyword … do and do not mean' paragraph still lists only bodies, comments, and review bodies. Update that paragraph to match so the two sections agree. P2: The `timeline` source note now claims reopened events are edge provenance, but reopened events are stored only in `item_events` and never become edges. Drop "/reopened" here to match `docs/schema.md` and the `item_events` note. P3: This branch treats tuple, set, and frozenset markers as the legacy all-connections boolean, so it logs complete connections as overflowed. Recognize the same container types as `_connection_complete`. ```
