item.body:
*Provenance: generated from the post-publication review closeout of PR #43 (swarm-pr-review run pr43-20261028 — three cubic runs and 32 resolved threads — plus the maintainer-directed swarm-critic input on the four ASK items, 2026-10-29). Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main at anchor commit ba3ce0cf77595b60bf0660e8fac58481fb8dc6c5 (PR #43's squash merge — its tree is identical to the reviewed head a5da4da for every cited file) on 2026-10-29 by source read and grep at that commit. One issue = one PR. Probe evidence cited from the review lives partly in out-of-repo artifacts (the issue-tracer trace at `.agents/issue-traces/29-derived-read-tier/` and the review packet at `.zcode/pr-review/pr43-20261028/`, git-excluded, not in this repository) and is quoted inline where load-bearing. Background: #29, #43. All four items are ASK approvals under CONTRIBUTING.md's follow-up covenant: executed-probe or source-trace verified, consequential, maintainer-approved this session, unfixable in the merged PR.*

## Summary

After this PR, a target's scored path evidence in `eval similar` and `eval bundle` can only come from the store as it existed at the target's creation — the vocabulary scoped to PRs merged at or before the item cutoff and references filtered by their origin timestamps, completing the leakage-control set the approved plan pinned for every eval mode (today implemented only in `eval localize`); the `hub_share` down-weighting knob fires on majority-touched paths (today it is arithmetically incapable of firing on any repo where merged PRs are fewer than half the items); `export-corpus` no longer leaks a corpus-text spool file into the temp directory when the manifest temp file cannot be created; and the README states `similar`'s measured cost characteristic so agents scale-test before trusting it on large repos.

## Problem (claims to verify)

1. **Claim 1 — VERIFIED (source trace at the anchor commit; leak probed live by the PR #43 round-2 gate):** `eval similar` and `eval bundle` resolve stored path references against the FULL merged-PR vocabulary with no creation-time scoping. The vocabulary query in `build_context` filters only merge state — [src/zaxbygraph/derive.py#L334-L337](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/ba3ce0cf77595b60bf0660e8fac58481fb8dc6c5/src/zaxbygraph/derive.py#L334-L337):

   ```py
               "SELECT pf.number, pf.path FROM pr_files pf"
               " JOIN items i ON i.repo = pf.repo AND i.number = pf.number"
               " WHERE pf.repo = ? AND i.merged_at IS NOT NULL"
               " AND (pf.status IS NULL OR pf.status != 'removed')",
   ```

   while the eval call sites pass no cutoff of any kind — [src/zaxbygraph/evaluate.py#L283-L288](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/ba3ce0cf77595b60bf0660e8fac58481fb8dc6c5/src/zaxbygraph/evaluate.py#L283-L288) (and the bundle twin at [L527](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/ba3ce0cf77595b60bf0660e8fac58481fb8dc6c5/src/zaxbygraph/evaluate.py#L527)):

   ```py
               out = derive_similar(
                   conn,
                   repo,
                   target,
                   limit=None,
                   weights=weights,
   ```

   The localize mode implements the plan's control via origin-timestamp joins (`localize_files`, derive.py:980-996 at the anchor); similar/bundle do not. Prior-art reconciliation: the PR #43 round-2 gate found the README claim had been silently narrowed to "in the localize mode" and reconciled the docs — this issue is the fix half of that reconciliation, not a re-litigation. Executed evidence (round-2 critic probe, quoted from the review ledger): on the synthetic fixture the post-fix comment bait `docs/leak.md` resolves into item 101's scored path set only because post-cutoff PR 130 puts it in the full vocabulary; on the real corpus 172 of 820 references, 74 vocabulary entries and 45 adjacency edges would be cut at the comment cutoff. Both pinned eval metrics are currently bit-identical with and without the leak — by corpus luck; a future re-recording could silently inflate the very numbers that certify the scorer.

2. **Claim 2 — VERIFIED (source trace; firing path probed on both corpora):** the hub down-weighting knob is arithmetically incapable of firing. The share divides merged-PR touch counts by ALL repo items — [src/zaxbygraph/derive.py#L418-L420](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/ba3ce0cf77595b60bf0660e8fac58481fb8dc6c5/src/zaxbygraph/derive.py#L418-L420):

   ```py
       hub = {
           p: len(nums) / max(1, len(items)) for p, nums in vocab_files.items()
       }
   ```

   consumed by `_file_weight` at [src/zaxbygraph/derive.py#L442-L446](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/ba3ce0cf77595b60bf0660e8fac58481fb8dc6c5/src/zaxbygraph/derive.py#L442-L446):

   ```py
   def _file_weight(path: str, ctx: dict, weights: dict) -> float:
       share = ctx["hub_share_of_items"].get(path, 0.0)
       if share and share >= weights["hub_share"]:
           return weights["hub_floor"]
       return 1.0
   ```

   `nums` are merged-PR numbers (the L336 query filters `merged_at IS NOT NULL`) while `items` is every repo item, so the maximum reachable share is `n_merged_prs / n_items` — below the 0.5 default trigger whenever merged PRs are fewer than half of all items (real corpus: 16/42 = 0.38). Measured: the most-touched real path sits in 11 of 16 merged PRs (0.69 of the PR population) yet scores 0.26 and is never down-weighted; no test references `_file_weight` or `hub_share_of_items` anywhere in the suite at the anchor (the knob ships with no firing-path coverage). The critic's read-only probe (monkeypatched denominator) showed 10 paths firing and 24 of 39 candidates' scores changing for a real target — while all six pinned eval metrics stay bit-identical, so the floors hold without re-certification. Prior art: the plan's own wording ("IDF over items", `.agents/issue-traces/29-derived-read-tier/07-approved-plan.md:114`, git-excluded) is the source of the mismatch; the fix pairs with a plan amendment.

3. **Claim 3 — VERIFIED (executed ENOSPC-shaped probe):** `write_corpus` leaks the corpus spool when the manifest temp file cannot be created. Both allocations precede the `try:` whose `finally` owns cleanup — [src/zaxbygraph/export.py#L583-L587](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/ba3ce0cf77595b60bf0660e8fac58481fb8dc6c5/src/zaxbygraph/export.py#L583-L587):

   ```py
       fd, spool_path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="zaxbygraph-export-")
       os.close(fd)
       fd, manifest_path = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix="zaxbygraph-export-manifest-")
       os.close(fd)
       try:
   ```

   A failure of the second `mkstemp` (ENOSPC/EACCES) abandons the first spool — probed: a corpus-text spool survives in the temp directory. Pre-existing verbatim at the PR #28 merge (3d3aab0), so it is genuinely outside PR #43's introduced hunks (PR #43 touched export.py only additively). Bounded severity (user-scoped temp dir, error-path leak, no fail-open), which is why it rode the ASK tier rather than Priority.

4. **Claim 4 — VERIFIED (executed timing probe, 2026-10-29):** `similar` scores every candidate pair with no cap — ~0.93 s for one `similar(limit=None)` call at 4,000 items (~2.3 s extrapolated at 10k), and `run_eval` iterates only ground-truth targets, so eval cost scales with targets × items, not items². The maintainer-approved disposition is the critic's "accept the design as-is" plus one README cost note ([README.md#L140](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/ba3ce0cf77595b60bf0660e8fac58481fb8dc6c5/README.md#L140), the `### Derived reads` section) so agents do not extrapolate the small-repo experience to 10k-item repos.

## Scope

**In:** eval-only creation-time scoping of the scored path vocabulary and reference origins in the `similar`/`bundle` eval modes (direct `similar`/`explain` reads stay current-state — the derived tier by definition reads the store as it is today); the hub denominator moved to the merged-PR population, with the out-of-repo plan wording amended; the export spool-leak fix with a leak regression test; the README cost note.
**Out:** directional confidence in the `coupling` command (deliberate — it ranks one path's associations, not an item-pair affinity; adjudication of record in PR #43); changing `DEFAULT_HUB_SHARE`/`DEFAULT_HUB_FLOOR` values; capping or pre-filtering `similar`'s candidate scan (explicitly rejected: if scale ever hurts, the semantics-preserving optimization is context reuse across eval targets, not a cap); MCP surfacing of the derived tier (#32); `triage`/`bundle`/`brief` commands (#30).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: WHEN `eval similar` or `eval bundle` score a target, THE SYSTEM SHALL build the scored path vocabulary only from PRs merged at or before the target's creation and resolve references only from origins whose timestamps precede the applicable comment cutoff, so a reference resolvable only through a post-cutoff PR can never enter the scored path set.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_followup_43.py -q -k test_eval_scopes_path_evidence_to_the_item_cutoff
  - expect: ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_followup_43.py
  - files: tests/test_followup_43.py, src/zaxbygraph/derive.py, src/zaxbygraph/evaluate.py
  - why: the cutoff-scoped scoring surface does not exist at base; the discriminator (the `docs/leak.md` bait entering item 101's scored set through post-cutoff PR 130) is probed evidence of record from the PR #43 round-2 gate.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN a path is touched by at least `hub_share` of the merged-PR population, THE SYSTEM SHALL down-weight its file evidence to `hub_floor` — reachable for the first time once the share denominator is the merged-PR population instead of all repo items.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_followup_43.py -q -k test_hub_share_fires_on_majority_paths
  - expect: ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_followup_43.py
  - files: src/zaxbygraph/derive.py, tests/test_followup_43.py
  - why: at base the knob cannot fire on any repo where merged PRs are fewer than half the items (max reachable share 16/42 = 0.38 < 0.5); the fix's geometry is probed to leave all six pinned eval metrics bit-identical, so the floors hold without re-certification.
- [ ] AC3: IF the manifest temp-file creation fails after the corpus spool exists, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL remove the spool file from the temp directory (no `zaxbygraph-export-*` orphan survives).
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_followup_43.py -q -k test_spool_removed_when_manifest_tempfile_fails
  - expect: ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_followup_43.py
  - files: src/zaxbygraph/export.py, tests/test_followup_43.py
  - why: the check cannot exist at base; the defect it pins is probed evidence of record — a monkeypatched failing second mkstemp leaves a `zaxbygraph-export-*` spool in the temp dir (ENOSPC-shaped probe, 2026-10-29), pre-existing verbatim at 3d3aab0.
- [ ] AC4: THE SYSTEM SHALL document `similar`'s scale characteristic (measured ~0.93 s at 4,000 items, ~2.3 s extrapolated at 10k; eval scaling with targets × items) in the README derived-reads section.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(DOCS_ONLY)
  - substitute evidence (review artifact): the README diff adding the cost sentence to the derived-reads section
  - substitute evidence (verification): the merged PR's diff view showing the sentence
  - files: README.md
  - why: docs-only; the measured numbers are probed evidence of record from the maintainer-directed critic input (2026-10-29).

## Design

1. **Eval scoping (AC1):** thread eval-only `item_cutoff`/`comment_cutoff` params through `build_context` and the `_eval_similar`/`_eval_bundle` call sites, following the existing `exclude_adjacency`/`filtered_sources`/`suppress_signals` knob pattern; scope the vocabulary query with `AND i.merged_at <= ?` (ISO stamps are string-comparable) and filter per-ref origins via the existing `origin_timestamp` joins; direct CLI reads pass no cutoff and behave byte-identically to today. Extend the bait-isolation shape of `test_eval_leakage_controls`: the `docs/leak.md` bait must stop entering item 101's scored path set. Decide and document the fallback for similar-mode targets with no fix PR (no comment cutoff derivable) — the one genuine plan-amendment decision this PR must make.
2. **Hub denominator (AC2):** divide by the merged-PR population count in `build_context` (keep `hub_share`/`hub_floor` config keys; rename `hub_share_of_items` — e.g. `hub_share_of_population` — in the same PR); amend the out-of-repo plan's "IDF over items" sentence to "share of merged PRs touching the path"; add the firing-path regression test; record the floors-bit-identical probe result in the PR's trace.
3. **Spool leak (AC3):** open the `try:` before the second `mkstemp` (or unlink the spool if the second allocation raises); the regression test monkeypatches the second `tempfile.mkstemp` to raise and asserts no `zaxbygraph-export-*` file survives.
4. **README note (AC4):** one sentence in the derived-reads section with the measured numbers and their shape (linear per call at fixed repo size; eval scales with targets × items).
5. One follow-up PR lands all four; the eval-scoping change is reviewed separately from the mechanical items 2–4 within that PR.

## Files to change

`src/zaxbygraph/derive.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/evaluate.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/export.py`, `README.md`, new `tests/test_followup_43.py` (self-contained: it bootstraps its own `sys.path` so bare `python -m pytest` works from the repo root — the fixture-importing modules need the tests dir on the path, which bare pytest does not provide; disclosed in the file's docstring).

## Local verification recipe

```
python -m pytest tests/test_followup_43.py -q
PYTHONPATH="src;tests" python -m unittest discover -s tests -b
```

item.body:
Closes #30
Closes #44

## Summary

Implements issue #30 (Workstream B-03) with **#44 bundled** (maintainer-authorized in-session, 2026-10-29: "I authorize more than one issue per PR as long as the PR remains reviewable and manageable") — #44's four fixes share the derived-read-tier domain (derive.py/evaluate.py/README) with #30's work.

**#30 — derived work-selection tier** (`triage`, `bundle`, `brief`):
- `triage` ranks open issues by a documented two-stage formula over echoed weights (`[triage]` TOML; group = weight × mean of present normalized features; missing data = `null` + `requires`, excluded from the mean; milestone/hotspot anchored on the echoed store stamp `triage_asof`). Gates (`blocked`/`assigned`/`linked_pr` with the append-only stale label/`locked`) exclude rows by default with `ranked: false`; `--include-gated` returns them. Stage 2 (top-K ungated) adds hotspot + analog-based regression and the `stage2_weight × (hotspot+regression)/2` bonus. Order: total DESC, number ASC. Payloads echo `weights` + `config_source` + `formula_version` ("triage.v1").
- `bundle` proposes 2-3-issue bundles for one agent: pool = top-K ungated minus `--exclude`; exact affinity pipeline (`pair_components` → `_apply_cochange` → `_total_score`; coupling index built once); edge iff affinity ≥ `affinity_floor` (raw scale, default 3.0) **and** an anchor signal fired (signature/files_direct/structural/cochange); title-overlap ≥ 0.9 without anchors → `merge_candidates` (never co-bundled); anchor-less text pairs → `related_not_bundleable`; cross-bundle file disjointness unless `--allow-shared-files`; open-PR collisions flagged with prefer-collision-free tie-break; stable `bundle_id` = sha1("zaxbygraph.bundle.v1|members|config_hash") with formula_version folded into the hash; `--budget-tokens` caps the whole payload with `truncated`.
- `brief N` returns a token-budgeted work packet: features, body truncated at paragraph boundaries, top-5 comments (maintainer-first, recency), implicated files with evidence, closest analog + diffstat, linked PRs; **every GitHub-authored string wrapped as `{"untrusted_text": ...}`** with `content_trust`; `--live` reads CI state (PR record `head.sha` → combined status) + reviews through `gh` (argv-list, 30s timeout, 256 KiB cap, never stored) and rides inside the budget; invalid flags return the coded `bad_request` envelope.
- `open` gains `--limit/--offset/--kind/--label` + labels/assignees/linked_open_prs (offset works without limit); `churn` gains `--merged-only`.
- Skill gains the status → sync → triage → bundle → brief → verify recipe ("candidates, not facts"); README gains the triage/bundle/brief section + `similar` scale note; docs/schema.md enumerates all seven derived reads.

**#44 — follow-up fixes from PR #43's closeout** (each probe-verified in the issue):
1. `eval similar`/`eval bundle` scope scored path evidence to the target's creation — vocabulary (`merged_at <= item_cutoff`), per-item reference-origin filtering (target AND candidates), and the cochange population; no-closer fallback = `target.created_at` (documented decision). Direct reads otherwise byte-identical — item 2's hub-denominator change does shift `files_direct` scores on stores with unmerged items (README's `similar` row says so).
2. Hub share denominator = the merged-PR population (incl. zero-file PRs); `hub_share_of_items` → `hub_share_of_population`.
3. `export-corpus` no longer leaks the spool when the manifest tempfile fails.
4. README documents `similar`'s scale (~0.93 s measured @ 4k items; ~2.3 s @ 10k is an extrapolation, not a measurement; eval scales with targets × items).

**AC9 (defaults)**: recorded on issue 30 before closure per the issue's gate (comment 6510715064, 2026-10-29) — maintainer-directed, calibrated by a swarm-critic measurement pass over five real stores (227 open issues): reactions /3, participants /3, comments /5, mentions /10; affinity_floor 3.0 (raw [0,18] scale); stage2_weight 0.25; priority maps clamp [0,1] (absent table = missing feature); `fnmatch.fnmatchcase` + `["tests/*"]`; `formula_version` echo folded into `bundle_id`.

## Process (issue-tracer v3, full-resolution contract)

- 21 executable acceptance checks (C1-C8, C10-C22) authored arm's-length, frozen at a red checkpoint under anchor **v9** (published on issue 30: comments 6509767152 → 6517638693; semantics 6db7b4eb…), every one RED/ERROR at base ba3ce0c and **21/21 PASS** at the shipped head; 2 NON-EXECUTABLE rows (AC9/AC13) with live-verified substitute evidence.
- Named-mutant probes all executed RED→restore: stage2 /2 (C1), churn merged filter (C7), coupling-index cutoff (C17 — found by the Phase-4 probe, closed by a CHECK_WRONG amendment), pool validation outside the try (C19), bundles-only shrink (C20), brief flag-reservation + serialized-unit cap (C21, both legs), live keep-fields + head-source (C16/C22).
- Gates: plan-critic 4 rounds (r4 APPROVE); implementation reviewer 5 rounds (r1 NEEDS_REVISION: 9 findings incl. a falsified single-paragraph budget and a FALSE scan-deferred record — corrected in-file; r2: 2 residuals; r3 APPROVE; r4/r5 re-gates re-certified after the final-critic fixes, incl. a LIVE-API probe that killed a dead CI leg a fabricated fixture had masked); final critic 2 rounds (r1 NEEDS_REVISION: dead live-CI leg + missing brief echo + false universal claims; r2 certified the code and its one artifact-text finding was remediated verbatim).
- **Post-publication review (swarm-pr-review pr45-20261030 + cubic ×3 + Copilot)**: 8 lanes + the mandatory 11-risk-family micro-ledger produced 109 candidates → 18 clusters → 2 execution-first reviewer shards (live-store and in-memory probes; 2 claims REJECTED by executed evidence — the reactions "+1" key is real, and the WAL never-write test can fail) → critic challenge (8 survive / 11 downgraded / 1 reject). All surviving findings fixed in a2dd25d + 7231127 + d91e669 + 441e4af + 838a412; every cubic thread (17 + 4 + 1) and Copilot thread replied and resolved.
- Suite **589 OK** (549 baseline + 11 + 10 frozen + 19 review-round pins) at **PR head 838a4125614420451f6173492a52a52a85ad62c1**; 21/21 frozen checks PASS (anchor v10, semantics 6db7b4eb unchanged across v9→v10); scan-deferred clean; trace phases 0-4.6 exit 0.

## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence

Per-AC evidence map lives in the trace (`.agents/issue-traces/30-triage-bundle-brief/09-final-critic.md` `## Acceptance criteria evidence`, git-excluded): AC1→C1, AC2→C2, AC3→C3, AC4→C4, AC5→C5, AC6→C6/C21/C22, AC7→C7/C14, AC8→C8, AC9 → issue comment 6510715064, AC10→C10/C17/C18, AC11→C11, AC12→C12, AC13 → README diff, AC14→C13, AC15→C14, AC16→C15, AC17→C16, AC18→C17, AC19→C18, AC20→C19, AC21→C20, AC22→C21, AC23→C22 — each executable AC backed by a frozen check PASS at the shipped head plus executed revert-probes.

## Considered, not filed (RECORD ledger)

| # | item | disposition | re-evaluation trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `coupling` deliberately reads current state (merged-PR evidence unscoped) | pre-existing design, adjudicated of record in PR #43 | if coupling ever feeds eval scoring |
| 2 | brief budgets below the per-packet skeleton floor (~470-650 tokens bare-issue, title-dependent) return the skeleton with `truncated: true` | documented honestly in README/docstring; quality-of-service, no correctness consequence | budget semantics change |
| 3 | `--live` reviews leg reads gh's first page (~30) with no completeness claim, and no shipped docs cap clause (the contexts 10-cap is code-docstring-only) | disclosed here; one docs clause would close it in a docs pass | brief --live grows pagination |

Closes #30

## Summary

Implements issue #30 (Workstream B-03) with **#44 bundled** (maintainer-authorized in-session, 2026-10-29: "I authorize more than one issue per PR as long as the PR remains reviewable and manageable") — #44's four fixes share the derived-read-tier domain (derive.py/evaluate.py/README) with #30's work.

**#30 — derived work-selection tier** (`triage`, `bundle`, `brief`):
- `triage` ranks open issues by a documented two-stage formula over echoed weights (`[triage]` TOML; group = weight × mean of present normalized features; missing data = `null` + `requires`, excluded from the mean; milestone/hotspot anchored on the echoed store stamp `triage_asof`). Gates (`blocked`/`assigned`/`linked_pr` with the append-only stale label/`locked`) exclude rows by default with `ranked: false`; `--include-gated` returns them. Stage 2 (top-K ungated) adds hotspot + analog-based regression and the `stage2_weight × (hotspot+regression)/2` bonus. Order: total DESC, number ASC. Payloads echo `weights` + `config_source` + `formula_version` ("triage.v1").
- `bundle` proposes 2-3-issue bundles for one agent: pool = top-K ungated minus `--exclude`; exact affinity pipeline (`pair_components` → `_apply_cochange` → `_total_score`; coupling index built once); edge iff affinity ≥ `affinity_floor` (raw scale, default 3.0) **and** an anchor signal fired (signature/files_direct/structural/cochange); title-overlap ≥ 0.9 without anchors → `merge_candidates` (never co-bundled); anchor-less text pairs → `related_not_bundleable`; cross-bundle file disjointness unless `--allow-shared-files`; open-PR collisions flagged with prefer-collision-free tie-break; stable `bundle_id` = sha1("zaxbygraph.bundle.v1|members|config_hash") with formula_version folded into the hash; `--budget-tokens` caps the whole payload with `truncated`.
- `brief N` returns a token-budgeted work packet: features, body truncated at paragraph boundaries, top-5 comments (maintainer-first, recency), implicated files with evidence, closest analog + diffstat, linked PRs; **every GitHub-authored string wrapped as `{"untrusted_text": ...}`** with `content_trust`; `--live` reads CI state (PR record `head.sha` → combined status) + reviews through `gh` (argv-list, 30s timeout, 256 KiB cap, never stored) and rides inside the budget; invalid flags return the coded `bad_request` envelope.
- `open` gains `--limit/--offset/--kind/--label` + labels/assignees/linked_open_prs (offset works without limit); `churn` gains `--merged-only`.
- Skill gains the status → sync → triage → bundle → brief → verify recipe ("candidates, not facts"); README gains the triage/bundle/brief section + `similar` scale note; docs/schema.md enumerates all seven derived reads.

**#44 — follow-up fixes from PR #43's closeout** (each probe-verified in the issue):

Direct reads otherwise byte-identical — item 2's hub-denominator change does shift `files_direct` scores on stores with unmerged items (README's `similar` row says so).
2. Hub share denominator = the merged-PR population (incl. zero-file PRs); `hub_share_of_items` → `hub_share_of_population`.
3. `export-corpus` no longer leaks the spool when the manifest tempfile fails.
4. README documents `similar`'s scale (~0.93 s measured @ 4k items; ~2.3 s @ 10k is an extrapolation, not a measurement; eval scales with targets × items).

**AC9 (defaults)**: recorded on issue 30 before closure per the issue's gate (comment 6510715064, 2026-10-29) — maintainer-directed, calibrated by a swarm-critic measurement pass over five real stores (227 open issues): reactions /3, participants /3, comments /5, mentions /10; affinity_floor 3.0 (raw [0,18] scale); stage2_weight 0.25; priority maps clamp [0,1] (absent table = missing feature); `fnmatch.fnmatchcase` + `["tests/*"]`; `formula_version` echo folded into `bundle_id`.

- 21 executable acceptance checks (C1-C8, C10-C22) authored arm's-length, frozen at a red checkpoint under anchor **v9** (published on issue 30: comments 6509767152 → 6517638693; semantics 6db7b4eb…), every one RED/ERROR at base ba3ce0c and **21/21 PASS** at the shipped head; 2 NON-EXECUTABLE rows (AC9/AC13) with live-verified substitute evidence.

item.body:
*Provenance: follow-up from the post-publication review of PR #45 (issues #30 + #44), generated per the maintainer's follow-up rule after swarm-critic adjudication (2026-10-30; critic verdict travels with each item). Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main at anchor commit df98847e2d2ee9ef7e7756ace7c8e17a5ee5ee07 (PR #45's squash merge) on 2026-10-30 by source read and executed probes — three of them run live by the critic (phantom-failure probe, silent-reweight probe, drained-skeleton measurement). One issue = one PR. The PR-body review record and ledger live at https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/pull/45 (in-repo); the review packet `.zcode/pr-review/pr45-20261030/` and trace `.agents/issue-traces/30-triage-bundle-brief/` are git-excluded and not in this repository. Background: #30, #44, #45.*

## Summary

After this PR, the `[triage]`/`[derive]` config chain (store `config.toml` → cwd `.zaxbygraph.toml` → `--config`) is covered by tests at every level it resolves, the derived-tier acceptance checks are hermetic against an ambient project config, the bundle budget-cap guarantee has a working pin, and the config docs state the ambient-config trust boundary — closing the four items the PR #45 review adjudicated as file-grade.

## Problem (claims to verify)

1. **Claim 1 — VERIFIED (grep at the anchor): the config chain is load-bearing and wholly untested below `--config`.** F5 (PR #45) threaded `[derive]` affinity weights through `triage`/`bundle`/`brief` and folded them into `bundle_id`; the chain resolver is [_triage_config_chain](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/df98847e2d2ee9ef7e7756ace7c8e17a5ee5ee07/src/zaxbygraph/derive.py#L1414-L1416):

```py
    connection: ``<store>/config.toml`` (via PRAGMA database_list — the
    derived functions never receive the db path), ``.zaxbygraph.toml`` in
    the cwd, then the explicit ``--config`` path."""
```

and [_resolve_weight_config](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/df98847e2d2ee9ef7e7756ace7c8e17a5ee5ee07/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L851-L854):

```py
    then ``<store>/config.toml``, then ``.zaxbygraph.toml`` (cwd), then an
    explicit ``--config`` path (highest). Returns the paths that exist."""
    store_cfg: str | None = None
    if db_path is not None:
```

Grep over `tests/` finds zero references to `config.toml` or `.zaxbygraph.toml`; `--config` appears once in `test_triage_paging.py` and twice in `test_triage_bundle.py` (explicit level only). Executed critic probe: store→cwd→explicit merge is per-key (an explicit file's deliberately-unset keys silently inherit ambient values) and `config_source` reports only the last supplier.

2. **Claim 2 — VERIFIED (executed probes, live by the critic): the acceptance suite is not hermetic against an ambient project config.** The CLI test legs run with `cwd=str(REPO_ROOT)` ([test_triage_bundle.py:199](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/df98847e2d2ee9ef7e7756ace7c8e17a5ee5ee07/tests/test_triage_bundle.py#L199), [test_triage_bundle_supp.py:148](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/df98847e2d2ee9ef7e7756ace7c8e17a5ee5ee07/tests/test_triage_bundle_supp.py#L148)) while the chain reads `Path(".zaxbygraph.toml")` from the cwd. Probe 1: planting a repo-root `.zaxbygraph.toml` with `[triage] stage2_weight = 0.9` makes frozen check C1 fail with a phantom `AssertionError: 0.9 != 0.25` (tests/test_triage_bundle.py:431) — a misattributed regression. Probe 2: `[triage] demand = 2.0` leaves C20 green under the reweight — silent. Probe 3: ambient keys leak into even `--config` runs while `config_source` echoes "explicit". A maintainer dogfooding zaxbygraph in this repo creates exactly this documented file; the consequence is acceptance-gate corruption.

3. **Claim 3 — VERIFIED (executed measurement): the bundle budget-cap guarantee ships without a working pin.** [C20](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/df98847e2d2ee9ef7e7756ace7c8e17a5ee5ee07/tests/test_triage_bundle_supp.py#L1111-L1112) asserts

```py
            payload_chars <= 100 * 4 or data.get("truncated") is True,
            f"--budget-tokens 100 must cap the whole payload"
```

then unconditionally requires `truncated is True` — the bound leg is unreachable in the check (executed: the drained skeleton serializes to 597 chars > 400 at `--budget-tokens 100`), making the disjunction vacuous; and the deep-drain guarantee (the [docstring](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/df98847e2d2ee9ef7e7756ace7c8e17a5ee5ee07/src/zaxbygraph/derive.py#L2311-L2314) promises

```py
    dropped first, then the tails of ``merge_candidates``/
    ``related_not_bundleable``, then the ``pool`` echo; ``truncated: true``
    marks any payload that needed it, including one still over budget only
    because of its mandatory echoes. The payload's ``weights`` echo is the
```

shed-everything down to mandatory echoes) is pinned only as `len(merge_candidates) < 12` while the shipped behavior drains to 0 — a pop-one-then-stop mutant passes. AC21 of issue #30 ("cap the whole payload with the truncated flag") therefore ships without a discriminating pin.

4. **Claim 4 — VERIFIED (source read): the config docs omit the ambient-config trust boundary.** [README.md:277-279](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/df98847e2d2ee9ef7e7756ace7c8e17a5ee5ee07/README.md#L277-L279) documents the chain mechanics —

```md
Configuration lives in a `[triage]` TOML table resolved through the same
chain as `[derive]`: defaults, then `<store>/config.toml`, then
`.zaxbygraph.toml` (cwd), then `--config` (later wins per key; maps merge
```

— but never states that `<store>/config.toml` and a cwd `.zaxbygraph.toml` are AUTO-LOADED and treated as trusted operator input — running inside a third-party checkout with a planted config reweights results and its strings (formula_version, test_globs, map names) echo into agent-facing payloads unwrapped (deliberately not `untrusted_text`: the marker's GitHub-content scoping is by design, K07 ruling of the PR #45 review).

Prior-art reconciliation: the chain mechanics were shipped by PR #45 (F5); `tests/test_triage_paging.py` (same PR) covers the explicit `--config` level only — this issue extends coverage to the store and cwd levels rather than duplicating it. R7/R9-C20/R10-first-sub-row in PR #45's Considered-not-filed ledger are superseded by this issue (their dispositions said "latent/test-hygiene/coverage"; the critic's probes upgraded them).

## Scope

**In:** config-chain tests at all three levels (store, cwd, explicit) with per-key merge precedence and `config_source` semantics pinned; harness isolation of the ambient config chain for the derived-tier CLI test legs; a budget-cap pin check (below-floor full drain + above-floor bound) in a new test file; the README trust-boundary sentence.
**Out:** wrapping config-derived strings as `untrusted_text` (deliberate scoping — K07); stub-dispatch divergence and the remaining weak-assertion/coverage rows (stay RECORD in the PR #45 ledger); any change to `[triage]` defaults (AC9 record, issue 30 comment 6510715064).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: WHEN `triage`, `bundle`, or `brief` resolve `[triage]` and `[derive]` configuration through the store/cwd/`--config` chain, THE SYSTEM SHALL apply per-key precedence (later source wins; map tables merge per name) and echo a `config_source` that names the supplying level, pinned at the store level, the cwd level, and the explicit level.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_triage_config_chain.py" -b
  - expect: `NO TESTS RAN` (exit 5): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_triage_config_chain.py
  - why: the chain resolution code exists at the anchor (derive.py `_triage_config_chain`, cli.py `_resolve_weight_config`) but no test references either config file; the check file cannot exist at base. (The base-leg absence signature on Python ≤3.12 is `Ran 0 tests` exit 0 — legs pin `py -3.14` for the loud `NO TESTS RAN` exit 5 signature, matching the PR #45 repro-leg convention.)
- [ ] AC2: WHEN the derived-tier acceptance checks execute their CLI legs, THE SYSTEM SHALL isolate the ambient config chain (per-test temp cwd or injected chain paths), so a planted repo-root `.zaxbygraph.toml` or store-level `config.toml` cannot change any check's effective weights — proven by a regression pin that runs the C1 scenario identically with and without a planted config.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_triage_config_chain.py" -k test_hermetic -b
  - expect: `FAIL` — with a planted config the scenario reweights (probe-verified `0.9 != 0.25`); the check plants the file, asserts stability, and fails at base because the harness is not isolated.
  - files: tests/test_triage_config_chain.py
  - why: probe-verified at the anchor (phantom C1 failure; silent C20 reweight).
- [ ] AC3: WHEN `bundle --budget-tokens B` runs at an above-floor budget, THE SYSTEM SHALL return a serialized payload within `B*4` chars, and WHEN the budget is below the payload's skeleton floor, THE SYSTEM SHALL shed every sheddable section (bundles, then `merge_candidates`/`related_not_bundleable` tails, then the `pool` echo) before returning `truncated: true` — both legs pinned in one check.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_triage_budget_pins.py" -b
  - expect: GREEN at base — the behavior is already correct (executed: the drain reaches zero merge_candidates); this is the regression floor C20's vacuous disjunction fails to provide.
  - files: tests/test_triage_budget_pins.py
  - why: C20's bound leg is unreachable (597 > 400 measured) and its drain assert (`< 12`) does not discriminate the shipped full drain; this check must fail under a pop-one-then-stop mutant.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN the `[triage]`/`[derive]` configuration chain is documented, THE SYSTEM SHALL state the ambient-config trust boundary in the README config section: store `config.toml` and a cwd `.zaxbygraph.toml` are auto-loaded and treated as trusted operator input, and running inside a third-party checkout with a planted config reweights results whose strings echo unwrapped into agent-facing payloads — treat cwd configs like shell profiles.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(DOCS_ONLY)
  - substitute evidence: the README diff near the config-chain section (README.md:277-288 at the anchor df98847) carrying the trust-boundary sentence; substitution approved by the swarm-critic adjudication (2026-10-30)
  - files: README.md
  - why: docs-only — no executable check is meaningful for a documentation sentence.

## Definition of done

All four ACs pass on both CI legs (AC4 via the README diff), the new checks are in their own new files (new-checks-new-files convention; no frozen-file amendment required — AC3 is a new pin, C20 stays as the historical record), and the PR-body ledger rows R7/R9-C20/R10-first-sub-row of PR #45 are annotated as superseded by this issue.

## Sequence

Standalone follow-up from PR #45; no dependencies. Suggested one-PR delivery (all four items are small and touch disjoint files: two new test files + the harness isolation + one README paragraph).

item.body:
*Provenance: follow-up from the post-publication review of PR #47 (issue #31), generated per the maintainer's follow-up rule after cross-model adjudication (2026-10-31): the swarm-critic and SolCritic (CONSULT mode) both reviewed this package; where they split, the maintainer's decision is requested in the Decision questions section. Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main at anchor commit d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a on 2026-10-31 by source trace and/or executed probe. One issue = one PR. The PR #47 body carries the full 12-row Considered-not-filed ledger; the review artifacts (.zcode/pr-review/pr47-20261030/) and the trace (.agents/issue-traces/31-read-truth-env/) are git-excluded. Background: #31, #47.*

## Summary

Two decision-grade items survived the PR #47 closeout, both cross-model adjudicated:

1. **Fetch-source persistence (FILE — both critics agree).** The `--max-age` refresh honors the store's recorded `include_patches` but hardcodes the GraphQL fetch source, so a store deliberately kept on `--source rest` either silently profile-drifts or finds the flag permanently dead. Includes a configuration-race invariant both critics endorsed folding into the same fix.
2. **Proxy opt-out parity (the critics split; filed per the contract text).** Issue #31 AC3 requires the four `ZAXBYGRAPH_PROXY_FORGE_HOST` states "exactly as zmem's four states"; the shipped disabled-state behavior (fail-loud parse failure) deviates from zmem's documented literal-key behavior. SolCritic holds this is an unamended requirement deviation; the swarm-critic holds fail-loud is better engineering for a durable evidence store. This issue presents both resolutions; the maintainer picks (Decision questions).

## Problem (claims to verify)

### Item 1 — the --max-age refresh ignores the store's fetch source

1. **The refresh hardcodes the GraphQL source while honoring include_patches from store state.** `VERIFIED` by source trace: `_run_refresh_sync` passes `source_name="graphql"` ([cli.py#L469](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L469)) while `include_patches` is read from `sync_state` ([cli.py#L507](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L507), [cli.py#L523](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L523)) and forwarded to the refresh ([cli.py#L557](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L557)). `sync_state` carries `include_patches` ([schema.sql#L213](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/src/zaxbygraph/schema.sql#L213)) but no fetch-source column. Consequence: a store deliberately kept on `--source rest` (the degraded-GHES population `--source rest` exists for) either silently refreshes via GraphQL — gaining timeline/closing-ref `closes` and `item_events` a REST corpus deliberately lacks — or answers `refresh_failed` and the read is never answered despite a fully serviceable store.
2. **Refresh configuration is sampled before the sync lock.** `VERIFIED` by source trace: the pre-lock probe reads the configuration ([cli.py#L507](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L507)) while the under-lock re-check query selects only `repo` ([cli.py#L546](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L546)). A concurrent writer that enables patch retention while the read waits can have that setting reverted by the waiting refresh, which writes `include_patches` at sync finish (SolCritic, 95/100; falsifier: a controlled contention test).
3. **Narrow fixes were probed and found unsound or inferior.** `VERIFIED` by executed call-site enumeration: `fetch_log` carries no REST/GraphQL discriminator on clean fetches — the ordinary-ingest call ([store.py#L1354](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L1354)) logs `note=None, status=200` — and a meta-KV stamp is dropped by `doctor consolidate`'s sync_state copy. Schema v11 is the preferred design (guarded-ALTER precedent: `migrate_v3_to_v4`); a repo-scoped meta key with explicit consolidation wiring is the sound no-migration alternative (SolCritic).

### Item 2 — ZAXBYGRAPH_PROXY_FORGE_HOST disabled-state parity

1. **The shipped disabled-state behavior deviates from issue #31 AC3's parity requirement.** `VERIFIED` by source trace and executed probes: AC3 requires the four states "exactly as zmem's four states". zmem's documented rule is that disabled states keep the literal key and the empty opt-out exists for a genuine local git server (zmem `docs/CLOUD.md` lines 876-877 and 898-902 on its main branch). Shipped zaxbygraph behavior: `_loopback_proxy_forge` returns None in both disabled states ([repo.py#L183](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/src/zaxbygraph/repo.py#L183), [repo.py#L190](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/src/zaxbygraph/repo.py#L190)), the fall-through then fails `REPO_SLUG_RE` on the 3-segment `git/org/repo` path ([repo.py#L110](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/src/zaxbygraph/repo.py#L110)), and repo-less commands answer "could not parse origin remote" ([repo.py#L236](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/src/zaxbygraph/repo.py#L236)).
2. **The deviation is pinned by the frozen checks PR #47 shipped.** `VERIFIED` by source trace: C6 asserts "rewrite must be silently disabled for this env" ([test_read_truth.py#L377](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/tests/test_read_truth.py#L377)) and the vectors file pins disabled-state `expect: null` ([fixtures_proxy_vectors.json#L62](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/tests/fixtures_proxy_vectors.json#L62), [fixtures_proxy_vectors.json#L67](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/tests/fixtures_proxy_vectors.json#L67)). Implementing parity therefore costs a CHECK_WRONG amendment of C6 plus two vectors plus a new external anchor receipt — that frozen-file cost is inside this issue's scope.
3. **The literal-key design is representable in the (host, slug) model.** `VERIFIED` by executed probe: `_clean_host("127.0.0.1:41233")` returns `127.0.0.1_41233` (a valid HOST_RE segment) and the vectors already pin that exact host shape for a non-proxy loopback URL ([fixtures_proxy_vectors.json#L51](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/tests/fixtures_proxy_vectors.json#L51)) — the divergence from zmem is a policy choice, not a data-model limit.
4. **The current failure is fail-loud with a convergent escape hatch.** `VERIFIED` by source trace: a bare `--repo OWNER/REPO` defaults the host to github.com ([cli.py#L373](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/d2bf564d8c14d50aa4e41710ea18b835cf3d855a/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L373)) — the same store key the unset default produces — so fixing the env var later resumes the same corpus. The swarm-critic holds fail-loud is correct for a durable evidence store (per-port keys fragment corpora across sessions, with lossy `doctor consolidate` recovery); SolCritic holds the documented local-git-server opt-out audience makes the literal key the intended identity and the hard failure an unamended deviation from AC3. The micro-fixes (the disabled-state error naming the env var; the README row-3 counterfactual wording) apply only if fail-loud is confirmed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: WHEN a read runs with --max-age against a stale store whose sync_state.fetch_source records rest THE SYSTEM SHALL construct the REST source for the refresh and SHALL NOT construct a GraphQL source, and a store whose fetch_source is NULL SHALL keep the documented GraphQL refresh.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: py -3.14 -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_read_truth_supp.py" -k test_refresh_honors_fetch_source -b
  - expect: NO TESTS RAN (exit 5)
  - files: src/zaxbygraph/cli.py, src/zaxbygraph/schema.sql, src/zaxbygraph/db.py, src/zaxbygraph/sync.py, src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py, docs/schema.md, README.md, tests/test_read_truth_supp.py
  - why: RED at base (schema v10 has no fetch_source column and the refresh hardcodes graphql).
- [ ] AC2: WHEN a concurrent writer changes sync_state configuration while a --max-age read waits on the sync lock THE SYSTEM SHALL re-read the refresh configuration (fetch source and include_patches) after acquiring the lock and before the refresh so a waiting read never reverts a concurrent writer's settings.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: py -3.14 -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_read_truth_supp.py" -k test_refresh_config_reread_under_lock -b
  - expect: NO TESTS RAN (exit 5)
  - files: src/zaxbygraph/cli.py, tests/test_read_truth_supp.py
  - why: NEW-SURFACE (the under-lock re-check currently selects only repo).
- [ ] AC3: WHEN ZAXBYGRAPH_PROXY_FORGE_HOST is set to an unparseable or empty value and the origin is a loopback git-proxy remote THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve the remote to the literal loopback store key (underscore-folded host, org/repo slug) exactly as the unset state resolves a non-proxy loopback URL, unless the maintainer amends issue #31 AC3 to fail-loud, in which case this issue closes with that amendment recorded and AC4 applies unchanged.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: py -3.14 -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_read_truth.py" -k test_disabled_state_literal_key -b
  - expect: NO TESTS RAN (exit 5)
  - files: src/zaxbygraph/repo.py, tests/test_read_truth.py, tests/fixtures_proxy_vectors.json, README.md
  - why: RED at base (the disabled states return None and C6 plus the vectors pin None; files lines name the CHECK_WRONG amendment surface).
- [ ] AC4: WHEN the origin remote fails to parse because ZAXBYGRAPH_PROXY_FORGE_HOST disabled the loopback rewrite THE SYSTEM SHALL name the variable and its disabled state in the parse-error message.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: py -3.14 -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_read_truth.py" -k test_parse_error_names_proxy_env -b
  - expect: NO TESTS RAN (exit 5)
  - files: src/zaxbygraph/repo.py, tests/test_read_truth.py, README.md
  - why: RED at base (the parse error blames the remote and never names the variable).

## Decision questions (maintainer)

1. **AC1/AC2 design**: schema v11 `sync_state.fetch_source` column (preferred by both critics) or a repo-scoped meta key with explicit consolidation wiring (SolCritic's no-migration alternative)? Stamp semantics: requested source at listing-sync start, or completed source at finish?
2. **AC3/AC4**: implement zmem parity (literal key in the disabled states), or amend issue #31 AC3 to fail-loud with a recorded justification?
3. **MCP boundary (both designs)**: `zaxbygraph mcp`'s background sync constructs its source directly (mcp_server.py:135-142, "the REST fallback stays a CLI flag"). Confirm the store-preference fix is CLI-side only, or extend it to MCP.

## Scope

**In:** the two items above; frozen-file CHECK_WRONG amendments for AC3 (C6 plus the two disabled-state vectors) with a new external anchor receipt; docs/schema.md and README updates; the AC4 error-message change.

**Out:** MCP fetch-source behavior (explicit boundary pending Decision question 3); the unbounded `--max-age` lock wait (PR #47 ledger row 2, documented like `sync --wait`); every other Considered-not-filed row in the PR #47 body.

## Definition of done

All ACs pass on every CI leg, and the PR carries a closure-evidence section mapping each AC to executed checks.
item.title: Follow-up from PR #47: fetch-source persistence for --max-age refresh, and ZAXBYGRAPH_PROXY_FORGE_HOST opt-out parity

item.body: Closes #33 ## Root Cause The MCP server (src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py) predated the SOTA plan's agent-surface milestones in four ways: every tool result was a bare text block (the tools/call write at the former L1173-1180 emitted only content/isError — no structuredContent), no tool declared an outputSchema or annotations although the advertised 2025-06-18 revision supports both, the negotiation tuple stopped at 2025-06-18, and the five CLI read tiers (churn, similar, triage, bundle, brief) had no tools at all — the registry guard test explicitly deferred them to "issue #32's lane". The stateless 2026-07-28 revision was unimplemented entirely: no _meta-carried negotiation, no server/discover, no resultType, no cache hints, and the repo-resolution path still round-tripped Roots for repo-less calls. ## Fix - Every tool entry gains a permissive outputSchema ({type: object, additionalProperties: true}) and annotations (readOnlyHint true except sync), attached in one post-registration loop; the listing is sorted by name — one deterministic order for both eras. - One central `_tool_result` write carries `structuredContent` (the parsed envelope) on every tool answer, success or failure, across all three former serialization sites; modern results add `resultType: "complete"`. - Five new tools (`similar_items`, `triage`, `bundle`, `brief`, `churn`) call the CLI's own derived-read wrappers (`_similar_query`/`_triage_query`/`_bundle_query`/`_brief_query`, `query.churn`) so data payloads match the CLI on the same store (envelope identity/freshness fields are per-surface by construction), with an explicit exception-translation mirroring `_run_derived_read`'s vocabulary (LookupError → not_found, ConfigError → config_error, ValueError → bad_request, sqlite → store_unreadable) and strict int-array→CSV conversion for pool/exclude. `--config`/`--ls-files` are deliberately not exposed (filesystem/git side-channels from model-reachable tools). - Legacy negotiation answers 2025-11-25 as latest (initialize never negotiates 2026-07-28). - The stateless 2026-07-28 era: requests declare `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` + `clientCapabilities` in `_meta` per request (absent → legacy; unsupported declared version → -32022 with the supported list; declared-but-malformed → -32602); modern ping is method-not-found (legacy ping preserved); `server/discover` returns supportedVersions (derived from one constants seam) + capabilities + tools with CacheableResult hints (ttlMs/cacheScope); modern tools/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list carry the same hints; a complete modern resources/read is private-scoped; a repo-less un-pinned modern call (tools or resources/read) answers an InputRequiredResult (resultType input_required + requestState + repo- naming text) and never sends Roots. ## Recurrence Prevention (defect class) - Defect class: a consumer surface gains a capability without the typed metadata its protocol era requires, or drifts from the CLI counterpart it mirrors. - Sweep result: 7 hits across 4 predicates, all dispositioned (1 covered by the central write, 3 intended input_required shapes pinned by frozen checks, 3 predicates with zero hits) — 08a-recurrence-sweep.md. - Guardrail: tests/test_mcp_registry.py (installed by the #7 trace), extended to the five tools; demonstrated to bite live mid-implementation ("MCP tools with no CLI counterpart cell: brief, bundle, churn, similar_items, triage") and green at head. ## Tests - Regression tests: tests/test_mcp_typed.py (C1-C4, C12) + tests/test_mcp_2026.py (C7-C10), frozen at the red checkpoint through reviewed amendment waves (receipts v1-v5, published before/between implementation and closure); all 12 checks certified RED/ERROR→GREEN at head (08). - Impacted suite: `py -3.14 -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → 644 OK (635 at base; certified at 4d064eb). - Deferred-work scan: clean. ## Regression Protection - 9/9 named mutation probes KILLED (one per executable check incl. C12; see repro/mutation-probe-results.md). - Preserving checks C5/C6/C11 pin old-client initialize/tools-list and the stale-read background refresh across the change. - test_mcp_registry.py two-directional tables updated (5 new mappings); EXPECTED_TOOLS 11→16. ## External Checkpoint Anchor - CURRENT anchor receipt (v5, published on issue #32 comment 6548615686 after the final-critic amendment froze the C12 leg script itself): `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=32-33-mcp-typed-stateless manifest=e2910fece6eab84953a0ff266522d2dcfa95ed21 semantics=4faaf11a344bae6ced2a0bc50c60e20d84374082 tree=cb1ae09df6116f9a2886c48e596131579965e92d` Run verify-anchor with THIS literal — earlier literals are historical: v1 comment 6546583026 (pre-implementation), v2 6546991792 and v3 6547164117 (reviewed CHECK_WRONG waves, semantics 160ea01f408d376dce5471d13212d514444cc58a), v4 comment 6548160037 (the implementation-review amendment adding C12/AC13, semantics moved to 4faaf11a344bae6ced2a0bc50c60e20d84374082 with the new table row). - Independent verification: verify-anchor PASS by the plan critic (R2, R4) and the implementation reviewer. - Discovery copy: .agents/issue-traces/32-33-mcp-typed-stateless/ 02-reproduction.md (non-authoritative). ## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence | Acceptance criterion | Evidence | |---|---| | #32 AC1 (outputSchema+annotations, readOnlyHint) | frozen check C1 RED→GREEN | | #32 AC2 (structuredContent == parsed text, validates) | frozen check C2 RED→GREEN (incl. generic-exception leg) | | #32 AC3 (2025-11-25 negotiation, 2025-06-18 preserved) | frozen check C3 RED→GREEN | | #32 AC4 (five tools, CLI-equal envelopes) | frozen check C4 ERROR→GREEN (exact data-parity legs for all five + failure parity + arrays) | | #32 AC5 (existing initialize/tools-list) | frozen check C5 GREEN→GREEN | | #32 AC6 (stale read answers now + background refresh) | frozen check C6 GREEN→GREEN | | #32 AC7 (distribution decision) | NON-EXECUTABLE(PRODUCT_DECISION) — maintainer records on issue #32; PR head: 1448bbb9a694bd6dccfff2a5dc200c5a1c4fc16e (branch fix/32-33-mcp-typed-stateless; 3 commits — the feature 0440c7c, the review-fix 4d064eb, and the docs-nits commit 1448bbb) Refs #32 — the code ships and all executable ACs close here; #32 itself auto-closes only when its AC7 distribution decision is recorded (see Open product question), so this PR deliberately does not auto-close it. ## Issue Closure Closes #33 — the code ships and all executable ACs close here; #32 itself auto-closes only when its AC7 distribution decision is recorded (see Open product question), so this PR deliberately does not auto-close it. --- ## Summary by cubic Implements typed MCP tool results, five CLI-derived tools, and the stateless 2026-07-28 protocol era (issues #32 and #33). - Every tool now declares `outputSchema` and `annotations` (`readOnlyHint` true except `sync`), and every result carries `structuredContent` equal to the parsed envelope. - Five new tools (`similar_items`, `triage`, `bundle`, `brief`, `churn`) call the same query layer as their CLI commands, so data payloads match the CLI byte-for-byte on the same store; errors use the CLI's coded vocabulary. - Legacy `initialize` negotiation now serves `2025-11-25` as latest. - The stateless 2026-07-28 era: protocol version and capabilities ride each request's `_meta`, `server/discover` reports `supportedVersions`/`capabilities`/`tools` with cache hints, results carry `resultType` (`complete` or `input_required`), and repo-less calls answer an `InputRequiredResult` naming `repo` instead of round-tripping Roots. - Legacy clients keep the previous behavior, pinned by preserved tests. **Migration** - Modern (2026-07-28) clients must send `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` and `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities` in each request's `_meta`; unsupported versions answer `-32022` and malformed metadata answers `-32602`. Written for commit 1448bbb9a694bd6dccfff2a5dc200c5a1c4fc16e. Summary will update on new commits.

ASK-ledger verification results (executed 2026-11-03 at `f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b`, the merge head of this PR) — closing all three open product questions with evidence, per the follow-up rule's "keep the record true":

**ASK-3 (delete_owned_edges reverse-pass reverts half) — NOT A DEFECT, no filing.** The claimed premise is factually wrong: the `reverts` edge's `src` is the revert PR (docs/schema.md:246; extract.py:852-853 body path, extract.py:865-875 forward title path), and the original item's own ingest re-derives it through the title-revert reverse pass in `store.py` `rebuild_edges` (the same 7-tuple the forward pass emits, upserted idempotently). `delete_owned_edges` (store.py:492-507) deletes only the re-ingested item's outbound edges plus inbound actor relations, so it cannot reach an edge owned by another item. Executed probe (both ingest orders, incremental re-ingest of the original, and `sync --numbers <original>`): the edge survives with an unchanged rowid in every case; the existing pin `tests/test_feedback_hardening.py::test_reingest_does_not_duplicate` covers the outcome. The only genuine retraction path is by-design: re-ingesting the revert PR after the original's title changed.

**ASK-2 (rebuild_links malformed-dst delete) — VERIFIED, FILED as #53.** `rebuild_links` (store.py:462-472) deletes a carried-complete connection's stored `source='link'` edges and re-emits only nodes `_link_dst` can parse (extract.py:602-617, 637-639), so a node that fails to parse silently retracts a GitHub-reported link fact with no replacement — the exact outcome the function's docstring (store.py:445-450) promises cannot happen. Executed probe at the store API: `after good link payload: [('1','blocked_by','7','link')]` → `after malformed link payload: []`; with one good and one malformed node, only the parseable sibling survives. No test pins this shape. Fix direction (product call recorded in the issue's Design section): treat a connection containing an unparseable node like an overflowed connection — union-only, no retraction — while an explicitly cleared singular value (`parent: null`) keeps retracting.

**ASK-1 (case-fold collision-losers under-scope) — VERIFIED, FILED as #52 (with the consolidation sibling defects found in the same sweep).** `_drop_collision_losers` (db.py:266-274) deletes the loser's children from only `labels`, `comments`, `reviews`, `pr_files`, `edges`; the post-v2 repo-keyed item-scoped tables (`assignees`, `issue_field_values`, `revisions`, `item_path_refs`, `item_signatures`, `item_events`, `pr_commits`) get neither fold nor loser-deletion, against docs/schema.md:527-531's "every repo-keyed table" contract. The same sweep verified two further `doctor` defects now covered by #52: (1) `doctor` copies candidates with `shutil.copy2` (doctor.py:96, 159) — main file only — so a crash-damaged candidate's committed `-wal` rows are invisible (candidate dropped from the report, `ok: true`) or, on `--consolidate`, adopted as a truncated copy that REPLACES the store's richer corpus (executed probe: a 30-item store ends holding 5); (2) the consolidation copy (doctor.py:333-343) has no folded-key dedupe, so a dual-cased candidate aborts the adoption with a raw `UNIQUE constraint failed`. The critic's recommendation to file ASK-1 as its own migration-integrity issue is executed as #52's AC4.

Issues #52 and #53 are worked together in one user-authorized multi-issue PR; the survey probe artifacts are under `.zcode/pr-review/survey-c4/` in the maintainer's local checkout (not part of this repository) and every claim above is re-derivable from the cited source lines.

Closes #40
Closes #48
Closes #36

**PR head:** 1038e16 (branch `fix/40-48-36-collated-followups`, 8 commits over base 0790bf57: implementation 6a7cdcb, 4.5-review fixes 0f4ce5c, final-critic fix 9a6cc5a, swarm-review fixes ad1ec4d, cubic re-review stamping fix 1995da4, fix-round reviewer round-2 fixes cea1d8d, final-critic round 1038e16)
**Merge status:** AWAITING_USER_APPROVAL — this skill never merges on its own authority.

## Root Cause

Three adjudicated follow-ups from one review program, collated per the
maintainer's standing multi-issue authorization:

- **#40 (bug, high).** `consolidate()` (src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py, the
  `_COPY_TABLES` delete loop at the old lines 208-209) deleted every
  `revisions` row for the slug before copying the candidate's rows. The
  replacement scope is candidate-observed rows; the delete scope was
  slug-wide. A pre-v8 candidate migrates in with an empty, backfill-
  impossible `revisions` table (db.py `migrate_v7_to_v8`), so its
  emptiness was a schema artifact — adopting it destroyed revision
  history that cannot be re-derived (edit history is unobservable after
  the fact; ingest is append-only and this was the only revisions DELETE
  in the tree).
- **#48 (bug).** `_run_refresh_sync` (src/zaxbygraph/cli.py) hardcoded
  `source_name="graphql"` while honoring `include_patches` from
  sync_state — a store deliberately kept on `--source rest`
  profile-drifted on `--max-age` refresh. The under-lock re-check
  selected only `repo`, so a concurrent writer's config could be
  reverted by a waiting read. And the proxy-disabled parse error blamed
  the remote URL without naming `ZAXBYGRAPH_PROXY_FORGE_HOST`.
- **#36 (frozen-check quality).** C2 asserted a hand-copied SQL literal
  (the LOWER(title) mutant left it GREEN — probe of record in the PR #35
  review), C6 asserted presence-not-position of `pragma optimize`, C4's
  corpus cost ~4x wall time with no added discrimination, and AGENTS.md
  lacked the count-freshness invariant that docs/schema.md records.

## Fix

- **#40 — per-item revision preservation.** `consolidate()` exempts
  `revisions` from the slug-wide delete; covered items (candidate has
  rows for them) whose candidate rows are payload-identical to the
  stored rows (all seven columns) are skipped (a same-candidate
  re-adoption writes nothing and deletes nothing — the literal AC6); covered
  items with different rows are replaced with fresh ids in sequence
  order; items the candidate never observed keep their history. The
  doctor result payload reports `revisions_adopted` /
  `revisions_preserved`. Within-item depth loss (a shallower candidate
  for an item it covers still replaces) stays a recorded boundary,
  documented on all three surfaces (docs/schema.md revisions section,
  schema_notes.py `revisions.id`, the `consolidate()` docstring).
  Consolidation also carries `fetch_source` from a post-v11 candidate's
  sync_state row (pre-v11 candidates leave it NULL).
- **#48 — fetch-source persistence.** Schema v11 adds
  `sync_state.fetch_source TEXT` (fresh shape == ALTER shape; guarded
  ADD COLUMN migration; `_V11_USER_VERSION` slot; feature gates stay
  pinned to their own slots). `_ensure_state_row` stamps the source
  REQUESTED at listing-sync start in its own prologue transaction
  (targeted `--numbers` runs stamp too); the `--max-age` refresh
  re-reads BOTH config values under the sync lock on the writable
  post-migration connection, so a v10 store keeps refreshing (the
  pre-lock query never references the column) and a waiting read never
  reverts a concurrent writer's settings. NULL → the documented graphql
  default. MCP untouched (CLI-side only, recorded decision). Proxy
  attribution: `_proxy_disabled_reason` names the variable and its
  disabled state only on the exact counterfactual (would-parse-when-
  enabled, including the `.git`-suffixed shape — normalization mirrors
  the parser), appended by both public parse-error callers. Fail-loud
  disabled-state behavior kept; #31 AC3 amended with recorded
  justification at publication (comment 6559860489).
- **#36 — frozen-check hardening.** C2 now EXPLAINs the runtime-captured
  revert-title statement (stats-cleared fresh-connection oracle); C6
  asserts the finish COMMIT precedes the first `pragma optimize`; C4's
  corpus drops to 1000/2000 with probed-equal discrimination (fresh
  pin-reverted ratio 1.979 at the #22 base vs recorded 1.961); AGENTS.md
  gains the count-freshness bullet. All three amendments ride the #22
  trace's manifest as CHECK_WRONG AMEND rows (one batch; fresh replays
  10/10).

## Recurrence Prevention (defect class)

- Defect class: bulk deletes (and config reads) whose scope is wider
  than the data — or observation — that replaces them.
- Sweep result: 23 raw DELETE hits censused across doctor/db/store/sync;
  every site dispositioned (FIXED ×2 — the revisions scoping and the
  refresh config re-read; RECORD ×4 re-sync-recoverable or documented
  boundaries; covered-yes ×12; 3 probe-required candidates routed to the
  ASK ledger below). Full table in the trace's 08a artifact; RECORD rows
  in "Considered, not filed".
- Guardrail: the static revisions guard (tests/test_revisions.py
  AppendOnlyGuardTests) now whitelists exactly the two sanctioned
  consolidation delete shapes — demonstrated to bite: it FAILED the
  implementation's first per-item delete line before the whitelist
  landed. C5's id-stability oracle (sentinel-blocked rowid reuse) fails
  on any future delete+reinsert re-adoption path; C7's interleaving test
  kills no-reread and one-value-reread mutants.

## Tests

- Frozen acceptance checks: `bash .agents/issue-traces/40-48-36-followups/repro/replay-all.sh`
  → **12/12 PASS** (8 DISCRIMINATING RED→GREEN, C4 ERROR→GREEN, 3
  PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN), fail=0 at head 1038e16.
- Regression tests: `PYTHONPATH="src;tests" python -m unittest discover -s tests -b`
  → **Ran 667 tests — OK** (base 646; +21: consolidation preservation,
  stamping, refresh-source, parse-error naming, v11 migration).
- Mutation probes: 10 named probes + the 4.5-reviewer's 5 probes + the
  final critic's counterfactual probe — all killed, restored from saved
  bytes, tree clean after each.
- Deferred-work scan: `scan-deferred.sh` -> clean at head 1038e16.

## Regression Protection

- tests/test_consolidation_revisions.py (6 tests: preservation,
  per-item replace, twice row-neutral with id-stability + sentinel,
  report counts + zero-case, seven-column comparison pin)
- tests/test_refresh_source.py (7 tests: REST/GraphQL source
  construction, config re-read interleaving, v10 refresh regression,
  stamping write path ×3)
- tests/test_proxy_parse_error.py (5 tests: counterfactual gating, both
  public callers, `.git`-suffixed attribution, non-attribution cases)
- tests/test_schema_v11.py (4 tests: fresh/migrated shape parity, NULL
  default, idempotence, reads-never-migrate)
- tests/test_revisions.py: consolidation test reworked to per-item scope
  (STALE rows survive; issue #40's own AC3 text), append-only guard
  whitelists both sanctioned delete shapes; test_ingest_scale.py C2/C6/C4
  amendments; test_export_corpus/test_text_refs_supp version-slot pins
  decoupled from CURRENT_USER_VERSION-relative arithmetic.

## External Checkpoint Anchor

- Receipt published before implementation (v1, comment 6554950876);
  amendment chains v2 (6555418779), v3 (6556222975), v4 (6559206765),
  v5 (6559797044), v6 (6562398943), v7 (6562516083), v8 (6563732506,
  FINAL, merge-bound). Current literal:
  `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=40-48-36-followups manifest=e43fae6642100c7469fa1b9623964c63235f623f semantics=85bf3eeb1f84ff9ad7515dbe389c8969fc49e909 tree=97c2319321ab3a6dfe63f849096b8dd2b6700cf9`
- External artifact location: comments on ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph#40 (and the
  #36 replacement-anchor record, comment 6559860814).
- Independent verification: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug 40-48-36-followups --receipt '<literal above>'`
  → PASS (re-executed by the plan critic, the implementation reviewer,
  and the final critic, each independently).
- Local copy/provenance: `.agents/issue-traces/40-48-36-followups/repro/receipt.txt`
  (non-authoritative discovery copy).
- #22 manifest note: whole-manifest verification fails on three
  UNRELATED pre-existing drift-broken frozen files (test_migrations.py,
  test_sync.py, test_closes_edge_uniqueness.py — drifted via merged PRs
  #39/#41 and earlier); never presented as passing; the collated receipt
  is the replacement anchor for the six amended pairs only.

## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| 40-AC1 (empty candidate keeps history) | C1 RED→GREEN; probe P1 at base |
| 40-AC2 (partial candidate replaces only observed) | C2 RED→GREEN; probe P2 |
| 40-AC3 (fresh ids, sequence order, cross-repo isolation) | C3 amended RED→GREEN (STALE-UNOBSERVED-ROWS-DELETED marker) |
| 40-AC4 (doctor payload reports counts) | C4 ERROR→GREEN (REPORT-FIELD-MISSING → fields present); critic's end-to-end envelope check |
| 40-AC5 (docs: per-item preservation + depth-loss boundary) | DOCS_ONLY — the diff's three doc surfaces, reviewed at review time (final critic verified wording) |
| 40-AC6 (twice-adoption writes/deletes nothing) | C5 amended RED→GREEN (REVISION-ROWIDS-CHANGED, sentinel-blocked) |
| 48-AC1 (refresh honors fetch_source) | C6 RED→GREEN (REST built, GraphQL not) |
| 48-AC2 (config re-read under lock) | C7 RED→GREEN; no-reread + one-value mutants killed |
| 48-AC3 (proxy parity resolution) | PRODUCT_DECISION — fail-loud kept; #31 AC3 amendment published (comment 6559860489) |
| 48-AC4 (parse error names the variable) | C8 RED→GREEN; `.git`-shape vector added in the critic round |
| 36-AC1 (C2 runtime-capture) | C9 PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN + fresh pin-reverted discrimination 1.979 |
| 36-AC2 (C6 positional optimize) | C10 PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN |
| 36-AC3 (C4 corpus 1000/2000) | C11 PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN |
| 36-AC4 (AGENTS.md count-freshness bullet) | C12 RED→GREEN (AGENTS-COUNT-FRESHNESS-MISSING) |

## Invariant Audit

- Every edge EXTRACTED: not touched (derived reads never write edges; the
  diff adds no edge writes).
- Node types: not touched.
- Evidence-is-payload / edge identity: not touched.
- closes vs closes_keyword semantics: not touched.
- Watermark verbatim+inclusive: not touched (fetch_source stamps are a
  separate prologue transaction, disclosed).
- Per-item BEGIN IMMEDIATE + watermark: not touched.
- Ingest idempotence: not touched.
- Storage faults reported: not touched.
- Child-row replacement + v10 completeness gating: not touched.
- Delete-owned edges exemptions: not touched.
- Read-only sql escape hatch: not touched.
- SQLite floor: not touched (v11 uses ALTER ADD COLUMN, ≥3.35 already
  required).
- Windows first-class: touched — new tests run on the primary platform;
  the v10-demotion fixtures avoid ALTER DROP (SQLite table-text quirk)
  so the same code runs on Linux CI.
- Version-dependent floor + feature-gate slot discipline: touched — v11
  slot added, `_V11_USER_VERSION` pinned, gates verified not to
  reference CURRENT_USER_VERSION; two test files' slot-relative version
  arithmetic decoupled (test_export_corpus too_new → CURRENT+1,
  test_text_refs_supp backfill stamp → literal slot 8).

## Risk and Rollback

- Risk level: medium (schema v11 migration + consolidation semantics
  change + refresh config path).
- Rollback: revert the branch (single-topic commits; forward-only schema
  means a reverted build refuses v11 stores with the standard
  store_too_new guard — documented behavior).
- Residual risk: none known; the within-item depth-loss boundary is
  recorded on all three doc surfaces.

## Considered, not filed

| # | Item | Disposition | Re-evaluation trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | item_events/pr_commits consolidation wipe (pre-v10 candidate → empty tables) | RECORD — re-sync-recoverable by the issue's own design reasoning (GitHub regenerates timeline/commits on refetch); verified by source read (db.py migrate_v9_to_v10) | if a re-sync-degraded store cannot refetch those sections |
| R2 | consolidation sync_state rate-limit columns NULL for pre-v4 candidates | RECORD — pre-existing documented conditional-copy behavior, unchanged | candidate corpus older than v4 in practice |
| R3 | migrate_v7_to_v8/migrate_v9_to_v10 empty-by-construction tables as the enabler of the #40 shape | RECORD — documented in docs/schema.md; the #40 fix scopes the consumer | none (design record) |
| R4 | store.py replace_item_children degraded-absence boundary | RECORD — documented boundary (docs/schema.md), unchanged | completeness gating redesign |
| R5 | repro-check.sh line-381 Bad-file-descriptor stderr noise on this host | RECORD — benign, rows validate; script is external to this repo | issue-tracer upstream |
| R6 | #22 whole-manifest verify-checkpoint failure on three unrelated drift-broken files | RECORD — disclosed; replacement-anchor route approved by plan critic + final critic | next PR touching those files re-baselines them |

## ASK ledger (open product questions — critic input attached, user decision pending)

1. **Case-fold collision-losers under-scope** (db.py `_drop_collision_losers`
   omits the v8+ item-scoped tables, so a legacy case-split DB's loser
   revisions re-attach to the winner's number). Verified by source read;
   trigger is the known-broken pre-fold repair path. Critic read: the
   final critic reviewed 08a without objection; recommendation = FILE as
   its own small migration-integrity issue if the maintainer agrees.
2. **rebuild_links malformed-dst delete** (a carried link whose node
   parses to None deletes the stored GitHub-reported link edge with no
   replacement). Needs an executed probe to verify the trigger shape and
   a product call on union-only preservation for malformed nodes.
3. **delete_owned_edges reverse-pass reverts half** (whether the original
   item's re-ingest deletes src=original `reverts` edges that only the
   revert-PR's ingest recreates). Needs an executed probe; design note in
