Closes #40
Closes #48
Closes #36

**PR head:** 1038e16 (branch `fix/40-48-36-collated-followups`, 8 commits over base 0790bf57: implementation 6a7cdcb, 4.5-review fixes 0f4ce5c, final-critic fix 9a6cc5a, swarm-review fixes ad1ec4d, cubic re-review stamping fix 1995da4, fix-round reviewer round-2 fixes cea1d8d, final-critic round 1038e16)
**Merge status:** AWAITING_USER_APPROVAL — this skill never merges on its own authority.

## Root Cause

Three adjudicated follow-ups from one review program, collated per the
maintainer's standing multi-issue authorization:

- **#40 (bug, high).** `consolidate()` (src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py, the
  `_COPY_TABLES` delete loop at the old lines 208-209) deleted every
  `revisions` row for the slug before copying the candidate's rows. The
  replacement scope is candidate-observed rows; the delete scope was
  slug-wide. A pre-v8 candidate migrates in with an empty, backfill-
  impossible `revisions` table (db.py `migrate_v7_to_v8`), so its
  emptiness was a schema artifact — adopting it destroyed revision
  history that cannot be re-derived (edit history is unobservable after
  the fact; ingest is append-only and this was the only revisions DELETE
  in the tree).
- **#48 (bug).** `_run_refresh_sync` (src/zaxbygraph/cli.py) hardcoded
  `source_name="graphql"` while honoring `include_patches` from
  sync_state — a store deliberately kept on `--source rest`
  profile-drifted on `--max-age` refresh. The under-lock re-check
  selected only `repo`, so a concurrent writer's config could be
  reverted by a waiting read. And the proxy-disabled parse error blamed
  the remote URL without naming `ZAXBYGRAPH_PROXY_FORGE_HOST`.
- **#36 (frozen-check quality).** C2 asserted a hand-copied SQL literal
  (the LOWER(title) mutant left it GREEN — probe of record in the PR #35
  review), C6 asserted presence-not-position of `pragma optimize`, C4's
  corpus cost ~4x wall time with no added discrimination, and AGENTS.md
  lacked the count-freshness invariant that docs/schema.md records.

## Fix

- **#40 — per-item revision preservation.** `consolidate()` exempts
  `revisions` from the slug-wide delete; covered items (candidate has
  rows for them) whose candidate rows are payload-identical to the
  stored rows (all seven columns) are skipped (a same-candidate
  re-adoption writes nothing and deletes nothing — the literal AC6); covered
  items with different rows are replaced with fresh ids in sequence
  order; items the candidate never observed keep their history. The
  doctor result payload reports `revisions_adopted` /
  `revisions_preserved`. Within-item depth loss (a shallower candidate
  for an item it covers still replaces) stays a recorded boundary,
  documented on all three surfaces (docs/schema.md revisions section,
  schema_notes.py `revisions.id`, the `consolidate()` docstring).
  Consolidation also carries `fetch_source` from a post-v11 candidate's
  sync_state row (pre-v11 candidates leave it NULL).
- **#48 — fetch-source persistence.** Schema v11 adds
  `sync_state.fetch_source TEXT` (fresh shape == ALTER shape; guarded
  ADD COLUMN migration; `_V11_USER_VERSION` slot; feature gates stay
  pinned to their own slots). `_ensure_state_row` stamps the source
  REQUESTED at listing-sync start in its own prologue transaction
  (targeted `--numbers` runs stamp too); the `--max-age` refresh
  re-reads BOTH config values under the sync lock on the writable
  post-migration connection, so a v10 store keeps refreshing (the
  pre-lock query never references the column) and a waiting read never
  reverts a concurrent writer's settings. NULL → the documented graphql
  default. MCP untouched (CLI-side only, recorded decision). Proxy
  attribution: `_proxy_disabled_reason` names the variable and its
  disabled state only on the exact counterfactual (would-parse-when-
  enabled, including the `.git`-suffixed shape — normalization mirrors
  the parser), appended by both public parse-error callers. Fail-loud
  disabled-state behavior kept; #31 AC3 amended with recorded
  justification at publication (comment 6559860489).
- **#36 — frozen-check hardening.** C2 now EXPLAINs the runtime-captured
  revert-title statement (stats-cleared fresh-connection oracle); C6
  asserts the finish COMMIT precedes the first `pragma optimize`; C4's
  corpus drops to 1000/2000 with probed-equal discrimination (fresh
  pin-reverted ratio 1.979 at the #22 base vs recorded 1.961); AGENTS.md
  gains the count-freshness bullet. All three amendments ride the #22
  trace's manifest as CHECK_WRONG AMEND rows (one batch; fresh replays
  10/10).

## Recurrence Prevention (defect class)

- Defect class: bulk deletes (and config reads) whose scope is wider
  than the data — or observation — that replaces them.
- Sweep result: 23 raw DELETE hits censused across doctor/db/store/sync;
  every site dispositioned (FIXED ×2 — the revisions scoping and the
  refresh config re-read; RECORD ×4 re-sync-recoverable or documented
  boundaries; covered-yes ×12; 3 probe-required candidates routed to the
  ASK ledger below). Full table in the trace's 08a artifact; RECORD rows
  in "Considered, not filed".
- Guardrail: the static revisions guard (tests/test_revisions.py
  AppendOnlyGuardTests) now whitelists exactly the two sanctioned
  consolidation delete shapes — demonstrated to bite: it FAILED the
  implementation's first per-item delete line before the whitelist
  landed. C5's id-stability oracle (sentinel-blocked rowid reuse) fails
  on any future delete+reinsert re-adoption path; C7's interleaving test
  kills no-reread and one-value-reread mutants.

## Tests

- Frozen acceptance checks: `bash .agents/issue-traces/40-48-36-followups/repro/replay-all.sh`
  → **12/12 PASS** (8 DISCRIMINATING RED→GREEN, C4 ERROR→GREEN, 3
  PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN), fail=0 at head 1038e16.
- Regression tests: `PYTHONPATH="src;tests" python -m unittest discover -s tests -b`
  → **Ran 667 tests — OK** (base 646; +21: consolidation preservation,
  stamping, refresh-source, parse-error naming, v11 migration).
- Mutation probes: 10 named probes + the 4.5-reviewer's 5 probes + the
  final critic's counterfactual probe — all killed, restored from saved
  bytes, tree clean after each.
- Deferred-work scan: `scan-deferred.sh` -> clean at head 1038e16.

## Regression Protection

- tests/test_consolidation_revisions.py (6 tests: preservation,
  per-item replace, twice row-neutral with id-stability + sentinel,
  report counts + zero-case, seven-column comparison pin)
- tests/test_refresh_source.py (7 tests: REST/GraphQL source
  construction, config re-read interleaving, v10 refresh regression,
  stamping write path ×3)
- tests/test_proxy_parse_error.py (5 tests: counterfactual gating, both
  public callers, `.git`-suffixed attribution, non-attribution cases)
- tests/test_schema_v11.py (4 tests: fresh/migrated shape parity, NULL
  default, idempotence, reads-never-migrate)
- tests/test_revisions.py: consolidation test reworked to per-item scope
  (STALE rows survive; issue #40's own AC3 text), append-only guard
  whitelists both sanctioned delete shapes; test_ingest_scale.py C2/C6/C4
  amendments; test_export_corpus/test_text_refs_supp version-slot pins
  decoupled from CURRENT_USER_VERSION-relative arithmetic.

## External Checkpoint Anchor

- Receipt published before implementation (v1, comment 6554950876);
  amendment chains v2 (6555418779), v3 (6556222975), v4 (6559206765),
  v5 (6559797044), v6 (6562398943), v7 (6562516083), v8 (6563732506,
  FINAL, merge-bound). Current literal:
  `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=40-48-36-followups manifest=e43fae6642100c7469fa1b9623964c63235f623f semantics=85bf3eeb1f84ff9ad7515dbe389c8969fc49e909 tree=97c2319321ab3a6dfe63f849096b8dd2b6700cf9`
- External artifact location: comments on ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph#40 (and the
  #36 replacement-anchor record, comment 6559860814).
- Independent verification: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug 40-48-36-followups --receipt '<literal above>'`
  → PASS (re-executed by the plan critic, the implementation reviewer,
  and the final critic, each independently).
- Local copy/provenance: `.agents/issue-traces/40-48-36-followups/repro/receipt.txt`
  (non-authoritative discovery copy).
- #22 manifest note: whole-manifest verification fails on three
  UNRELATED pre-existing drift-broken frozen files (test_migrations.py,
  test_sync.py, test_closes_edge_uniqueness.py — drifted via merged PRs
  #39/#41 and earlier); never presented as passing; the collated receipt
  is the replacement anchor for the six amended pairs only.

## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| 40-AC1 (empty candidate keeps history) | C1 RED→GREEN; probe P1 at base |
| 40-AC2 (partial candidate replaces only observed) | C2 RED→GREEN; probe P2 |
| 40-AC3 (fresh ids, sequence order, cross-repo isolation) | C3 amended RED→GREEN (STALE-UNOBSERVED-ROWS-DELETED marker) |
| 40-AC4 (doctor payload reports counts) | C4 ERROR→GREEN (REPORT-FIELD-MISSING → fields present); critic's end-to-end envelope check |
| 40-AC5 (docs: per-item preservation + depth-loss boundary) | DOCS_ONLY — the diff's three doc surfaces, reviewed at review time (final critic verified wording) |

| 48-AC1 (refresh honors fetch_source) | C6 RED→GREEN (REST built, GraphQL not) |
| 48-AC2 (config re-read under lock) | C7 RED→GREEN; no-reread + one-value mutants killed |

item.body:
Closes #34. Closes #46.

Collated trace `34-46-snapshot-config-hardening` (user-authorized multi-issue PR per the 2026-11-01 directive; precedent PR #50). Base `f00d38b`, head `5d47b88` (critic-approved `ddf1070` + the CI-identity fix `2609692` + four post-publication review-fix commits `04d6724`, `99f62f0`, `0dbe728`, `5d47b88`), 20 files, +2736/-30. Full protocol: plan-critic 5 rounds (APPROVE), implementation reviewer 7 rounds (APPROVE), final critic 6 rounds (all findings fixed).

## Summary

**#34 (Workstream E — verified store transport, new feature).** `snapshot publish` moves a store as a single orphan commit (manifest + gzip parts) to a target repo; `snapshot pull` stages-then-verifies and installs atomically under the sync lock. Every manifest field derives from one staged backup (completeness, watermark, schema, corpus digest); pull refuses tampered/oversized/newer-schema snapshots, protects a newer local store without `--force`, writes provenance into the staged db, and quiesces the destination before the single `os.replace`. `status` gains `data.snapshot`; consolidation drops `snapshot.*` provenance with disclosure. `--verify-sample N` re-fetches N random items and compares their stored fields for drift; `docs/examples/snapshot-publish.yml` is the scheduled single-writer workflow. AC6's live probe is recorded on #34 (comments 6565353565 + correction 6565943329: GitHub accepts `refs/zaxbygraph/*`; the branch fallback is pinned in-suite).

**#46 (derived-tier acceptance-gate integrity, defects).** The config chain (store `config.toml` → cwd `.zaxbygraph.toml` → `--config`) is now covered at all three levels with per-key precedence, per-name map merge and `config_source` labels for both public chain entry points. All derived-tier CLI leg runners execute in isolated cwds (temp dirs; a temp git checkout for the checkout-dependent `similar` legs) — a planted repo-root config can no longer reweight checks. `tests/test_triage_budget_pins.py` replaces C20's vacuous disjunction with binding/below-floor/above-floor legs (pop-one mutant killed). README states the ambient-config trust boundary and the remote-use recipes.

## Closure evidence

Frozen checks C1-C10 (12/12 verify-checkpoint, anchor receipts v1-v5 on #46, semantics digest `18963773...` CONSTANT): all executable ACs RED/ERROR at base → GREEN at head (C8 PRESERVING GREEN-both). AC6 substitute transcript on #34; AC7/AC11 README pins executable. Full suite **718 tests OK** at the shipped head (672 at base); CI **9/9 green** (4x ubuntu + 4x windows + cubic); `scan-deferred` clean.

## Review findings resolved

Post-publication review raised **53 findings** — 20 normalized findings from
the swarm-pr-review (6 base lanes + 10 risk-family micro-lanes, 2 critic
passes, verdict REQUEST_CHANGES on two HIGH items) and 33 from four cubic
re-review runs (cubic re-reviews on every push, so each round was adjudicated
against the then-current head). **All 53 are FIXED in this PR; zero RECORD,
zero FILE, zero ASK.** The 20 swarm-pr-review findings are grouped by fix
area below (12 rows); each of the 33 cubic findings has its own row. Every
item is a defect this PR introduced, so the "fix in this PR" rule applies
throughout and nothing needed a follow-up issue. Each fix carries a
regression test, and the three production pins that guard a load-bearing
property were mutation-verified by reverting the fix and confirming the test
fails (CUB-14 install ordering, the URI fail-open, the bounded-decompression
spy).

| Finding | Source | Disposition | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| PRR-A (HIGH) — envelope escapes: TypeError/FileNotFound/Timeout/OSError bypassed the failure envelope | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| PRR-B — snapshot handlers bypassed resolve_db (ZAXBYGRAPH_DB / legacy fallback ignored) | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |

| PRR-E1-E4 — example workflow: no concurrency group, unpinned install, no prior-snapshot restore, unnecessary gh auth setup-git | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| PRR-F1/F2/F3 — sidecars deleted before the replace; replace faults unclassified; schema-less poison file created on a non-file --db | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |

| PRR-I1-I7 — CLI envelope legs ignored stderr; coded-refusal projection unpinned; multi-repo/repo-mismatch unpinned; POSIX reader leg non-discriminating; temp leaks | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |

| R3-3 — read-only file: URI built from a raw path silently skipped the multi-repo and newer-local guards | cubic run 3 | FIXED | `0dbe728` |
| R3-4 — the --force leg asserted only that the destination still existed | cubic run 3 | FIXED | `0dbe728` |
| R4-1 — check=True legs discarded git's stderr, so the cause was still lost | cubic run 4 | FIXED | `5d47b88` |

## Considered, not filed

| Item | Reason | Gate failed / re-evaluation trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `--verify-sample` compares a payload-level projection (title/body/state/timestamps/author/labels/pull-marker), not the issue's `content_hash` wording | children ride per-item REST endpoints and `item_events`/`pr_commits`/`issue_field_values` are GraphQL-only, so a REST-only re-fetch cannot faithfully reproduce them; any full-content comparison reported unchanged items as drift (final-critic rounds 2-3). CLI help states the compared field set | RECORD (disclosed semantics reduction; re-evaluate if a per-item child/GraphQL re-fetch becomes available) |
| AC6 evidence = live accepted-ref transcript + two hook-simulated fallback legs | the issue's substitute-evidence clause demands exactly the recorded push/ls-remote transcript; a live refusal probe is impossible (GitHub accepts custom refs) | RECORD (evidence composition; correction history on #34) |
| AC6 scratch repo not deleted | the gh token lacks `delete_repo` scope; repo is private and holds only the throwaway probe snapshot | RECORD + maintainer action (delete `zaxbysauce/zaxbygraph-ac6-probe`) |
| Platform-conditional active-reader test (Windows `dest_open` refusal / POSIX installs over a live reader) | platform file-locking semantics differ; each leg asserts real behavior (PR #42 convention); the quiesce failure falls through by design | RECORD |
| `wal_checkpoint` busy result not judged | observability is sqlite-build-dependent; the guarded OSError refusal is the single committed behavior | RECORD |
| Consolidation drops `snapshot.*` provenance | the merged corpus is not the pulled snapshot (plan s11; pinned by test) | RECORD |
| AC5 dual-leg (Windows + Linux) | closed by CI: both platforms green at the shipped head | CLOSED by the CI matrix |
| `db_sha`/`gz_sha` refusal legs, watermark/GIT-env pins, planted `--ls-files` leg | substance holds (part-sha/quick_check/schema refusal pinned); these specific legs are not pinned | RECORD |
| PR #45 ledger rows R7 / R9-C20 / R10-first-sub-row | superseded by this issue per #46's DoD | annotated superseded (no new filing) |

## Waivers (or none)

None. Every acceptance criterion passes on the evidence above; the disclosures above are RECORD rows, not waivers.

## Test plan

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → Ran 718 tests, OK at the shipped head.
- CI: 9/9 green (windows-latest + ubuntu-latest x 3.11/3.12/3.13/3.14, plus cubic).

- Reviewer/critic mutant probes: pop-one budget mutant killed by the new pins; projection-collapse mutant killed by the drift pins (failures=2); supp-isolation revert killed by the hermeticity pin; guard-narrowing killed by the corrupt-dest pin.

fix: review round 4 — restored staged-digest pin (lost to a block ove…

…rwrite), parts dict-entry leg, POSIX reader branch opens a reader, busy verdict dropped with disclosure

- test_pull_refuses_wrong_corpus_digest RESTORED: the round-3 rebuild
  silently replaced the block carrying it (the reviewer caught the loss;
  the round-4 message had claimed it restored). Mutant re-verified:
  deleting _check_staged_digest leaves the pin red.
- test_pull_refuses_malformed_parts now drives BOTH shapes (non-list
  and dict-missing-entry) — the dict-entry falsifier previously unpinned.
- The POSIX branch of the active-reader test now opens a real reader and
  asserts the install lands over it (the disclosed asymmetry is now
  exercised on both legs).
- The wal_checkpoint busy-verdict branch is REMOVED by design: its
  observability is sqlite-build-dependent and the mutant probe could not
  make the committed pin discriminate it on this box; the guarded
  OSError refusal is the single committed behavior (Windows refuses on
  open handles, POSIX installs over live readers — disclosed in the
  test), the checkpoint call remains as best-effort frame back-fill,
  and the reviewer's drop-it option is taken with the reason recorded.
- 08 counts corrected.

fix: swarm-pr-review fix round — snapshot transport hardening (PR #51)

Resolves all 20 normalized findings from the swarm-pr-review of PR #51
(16 lanes, 2 critic passes). Suite: 713 tests OK.

Transport correctness (snapshot.py):

- PRR-A: every reachable failure mode now exits through SnapshotError
  with a coded key. A manifest that decodes to null/scalar raises
  bad_manifest instead of TypeError; git transport faults (missing
  binary, timeout, OSError) are classified git_missing/git_timeout/
  git_failed rather than surfacing a traceback; destination-side
  replace faults classify winerror 17/EXDEV as dest_cross_volume and
  winerror 5/32 (EACCES/EBUSY/EPERM/ETXTBSY) as dest_open.
- PRR-C: pull() binds the destination. expected_repo/expected_host
  produce coded repo_mismatch/host_mismatch refusals, a store holding
  a second repo refuses as multi_repo_destination without --force,
  and _local_watermark is repo-scoped, returns None for a missing file
  and never creates one (mode=ro URI).
- PRR-D: publish and the staged verify both enforce the export
  user_version floor, so an old store is refused as store_too_old
  rather than publishing an unreadable corpus.
- PRR-G: staged decompression is bounded by PULL_MAX_DB_BYTES
  (snapshot_too_large); part descriptors must match the bytes actually
  received (part_size_mismatch) in addition to the sha.
- PRR-H: pull fetches every candidate ref and keeps malformed manifests
  as candidates with an empty watermark, so a corrupt SNAPSHOT_REF
  cannot mask a good one and bad_manifest is reachable.
- PRR-F3: publish refuses a non-file --db (no_corpus) before connecting,
  so a schema-less poison file can never become the snapshot.
- PRR-K: _run_git strips GIT_AUTHOR/GIT_COMMITTER identity env for
  determinism and configures gh's credential helper per invocation
  (no global git config, GH_TOKEN stays the only credential).

CLI (cli.py):

- PRR-B: snapshot handlers resolve the store through resolve_db
  (--db > ZAXBYGRAPH_DB > user store > legacy in-repo > would-be path)
  and pass expected_repo/expected_host down to pull.
- PRR-I2: SnapshotError ships code_key=exc.code, so coded refusals
  reach the machine envelope instead of collapsing to bad_request.

Example workflow (docs/examples/snapshot-publish.yml):

- PRR-E1-E4: concurrency group (no racing force-pushes), pinned
  commit-sha install in a token-less step, a restore-the-previous-
  snapshot step so scheduled runs sync incrementally, and no
  gh auth setup-git (the per-invocation credential config handles it).

Tests:

- PRR-I1/I2: CLI envelope legs assert an EMPTY stderr and one parseable
  six-key envelope; a new leg pins that a refusal carries the snapshot's
  code (repo_not_synced), not bad_request.
- PRR-I3/I4: multi-repo destination and repo-mismatch refusals are
  pinned byte-identical-before and --force-overridable.
- PRR-I5: the tamper descriptor now matches its junk bytes so
  part_sha_mismatch fires; new legs pin part_size_mismatch and
  bad_manifest for null/scalar manifests.
- PRR-I6: the POSIX reader leg mutates issues_since first so its
  watermark assertion cannot be pre-true.
- PRR-I7: module-level leg cwd/checkout temp dirs are registered with
  atexit in the five test modules that allocate them, so repeated
  suite runs do not accumulate directories.

Docs:

- README: --verify-sample scope states it compares stored item fields
  against the live payload and is not the content_hash a full re-sync
  would compute.

fix: review round 5 — corrupt-destination recovery, guard widened to …

…sqlite3.Error, docs/tests truth

- _install's quiesce guard now catches (OSError, sqlite3.Error): pull is
  the documented recovery path for a corrupt store, so an unreadable
  destination falls through to the guarded install and the validated
  snapshot replaces the unreadable bytes (was: unhandled
  sqlite3.DatabaseError traceback).
- New pin: test_pull_replaces_corrupt_destination (non-sqlite dest ->
  quick_check ok after the pull).
- _install docstring states the real contract (quiesce falls through by
  design; the guarded OSError is the committed refusal); the stale
  busy-verdict comment in the POSIX leg is corrected and the leg now
  asserts the snapshot watermark (discriminating, not just file
  existence).

fix: cubic re-review round 3 — bounded decompression, URI-safe read-o…

…nly opens

Cubic's third run on this branch raised four findings against the previous
head; three are new and fixed here, each pinned by a mutation-verified
regression test (both production pins were probed by reverting the fix and
confirming the test fails).

- The pull ceiling now bounds the ALLOCATION. PULL_MAX_DB_BYTES was checked
  after gzip.decompress had already produced the full expansion, so it
  capped nothing: a small published part that expands ~1030x could force an
  arbitrarily large allocation before the refusal fired. Decompression now
  streams through GzipFile.read(ceiling + 1), so the largest buffer this
  path can build is one byte over the ceiling. A test pins the property
  structurally by spying on gzip.decompress and asserting it is never
  called.
- The read-only opens are URI-safe. The file: URI was built from a raw
  path, so a destination containing '?', '#' or '%' made sqlite3.connect
  raise, and the caller's except branch silently returned - skipping the
  multi_repo_destination and local_newer guards with no signal, i.e. a
  whole-file replace could drop another repo's corpus. Both guards now
  open through _open_readonly(), which uses Path.as_uri() to percent-
  encode the path. The regression test drives a genuine two-repo
  destination at a '%..#...' path and asserts the refusal still fires.
- The --force leg of the multi-repo test asserted only that the destination
  still existed, which was already true. It now asserts the bytes changed
  and that sync_state holds only the snapshot's repo.

Suite: 718 tests OK. CI 7/8 green at the previous head (windows 3.13/3.14
still running).

fix: review round 6 — the POSIX reader leg asserts the manifest water…

…mark (no fixture literal)

old order fails it). The other six were already fixed by 04d6724.

  previously ran after _install(), so a gh/source fault raised a refusal
  envelope for a pull whose store had already been replaced - the
  envelope promised nothing was replaced when it had been. A drift
  report is not a fault and still rides along in the result.

  land"; by then os.replace has committed, so it now says the store was
  already replaced and must be re-pulled or restored.

  missing or misconfigured git fails at the fixture, not three tests
  later; _cli_json asserts the exit code and reports stderr/stdout
  instead of raising JSONDecodeError on an empty stdout.

Closes #34. Closes #46.

Collated trace `34-46-snapshot-config-hardening` (user-authorized multi-issue PR per the 2026-11-01 directive; precedent PR #50). Base `f00d38b`, head `5d47b88` (critic-approved `ddf1070` + the CI-identity fix `2609692` + four post-publication review-fix commits `04d6724`, `99f62f0`, `0dbe728`, `5d47b88`), 20 files, +2736/-30. Full protocol: plan-critic 5 rounds (APPROVE), implementation reviewer 7 rounds (APPROVE), final critic 6 rounds (all findings fixed).

## Summary

**#34 (Workstream E — verified store transport, new feature).** `snapshot publish` moves a store as a single orphan commit (manifest + gzip parts) to a target repo; `snapshot pull` stages-then-verifies and installs atomically under the sync lock. Every manifest field derives from one staged backup (completeness, watermark, schema, corpus digest); pull refuses tampered/oversized/newer-schema snapshots, protects a newer local store without `--force`, writes provenance into the staged db, and quiesces the destination before the single `os.replace`. `status` gains `data.snapshot`; consolidation drops `snapshot.*` provenance with disclosure. `--verify-sample N` re-fetches N random items and compares their stored fields for drift; `docs/examples/snapshot-publish.yml` is the scheduled single-writer workflow. AC6's live probe is recorded on #34 (comments 6565353565 + correction 6565943329: GitHub accepts `refs/zaxbygraph/*`; the branch fallback is pinned in-suite).

**#46 (derived-tier acceptance-gate integrity, defects).** The config chain (store `config.toml` → cwd `.zaxbygraph.toml` → `--config`) is now covered at all three levels with per-key precedence, per-name map merge and `config_source` labels for both public chain entry points. All derived-tier CLI leg runners execute in isolated cwds (temp dirs; a temp git checkout for the checkout-dependent `similar` legs) — a planted repo-root config can no longer reweight checks. `tests/test_triage_budget_pins.py` replaces C20's vacuous disjunction with binding/below-floor/above-floor legs (pop-one mutant killed). README states the ambient-config trust boundary and the remote-use recipes.

## Closure evidence

Frozen checks C1-C10 (12/12 verify-checkpoint, anchor receipts v1-v5 on #46, semantics digest `18963773...` CONSTANT): all executable ACs RED/ERROR at base → GREEN at head (C8 PRESERVING GREEN-both). AC6 substitute transcript on #34; AC7/AC11 README pins executable. Full suite **718 tests OK** at the shipped head (672 at base); CI **9/9 green** (4x ubuntu + 4x windows + cubic); `scan-deferred` clean.

## Review findings resolved

Post-publication review raised **53 findings** — 20 normalized findings from
the swarm-pr-review (6 base lanes + 10 risk-family micro-lanes, 2 critic
passes, verdict REQUEST_CHANGES on two HIGH items) and 33 from four cubic
re-review runs (cubic re-reviews on every push, so each round was adjudicated
against the then-current head). **All 53 are FIXED in this PR; zero RECORD,
zero FILE, zero ASK.** The 20 swarm-pr-review findings are grouped by fix
area below (12 rows); each of the 33 cubic findings has its own row. Every
item is a defect this PR introduced, so the "fix in this PR" rule applies
throughout and nothing needed a follow-up issue. Each fix carries a
regression test, and the three production pins that guard a load-bearing
property were mutation-verified by reverting the fix and confirming the test
fails (CUB-14 install ordering, the URI fail-open, the bounded-decompression
spy).

| Finding | Source | Disposition | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|
| PRR-A (HIGH) — envelope escapes: TypeError/FileNotFound/Timeout/OSError bypassed the failure envelope | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| PRR-B — snapshot handlers bypassed resolve_db (ZAXBYGRAPH_DB / legacy fallback ignored) | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| PRR-C (HIGH) — pull never bound the destination: repo A's snapshot could replace repo B's store; watermark read was LIMIT 1 | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| PRR-D — pre-v10 store accepted, then raw sqlite error in the digest path | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| PRR-E1-E4 — example workflow: no concurrency group, unpinned install, no prior-snapshot restore, unnecessary gh auth setup-git | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| PRR-F1/F2/F3 — sidecars deleted before the replace; replace faults unclassified; schema-less poison file created on a non-file --db | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| PRR-G — unbounded decompression; part descriptor not checked against bytes received | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| PRR-H — a stale custom ref could mask a good snapshot | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| PRR-I1-I7 — CLI envelope legs ignored stderr; coded-refusal projection unpinned; multi-repo/repo-mismatch unpinned; POSIX reader leg non-discriminating; temp leaks | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| PRR-J — README --verify-sample scope omitted | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| PRR-K — git subprocess inherited ambient identity/config | swarm-pr-review | FIXED | `04d6724` |

| R2-5 — _leg_checkout ran git without checking return codes | cubic run 2 | FIXED | `99f62f0` |
| R2-6 — _cli_json decoded stdout without asserting the subprocess succeeded | cubic run 2 | FIXED | `99f62f0` |
| R2-7 — mkdtemp leak (test_triage_budget_pins) | cubic run 2 | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| R2-8 — mkdtemp leak (test_triage_bundle) | cubic run 2 | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| R2-9 — mkdtemp leak (test_triage_bundle_supp) | cubic run 2 | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| R2-10 — mkdtemp leak (test_triage_paging) | cubic run 2 | FIXED | `04d6724` |
| R3-1 — PULL_MAX_DB_BYTES checked after the expansion was already allocated | cubic run 3 | FIXED | `0dbe728` |
| R3-2 — resolve_db legacy fallback could publish another repo's corpus under the requested slug | cubic run 3 | FIXED | `99f62f0` |
| R3-3 — read-only file: URI built from a raw path silently skipped the multi-repo and newer-local guards | cubic run 3 | FIXED | `0dbe728` |
| R3-4 — the --force leg asserted only that the destination still existed | cubic run 3 | FIXED | `0dbe728` |
| R4-1 — check=True legs discarded git's stderr, so the cause was still lost | cubic run 4 | FIXED | `5d47b88` |

## Considered, not filed

| Item | Reason | Gate failed / re-evaluation trigger |
|---|---|---|
| `--verify-sample` compares a payload-level projection (title/body/state/timestamps/author/labels/pull-marker), not the issue's `content_hash` wording | children ride per-item REST endpoints and `item_events`/`pr_commits`/`issue_field_values` are GraphQL-only, so a REST-only re-fetch cannot faithfully reproduce them; any full-content comparison reported unchanged items as drift (final-critic rounds 2-3). CLI help states the compared field set | RECORD (disclosed semantics reduction; re-evaluate if a per-item child/GraphQL re-fetch becomes available) |
| AC6 evidence = live accepted-ref transcript + two hook-simulated fallback legs | the issue's substitute-evidence clause demands exactly the recorded push/ls-remote transcript; a live refusal probe is impossible (GitHub accepts custom refs) | RECORD (evidence composition; correction history on #34) |
| AC6 scratch repo not deleted | the gh token lacks `delete_repo` scope; repo is private and holds only the throwaway probe snapshot | RECORD + maintainer action (delete `zaxbysauce/zaxbygraph-ac6-probe`) |
| Platform-conditional active-reader test (Windows `dest_open` refusal / POSIX installs over a live reader) | platform file-locking semantics differ; each leg asserts real behavior (PR #42 convention); the quiesce failure falls through by design | RECORD |
| `wal_checkpoint` busy result not judged | observability is sqlite-build-dependent; the guarded OSError refusal is the single committed behavior | RECORD |
| Consolidation drops `snapshot.*` provenance | the merged corpus is not the pulled snapshot (plan s11; pinned by test) | RECORD |
| AC5 dual-leg (Windows + Linux) | closed by CI: both platforms green at the shipped head | CLOSED by the CI matrix |
| `db_sha`/`gz_sha` refusal legs, watermark/GIT-env pins, planted `--ls-files` leg | substance holds (part-sha/quick_check/schema refusal pinned); these specific legs are not pinned | RECORD |
| PR #45 ledger rows R7 / R9-C20 / R10-first-sub-row | superseded by this issue per #46's DoD | annotated superseded (no new filing) |

## Waivers (or none)

None. Every acceptance criterion passes on the evidence above; the disclosures above are RECORD rows, not waivers.

## Test plan

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → Ran 718 tests, OK at the shipped head.
- CI: 9/9 green (windows-latest + ubuntu-latest x 3.11/3.12/3.13/3.14, plus cubic).

- Reviewer/critic mutant probes: pop-one budget mutant killed by the new pins; projection-collapse mutant killed by the drift pins (failures=2); supp-isolation revert killed by the hermeticity pin; guard-narrowing killed by the corrupt-dest pin.

item.body:
*Provenance: generated from the 2026-11-03 post-merge survey of this repository (every tracked issue closed except the tracking epics; remaining work found by an executed-probe sweep of the migration/consolidation surface — probe artifacts under `.zcode/pr-review/survey-c4/` in the maintainer's local checkout, NOT part of this repository; every claim below is re-derivable from the cited source). Every claim was re-checked against origin/main at anchor commit `f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b` on 2026-11-03 by source read and executed probes. One issue = one PR; the two issues filed in this survey share ONE user-authorized multi-issue PR (maintainer directive 2026-11-03; precedent PR #50/#51), each acceptance criterion independently frozen and verified, and the PR stays reviewable because the four fixes are small and touch disjoint functions.*

## Summary

`doctor` becomes trustworthy on exactly the stores it exists to repair. Today it copies candidate DBs with `shutil.copy2` — the main file only — so a candidate whose writer was killed before a clean close (a crashed `sync`, the crash-recovery path issue #1 exists for) is either invisible to `doctor` or, worse, adopted and used to REPLACE the store's richer corpus with a truncated copy. And a candidate carrying one slug under two casings aborts the whole adoption with a raw `UNIQUE constraint failed` error, because the consolidation copy has no folded-key dedupe and the v1→v2 collision cleanup only covers the five tables that existed at v1. After this PR: a crash-damaged candidate is copied faithfully (its committed WAL frames included), a case-split candidate is adopted or cleanly reported, and the collision cleanup covers every repo-keyed item-scoped table the schema has today.

## Problem (claims to verify)

1. **`doctor` copies candidates with `shutil.copy2`, which copies only the main database file — never the `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars.** `VERIFIED` — source trace plus two executed probes at the anchor commit. The module docstring already knows the candidates are WAL-mode stores, [`src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py` L3–L8](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L3-L8):

   ```python
   `doctor` reports every legacy per-checkout DB holding the resolved slug;
   `doctor --consolidate` copies the freshest COMPLETE corpus into the
   user-level store. Originals are never modified or deleted: inspection and
   adoption always work on temp copies (a mode=ro open of a WAL-mode DB would
   still materialize -shm/-wal beside the original, so even inspection goes
   through a copy).
   ```

   …but both copy sites copy the main file only. [`inspect`](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L90-L96), L90–L96:

   ```python
   def inspect(path: Path, repo: str) -> dict | None:
       """Per-DB stats for one slug, read from a temp copy. None = unreadable."""
       repo_l = repo.lower()
       with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
           copy = Path(td) / path.name
           try:
               shutil.copy2(path, copy)
   ```

   …and [`_MigratedCopy.__init__`](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L155-L159), L155–L159:

   ```python
       def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
           self._td = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="zaxbygraph-doctor-")
           try:
               self.path = Path(self._td) / path.name
               shutil.copy2(path, self.path)
   ```

   Every store this tool creates is WAL-mode ([`db.py` L59](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L59): `conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL")`). Executed probe (`probe_wal_kill.py`): a 10-item candidate whose writer process was killed after commit (`os._exit` before clean close — exactly a Ctrl-C'd/crashed `sync`) is copied to a 4096-byte main file; `inspect()`'s items query raises `sqlite3.DatabaseError`, `inspect()` returns `None`, and `doctor` skips the candidate while still reporting `{"ok": true, ...}` with the candidate absent from `scanned`.

2. **`consolidate` is REPLACE-THE-SLUG, so a truncated candidate destroys the store's corpus.** `VERIFIED` — source trace plus executed probe. [`src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py` L233–L240](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L233-L240) deletes every store row for the folded slug, then inserts the candidate's rows:

   ```python
               dst.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
               try:
                   for table, autoinc_pk in _COPY_TABLES:
                       if table == "revisions":
                           continue  # per-item scoping below (issue #40)
                       dst.execute(
                           f"DELETE FROM {table} WHERE repo = ?", (repo_l,)
                       )
   ```

   The docstring commits to plain inserts, [L198–L200](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L198-L200):

   ```python
       ids (items.id, releases.id, reviews.id). sync_state is replaced and counts recomputed. Plain
       INSERTs only: post-delete there is nothing to conflict with, and
       INSERT OR REPLACE's double-unique semantics could silently drop rows.
   ```

   Executed probe (`probe_wal_copy2.py`): a store holding 30 items for `owner/repo` consolidating a 10-item candidate whose last 5 committed items live only in the `-wal` ends holding **5** items (`STORE items AFTER: 5`), with the doctor reporting the candidate as `"items": 5, "complete": true, "adopted": true`. The store's corpus is silently replaced by the truncated copy until the next full sync.

3. **Consolidation's row copy has no folded-key dedupe.** `VERIFIED` — source trace plus executed probe. [`src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py` L333–L343](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L333-L343) selects `lower(repo)` and plain-`INSERT`s the candidate's rows; "post-delete there is nothing to conflict with" holds against the store's deleted rows but not against the candidate's OWN rows folding onto one key:

   ```python
                       rows = src.execute(
                           f"SELECT {select_cols} FROM {table}"
                           + (" WHERE lower(repo) = ?" if "repo" in cols else "")
                           + order_by,
                           (repo_l,) if "repo" in cols else (),
                       ).fetchall()
                       insert_sql = (
                           f"INSERT INTO {table} ({', '.join(cols)}) "
                           f"VALUES ({placeholders})"
                       )
                       dst.executemany(insert_sql, [tuple(r) for r in rows])
   ```

   Executed probe (`build_legacy.py` + CLI): a candidate at user_version 11 carrying one slug under two casings aborts the whole adoption with `error: UNIQUE constraint failed: items.repo, items.number`; the same candidate shaped at the v1 slot with dual-cased `assignees` rows aborts with `UNIQUE constraint failed: assignees.repo, assignees.number, assignees.login`. (A 2026-10-03 field note recorded the same crash on `labels.repo, labels.number, labels.name`; that exact symptom no longer reproduces for a genuine v1-era DB because the v1→v2 fold dedupes the tables it covers — the root cause in claim 4 is what remains, and claim 3's missing dedupe is why it still aborts.)

4. **`_drop_collision_losers` covers only the five v1-era tables.** `VERIFIED` — source trace. [`src/zaxbygraph/db.py` L264–L274](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L264-L274) deletes the loser's children from `labels`, `comments`, `reviews`, `pr_files`, `edges` only:

   ```python
           nid = str(number)
           for (casing,) in loser_casings:
               conn.execute("DELETE FROM labels WHERE repo = ? AND number = ?", (casing, number))
               conn.execute("DELETE FROM comments WHERE repo = ? AND number = ?", (casing, number))
               conn.execute("DELETE FROM reviews WHERE repo = ? AND number = ?", (casing, number))
               conn.execute("DELETE FROM pr_files WHERE repo = ? AND number = ?", (casing, number))
               conn.execute(
                   "DELETE FROM edges WHERE repo = ? AND ("
                   "(src_type = 'item' AND src_id = ?) OR (dst_type = 'item' AND dst_id = ?))",
                   (casing, nid, nid),
               )
   ```

   The repo-keyed item-scoped tables added after v2 — `assignees` and `issue_field_values`, created in `migrate_v6_to_v7` at [`db.py` L782–L791](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L782-L791) — plus `revisions` (v8), `item_path_refs`/`item_signatures` (v9) and `item_events`/`pr_commits` (v10), get neither fold nor loser-deletion:

   ```python
       conn.execute(
           "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS assignees ("
           "repo TEXT NOT NULL, number INTEGER NOT NULL, login TEXT NOT NULL,"
           " PRIMARY KEY (repo, number, login))"
       )
       conn.execute(
           "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS issue_field_values ("
           "repo TEXT NOT NULL, number INTEGER NOT NULL, field_name TEXT NOT NULL,"
           " value TEXT, PRIMARY KEY (repo, number, field_name))"
       )
   ```

   That contradicts the documented contract, [`docs/schema.md` L527–L531](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b/docs/schema.md#L527-L531):

   ```text
   Migration 1→2 adds `sync_state.full_sync_pending` and folds repo slugs to
   lowercase across every repo-keyed table, merging case-split duplicates
   (freshest row per folded key; `sync_state` timestamps take MAX; distinct-id
   `(repo, number)` collisions keep the freshest item and delete the losers'
   number-scoped rows under their own casing). For a legacy row whose
   ```

   Prior-art reconciliation: the consolidation path DOES enumerate all of them — [`doctor.py` L51–L70](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b/src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py#L51-L70) `_COPY_TABLES`:

   ```python
   _COPY_TABLES = (
       ("items", None),
       ("labels", None),
       ("assignees", None),
       ("issue_field_values", None),
       ("comments", "pk"),
       ("reviews", None),
       ("pr_files", None),
       ("releases", None),
       ("edges", "id"),
       ("fetch_log", "id"),
       ("revisions", "id"),
       # v9 text-derived references (issue #26) and v10 events/commits
       # (issue #27): composite-keyed item-scoped children, so consolidation
       # must copy them like the other child tables or silently drop history.
       ("item_path_refs", None),
       ("item_signatures", None),
       ("item_events", None),
       ("pr_commits", None),
   )
   ```

   — so the tables were known to be repo-keyed when that list was written; this PR extends the migration's cleanup to match, it does not invent a mechanism. This is also PR #50's ASK-ledger item 1 (critic recommendation on record: "FILE as its own small migration-integrity issue").

## Scope

In: faithful candidate copies in `doctor` (WAL sidecars or the SQLite backup API, following the in-repo precedent at [`snapshot.py` L216–L220](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/f28e4b43a40688c3b47bf0f162befd04ece9270b/src/zaxbygraph/snapshot.py#L216-L220), which uses `conn.backup(dst)`); folded-key-safe adoption in `consolidate`; `_drop_collision_losers` coverage of the post-v2 item-scoped tables; regression tests for each.

Out: `snapshot publish/pull` (already uses the backup API and `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`); the replace-the-slug semantics of consolidation for well-formed candidates; the derived read tier; the `_fold_sync_state` pre-v4 column list (verified unreachable: at `user_version < 2` the v4+ columns do not exist yet).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1: WHEN `doctor` inspects a candidate whose committed rows live in an un-checkpointed `-wal` sidecar, THE SYSTEM SHALL report the candidate's true item count instead of dropping it as unreadable.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_doctor_wal_copy.py" -k test_inspect_sees_wal_committed_rows -b
  - expect: FAIL at base — the killed-writer candidate is absent from `scanned` (`inspect()` returns None on `no such table: items`, probe-verified); the check builds the same crash-damaged candidate and asserts the reported count.
  - files: tests/test_doctor_wal_copy.py, src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py
  - why: `shutil.copy2` at doctor.py:96 copies the main file only; rows committed after the last checkpoint live in the `-wal` and vanish from the copy.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN `doctor --consolidate` adopts a candidate whose committed rows live in an un-checkpointed `-wal` sidecar, THE SYSTEM SHALL adopt the candidate's full corpus so the store is not truncated.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_doctor_wal_copy.py" -k test_consolidate_adopts_wal_committed_rows -b
  - expect: FAIL at base — `STORE items AFTER: 5` for a 10-item candidate (the store's 30-item corpus replaced by the truncated copy, probe-verified); the check asserts the full corpus survives.
  - files: tests/test_doctor_wal_copy.py, src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py
  - why: `_MigratedCopy` (doctor.py:159) copies the main file only, and consolidate is replace-the-slug (doctor.py:233-240).
- [ ] AC3: WHEN `doctor --consolidate` adopts a candidate carrying the same (repo, number) under two casings, THE SYSTEM SHALL complete the adoption with one folded row set instead of aborting on a UNIQUE constraint failure.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_doctor_consolidate_fold.py" -k test_dual_casing_candidate_adopts -b
  - expect: FAIL at base — `error: UNIQUE constraint failed: assignees.repo, assignees.number, assignees.login` aborts the adoption (probe-verified); the check builds the dual-cased candidate and asserts one row per folded key.
  - files: tests/test_doctor_consolidate_fold.py, src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py
  - why: doctor.py:333-343 plain-INSERTs `lower(repo)`-selected rows with no conflict clause, so the candidate's own folded duplicates collide.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN `migrate_v1_to_v2` resolves a distinct-id `(repo, number)` collision, THE SYSTEM SHALL delete the loser's number-scoped rows in every repo-keyed item-scoped table, including the post-v2 ones.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_migrations.py" -k test_collision_losers_cover_all_repo_keyed_tables -b
  - expect: FAIL at base — loser-casing rows survive in `assignees`/`issue_field_values`/`revisions`/`item_path_refs`/`item_signatures`/`item_events`/`pr_commits` (probe-verified shape); the check asserts zero survivor rows under the loser casing in every repo-keyed table.
  - files: tests/test_migrations.py, src/zaxbygraph/db.py
  - why: db.py:266-274 lists five tables; the seven post-v2 item-scoped tables are omitted, against docs/schema.md:527-531's "every repo-keyed table" contract.
- [ ] AC5: WHILE consolidation runs on well-formed and genuine case-split candidates, THE SYSTEM SHALL keep its documented semantics: genuine v1-era case-split DBs adopt cleanly, revisions stay per-item scoped, and a same-candidate re-adoption is a no-op.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_migrations.py" -b
  - expect: GREEN at base and head — the existing migration/consolidation/revisions/idempotency pins, plus the executed counter-probe that a genuine v1-schema case-split DB adopts cleanly (both the folded-items and delete-and-recreate shapes).
  - files: tests/test_migrations.py, tests/test_consolidate_revisions.py, src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py, src/zaxbygraph/db.py
  - why: regression floor — the fix must not change adoption semantics for candidates the tool can produce (the counter-probe at base: `adopted: true, items: 1, complete: true`).

## Design

1. Faithful copy: replace both `shutil.copy2` sites with a copy that includes live WAL content — either copy `path`, `path-wal`, `path-shm` together (the sidecars must be copied while no writer is active; the candidate is a legacy DB no live process owns, but a concurrent writer is possible), or open the candidate and use the SQLite online backup API (`sqlite3.Connection.backup`) into the temp copy, which folds WAL content in without touching the original. The backup API matches the `snapshot.py` precedent; the sidecar copy matches the module docstring's existing reasoning. Either way the copy must be verified by reading a row count from it before inspection proceeds (a still-unreadable copy keeps today's `None` path).
2. Folded-key-safe adoption: the copy loop inserts with a folded-key conflict policy — either delete-then-insert per folded key before the bulk copy, or an upsert whose conflict target is the table's real PK/unique key, chosen per table from `PRAGMA table_info` + the schema's declared keys. The choice must preserve the documented idempotency (a same-candidate re-adoption writes no rows) and the revisions per-item scoping.
3. Collision coverage: extend the per-loser DELETE loop to every repo-keyed item-scoped table, guarded by table existence so the migration stays portable if the chain is re-ordered. A blind `UPDATE ... SET repo = lower(repo)` is NOT safe for the composite-PK tables (identical `(number, origin, path)` rows under both casings would collide) — the loser's rows are deleted, the winner's are kept, exactly as for the v1-era five.

## Dependencies

Depends on: none. Blocks: none. Gated on: none.

## Files to change

- `src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py` — faithful candidate copy (both sites), folded-key-safe adoption copy.
- `src/zaxbygraph/db.py` — `_drop_collision_losers` table coverage.
- `tests/test_doctor_wal_copy.py` (new), `tests/test_doctor_consolidate_fold.py` (new), `tests/test_migrations.py` (new case).
- `docs/schema.md` — only if the fold- or consolidation-semantics wording needs a correction (the ACs above bind; docs follow the code).

## Local verification recipe

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s tests -b
python -m zaxbygraph doctor --repo owner/repo --consolidate --db <store> --scan <dir> --format json
```

## Definition of done

All five ACs pass with the frozen-check replay recorded (base RED for the right reason, head GREEN); the full suite is green; the recurrence sweep dispositions every hit of the "copy/fold assumes a quiescent, well-formed, single-cased store" class; independent implementation review and final critic both APPROVE on the shipped head SHA; the PR body carries the `## Waivers (or none)` heading.
