item.title: [Workstream A] PR 2 of 3: One comment can no longer wedge sync, and sync stops recording deletions that did not happen or missing ones that did

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the first-class review of 2026-11-09 (`docs/reports/2026-11-09-first-class-review.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`): a hands-on run of the tool against this repository's own 63 issues and PRs, plus three independent code reviews whose probes were re-run before filing. Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main 6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7 on 2026-11-09 by an executed probe or a source trace (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 878 tests ... OK (skipped=3)`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #64._

## Summary
After this PR (migration v12):
- `closes_keyword` comes only from text GitHub itself honours: PR descriptions and commit messages.
- References inside code spans, comment ids, and other repositories' numbers no longer become edges.
- Every actor carries an `is_bot` flag that read commands can filter on.
- Ingesting an issue no longer scans every PR's branch name.

## Problem (claims to verify)
Measured on the real store of this repository (63 items); the recomputed edges match the stored edges exactly.

1. **20% of `closes_keyword` edges come from text GitHub never honours.** Of 41 edges, 8 come from issue bodies, comments or reviews. The comment-derived ones are all wrong: PR 14→#5, 14→#2, 41→#7, 58→#1. PR 58→#1 comes from a bot comment quoting a diff line that contains `` `closes #1` ``. [VERIFIED by probe, re-run, and by query on the store.]
   [extract.py#L291-L300](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/extract.py#L291-L300)
   ```py
       closed_locations = iter_closing_locations(body, repo, f"comment:{cid}")
       closed = {n for n, _ in closed_locations}
       for n, location in closed_locations:
           if n != number:
               edges.append(
                   (
                       "item",
                       str(number),
                       "closes_keyword",
                       "item",
   ```
2. **21 of 362 `mentions` edges point at items that do not exist.** Seven are comment ids (`comment #6732496263`), twelve are another repository's numbers written with a space (`ZaxbyHub/ragappv3 #308`), and ten exist only inside code. [VERIFIED by probe, re-run.]
3. **Nothing in the tool knows what a bot is.** 599 of 1,260 comments and reviews in this store are bot-authored (`cubic-dev-ai[bot]`, `Copilot`); 99 of 168 `commented`/`reviewed` edges have bot actors; 33 `mentions` exist only because of bot text. [VERIFIED by probe, re-run; `grep` for `is_bot` or `[bot]` in `src/` finds nothing.]
4. **Every issue ingest scans every PR `head_ref` in the repository and tokenizes each in Python.** [VERIFIED by timing: issue re-ingest costs 5.3 / 11.2 / 30.4 ms at 1k / 3k / 10k PRs while PR re-ingest stays at 3–4 ms.]
   [store.py#L1021-L1026](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L1021-L1026)
   ```py
           for row in conn.execute(
               "SELECT number, head_ref FROM items INDEXED BY idx_items_repo_head"
               " WHERE repo = ? AND kind = 'pr' AND head_ref IS NOT NULL AND number != ?",
               (repo, nid),
           ).fetchall():
               tokens = branch_number_tokens(row["head_ref"])
   ```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN a closing keyword appears in an issue body, a comment, or a review THE SYSTEM SHALL record `mentions` for it and never `closes_keyword`; closing keywords in a PR description or commit message SHALL keep producing `closes_keyword`.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_extract_noise.py -q -k test_closing_keywords_only_from_pr_body_and_commits`
  - expect: FAIL: a comment `fixes #5` yields `closes_keyword` (observed on the real store).
  - files: tests/test_extract_noise.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 1.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN a `#N` token sits inside inline code, a fenced block, a diff hunk, or a `>` quote THE SYSTEM SHALL emit no edge for it.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_extract_noise.py -q -k test_references_inside_code_are_ignored`
  - expect: FAIL: a quoted diff line containing `closes #1` yields an edge.
  - files: tests/test_extract_noise.py
  - why: RED at base per claims 1–2.
- [ ] AC3: WHEN text says `comment #<id>` or `<owner>/<repo> #N` for another repository THE SYSTEM SHALL emit no local edge.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_extract_noise.py -q -k test_comment_ids_and_spaced_foreign_refs_dropped`
  - expect: FAIL: `mentions` edges to items 6732496263 and 308 (probe-observed).
  - files: tests/test_extract_noise.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 2.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN an actor's login ends in `[bot]`, or its payload `type` is `Bot`, or it is in the configured bot list THE SYSTEM SHALL store `actors.is_bot = 1`, backfilled by migration v12 from stored payloads.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_extract_noise.py -q -k test_actors_carry_is_bot`
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_extract_noise.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_extract_noise.py
  - why: No column at base.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN an issue is ingested THE SYSTEM SHALL find branch-linked PRs by an indexed equality lookup on a stored branch token, with per-item cost flat between 1k and 10k PRs (VDBE step count within 1.25×).
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_extract_noise.py -q -k test_branch_lookup_is_indexed`
  - expect: FAIL: plan is `SEARCH items USING INDEX idx_items_repo_head (repo=? AND head_ref>?)`; step count grows about 6×.
  - files: tests/test_extract_noise.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 4.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN migration v12 runs on a v11 store THE SYSTEM SHALL re-derive keyword edges under the new rules from stored text, with no GitHub calls, and keep every `timeline`, `closing_ref` and `link` edge.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_extract_noise.py -q -k test_v12_rederives_keyword_edges`
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_extract_noise.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_extract_noise.py
  - why: No v12 at base.
- [ ] AC7: WHEN the relation registry is checked THE SYSTEM SHALL still classify and document every relation.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_relation_registry.py -q -k test_`
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_relation_registry.py
  - why: GREEN at base.

## Scope
**In:** the extraction rules above, `is_bot`, the branch-token column and index, migration v12, `docs/schema.md`. Streaming cursors in the v7/v9/v12 backfills in place of `.fetchall()` on whole tables.
**Out:** using `is_bot` in scoring and reads (#69, #71).

**Decision recorded in the epic:** this narrows the AGENTS rule "mentions and closes from comments roll up to the owning item" to mentions only. The PR amends `AGENTS.md` accordingly.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: #66
- Schema after: none (v12 is the lane head of this program)

`src/zaxbygraph/extract.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/store.py` (hotspot), `src/zaxbygraph/db.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/schema.sql`, `AGENTS.md`, `docs/schema.md`, new `tests/test_extract_noise.py`.

item.title: [Workstream A] PR 3 of 3: Keyword edges stop inventing closures and mentions, bots are identifiable, and issue ingest stops scanning every PR branch

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the first-class review of 2026-11-09 (`docs/reports/2026-11-09-first-class-review.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`): a hands-on run of the tool against this repository's own 63 issues and PRs, plus three independent code reviews whose probes were re-run before filing. Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main 6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7 on 2026-11-09 by an executed probe or a source trace (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 878 tests ... OK (skipped=3)`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #64._

## Summary
After this PR, `eval` replays the real `triage` and `bundle` on the backlog as it stood before each historical fix PR, and scores what they proposed against what was fixed together. It works on REST-synced stores. Every metric is reported next to a naive baseline, so a number that looks good but is not can be seen. `triage --as-of T` and `bundle --as-of T` expose the same as-of view to agents.

This PR changes no scoring. It exists so that #69 can be judged.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **`eval bundle` does not run `bundle`.** It scores `similar`'s top five candidates per target. With five proposals against roughly one true partner, precision is structurally capped near 0.13, and the greedy selection, floor, anchors and triage weighting are never exercised. [VERIFIED by source trace:]
   [evaluate.py#L580-L586](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/evaluate.py#L580-L586)
   ```py
           # The proposal set is the tier's top-5 VISIBLE issue candidates: the
           # visibility filter runs before the width cut, so post-creation PRs
           # and future items can never consume the slots (pr43 review
           # PRR-006's bundle half).
           top = [c["number"] for c in visible[:5]]
           for number in top:
               proposed.add(frozenset((target, number)))
   ```

                   if not allow_shared_files and (cand_files & used_files):

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the first-class review of 2026-11-09 (`docs/reports/2026-11-09-first-class-review.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`): a hands-on run of the tool against this repository's own 63 issues and PRs, plus three independent code reviews whose probes were re-run before filing. Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main 6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7 on 2026-11-09 by an executed probe or a source trace (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 878 tests ... OK (skipped=3)`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #64._

## Summary
After this PR, every `sql` query has a time and size limit, a failed background refresh cannot turn a complete store into a "broken" one or spawn a retry storm, the server never waits on a client capability the client did not declare, and the common reads are bounded and can leave out bot text.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **`sql` has no time, step or size cap.** [VERIFIED, re-run before filing: `zaxbygraph sql "WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM c) SELECT count(*) FROM c"` is still running when killed by `timeout`; over MCP the single-threaded server stops answering everything, `ping` included. `SELECT * FROM comments` at the default limit of 200 returns 1.96 MB (about 480k tokens). `SELECT randomblob(10)` fails with `Object of type bytes is not JSON serializable`.] No `set_progress_handler` exists in `src/`.
   [query.py#L1339-L1344](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L1339-L1344)
   ```py
   def run_sql(conn: sqlite3.Connection, sql: str, limit: int = 200, repo: str | None = None) -> dict:
       assert_read_sql(sql)
       limit = _clamp_fetch_limit(limit)
       cur = conn.cursor()
       try:
           cur.execute(sql)
   ```
2. **A stale MCP read can poison a healthy store.** Every stale read starts a background sync; when it fails, `last_error` is written and `complete` flips to false on a store that was complete, `refreshing: true` is still reported, and each further read starts another job. [VERIFIED by probe, re-run: six `graph_status` reads one second apart produced failed jobs `sync-1…sync-5`; read 0 reported `complete: True`, read 1 onward `complete: False`; the database bytes changed.] The tools involved are annotated `readOnlyHint: true`.
   [mcp_server.py#L555-L559](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py#L555-L559)
   ```py
       age = fresh.get("age_s")
       if age is not None and age > ctx.stale_after_s:
           try:
               _start_job(db_path, slug, ctx.sync_runner)
               fresh["refreshing"] = True
   ```
3. **A repo-less call blocks the server on `roots/list` even when the client declared no roots capability.** [VERIFIED by probe: after `initialize` with `capabilities: {}`, `tools/call graph_status {}` emits a server-initiated `roots/list` and a following `ping` gets no reply.]
   [mcp_server.py#L356](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py#L356)
   ```py
       _send(ctx.stdout, {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": req_id, "method": "roots/list"})
   ```
4. **The most common read is unbounded and mostly bot text.** `item 51` is 107,898 chars (about 27k tokens); 81% of its comment text is from `cubic-dev-ai[bot]` and `Copilot`. `--max-comments 5` still returns 12k tokens because reviews and the body are uncapped, with `truncated: false`. MCP `get_item` has no comment cap at all (17k tokens of text for item 49, 35k on the wire). MCP `related` at its maximum depth returns about 75k tokens with no cap. [VERIFIED by measurement on the real store.]

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: IF a `sql` query runs past a deadline (default 5 s, configurable) THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL interrupt it and return a coded `timeout` error, on both the CLI and MCP, leaving the server responsive.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_surface_safety.py -q -k test_sql_deadline`
  - expect: FAIL: the recursive query never returns (killed by timeout, observed).
  - files: tests/test_surface_safety.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 1.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN a `sql` result exceeds a byte budget THE SYSTEM SHALL stop fetching, set `truncated: true`, cap oversized cells, and encode bytes values as hex.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_surface_safety.py -q -k test_sql_byte_budget_and_bytes`
  - expect: FAIL: 1.96 MB returned; `randomblob` raises a serialization error.
  - files: tests/test_surface_safety.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 1.
- [ ] AC3: IF a background refresh fails THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL leave `complete` and `last_error` of a previously complete store unchanged, report `freshness.refresh_failed` with the reason, and not start another refresh for that store until a backoff has elapsed.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_surface_safety.py -q -k test_failed_refresh_does_not_poison_or_storm`
  - expect: FAIL: `complete` flips to False and five jobs start in six reads (probe-observed).
  - files: tests/test_surface_safety.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 2.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN a legacy client did not declare the roots capability THE SYSTEM SHALL never send `roots/list`; it SHALL resolve from the server pin or working directory, or return a `bad_request` naming `repo`.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_surface_safety.py -q -k test_no_roots_request_without_capability`
  - expect: FAIL: the server emits `roots/list` and stops answering (probe-observed).
  - files: tests/test_surface_safety.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 3.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN `item` or MCP `get_item` runs with defaults THE SYSTEM SHALL return at most a bounded number of comments and reviews and bounded body text, report `comments_omitted` and `reviews_omitted`, and set `truncated: true` when anything was cut.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_surface_safety.py -q -k test_item_is_bounded_by_default`
  - expect: FAIL: 107,898 chars for item 51; `truncated: false` with 61 comments omitted.
  - files: tests/test_surface_safety.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 4.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN `--no-bots` (CLI) or `exclude_bots: true` (MCP) is passed to `item`, `search` or `brief` THE SYSTEM SHALL omit content authored by actors with `is_bot = 1` and report how much was omitted.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_surface_safety.py -q -k test_reads_can_exclude_bots`
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_surface_safety.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_surface_safety.py
  - why: No flag at base; `is_bot` comes from #67.
- [ ] AC7: WHEN MCP `related` would exceed a node or byte budget THE SYSTEM SHALL stop expanding and set `truncated: true`.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_surface_safety.py -q -k test_related_is_bounded`
  - expect: FAIL: depth 5 returns about 650 KB with `truncated: false`.
  - files: tests/test_surface_safety.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 4.
- [ ] AC8: WHEN any write, attach, pragma or extension is attempted through `sql` THE SYSTEM SHALL keep refusing it.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_query.py -q -k test_run_sql_negative_limit_is_clamped`
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_query.py
  - why: GREEN at base; the progress handler must not weaken either read-only layer (AGENTS).
- [ ] AC9: WHEN a stale read happens and the refresh succeeds THE SYSTEM SHALL answer immediately and refresh in the background, as today.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_mcp.py -q -k test_stale_read_answers_now_and_refreshes_in_background`
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_mcp.py
  - why: GREEN at base.

## Scope
**In:** progress-handler deadline and byte budget for `sql`; refresh failure isolation and backoff; roots capability check; bounded `item`/`get_item`/`related`; bot exclusion on reads; `BrokenPipeError` handled in `main` (piping any command to `head` prints a traceback today).
**Out:** result honesty and typed schemas (#72).

## Sequence
[Workstream C] A safe and honest agent surface: #71 -> #72 (this issue is C-01).

## Dependencies
- Depends on: #67 for AC6 only (`is_bot`); AC1–AC5 and AC7 are independent and may merge first if AC6 is split to the rebase
- Schema after: none
- Gated on: none

## Files expected to change
`src/zaxbygraph/query.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/db.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/cli.py`, `README.md`, `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md`, `docs/schema.md`, new `tests/test_surface_safety.py`.

## Definition of done
All ACs pass on every CI leg (Windows and Linux). The PR body says `Closes #<n>` and carries `## Closure evidence` with each AC's argv and result.

Agent claim released: PR #78 MERGED as 36d4bb4111995a5ce59d844984e6619fde384321 (squash, 2026-11-13T21:53:14Z), closing #72. Session 851890b2fa2d1496f1c30f2bcd851fa4 is done with this issue.

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the first-class review of 2026-11-09 (`docs/reports/2026-11-09-first-class-review.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`): a hands-on run of the tool against this repository's own 63 issues and PRs, plus three independent code reviews whose probes were re-run before filing. Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main 6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7 on 2026-11-09 by an executed probe or a source trace (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 878 tests ... OK (skipped=3)`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #64._

_Amended 2026-11-10 from the usage-trace addendum (`docs/reports/2026-11-10-usage-trace-addendum.md`, same branch): claims 7–11 and AC10–AC14 added, each re-run on 6009c30 that day. Claims 1–6 and AC1–AC9 are unchanged._

## Summary
After this PR, an agent can trust `ok: true`: a store with no data, an unknown item, a mistyped path, an unreachable snapshot remote and a truncated search each say what they are. `--fields` and `--format jsonl` work on every list-bearing command. Search reports stable counts and ranks item text above bot-comment matches. Each MCP tool declares the shape it really returns. A `sql` query that compares a column to a value the store never holds says so, a usage error arrives as an envelope, and the CLI can describe the shape of every command's output.

## Problem (claims to verify)
All verified by running the command on the real store unless noted.

1. **A failed first sync turns "no corpus" into empty success.** Before any sync, `status` and `search` exit 3. After a failed first sync they exit 0 with `ok: true`, `items: []`, `corpus_items: 0`. [Observed live in this session.]
2. **Wrong inputs read as success** (all exit 0, `ok: true`):
   - `related 99999` returns a ghost node `{"number": 99999, "kind": null, "title": null}`;
   - `path 99999 5` returns `path: null`, the same as "not connected";
   - `file-history cli.py`, `SRC/zaxbygraph/CLI.py` and `src\zaxbygraph\cli.py` return `entries: []`;
   - `bundle --pool 9,1,2` (closed items and a PR) returns empty bundles with no reason;
   - MCP `search` with `cursor: "abc"` silently serves page 1.
3. **`--fields` and `--format jsonl` are silent no-ops on `search`, `item` and `related`.** `search sync --fields number,title` is 13,582 chars against 13,581 without; `search sync --format jsonl | wc -l` is 1.
4. **Search counts and ranking mislead.** `search "quadratic sync"` returns 20 of 56 with `truncated: false` and no way to page on the CLI. With `--limit 1` the same query reports `matched_mode: "all", total_matches: 6`; with the default limit, `"any", total_matches: 56`. Its top hit matches only through one bot review comment and has an empty `snippet`; the items about the subject (#35, #22) rank 2 and 5. For "ingest gets slower as the database grows" they are not in the top four and 61 of 63 items match.
   [query.py#L385-L459](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/query.py#L385-L459)
5. **`snapshot pull` reports an unreachable remote as "no snapshot published".** `snapshot pull /nonexistent/remote.git` and an unresolvable URL both return `code: "snapshot_absent"`, exit 2, hint "publish first". Publish and pull success envelopes also carry `freshness: {synced_at: null, complete: false}` for a complete store.
   [snapshot.py#L589-L592](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/snapshot.py#L589-L592)
6. **Every MCP `outputSchema` is the same empty object schema**, so nothing is typed and every result validates trivially.
   [mcp_server.py#L1310-L1311](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py#L1310-L1311)
   ```py
   for _tool in _TOOLS:
       _tool["outputSchema"] = {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": True}
   ```
7. **A `sql` literal the store never holds returns zero rows as success.** `sql` is a quarter of all recorded use (1,285 of 5,069 invocations). Each of these returns `ok: true`, exit 0, a zero count and no hint:
   - `SELECT count(*) FROM items WHERE kind='pull_request'` (stored: `issue`, `pr`);
   - `... WHERE state='OPEN'` (stored: `open`, `closed`);
   - `SELECT count(*) FROM comments WHERE kind='issue'` (stored: `issue_comment`, `review_comment`);
   - `... WHERE repo='ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph'` (stored lowercase).

   In the digest about 20 engagements read such a zero as a fact ("0 open PRs", "no claims") and five fell back to paging `gh`. In one, three claim sweeps filtered `comments.kind='issue'`, reported "NO CLAIMS", and the session selected two issues a parallel session had claimed fifteen minutes earlier; it then stored a false lesson that the comments table lags. [VERIFIED by executed probes on 6009c30, 2026-11-10; the incident VERIFIED in the digest ledger (addendum §4.1).]
8. **An unknown table gets no hint.** `SELECT labels FROM items` returns `no_such_column` with the column list. `SELECT * FROM issues` returns `no_such_table` with no hint, and `PRAGMA table_info(items)` returns `bad_sql` with no pointer to `zaxbygraph schema`. The digest records guessed tables `issues` and `item_labels`, and agents reading `sqlite_master` to recover. [VERIFIED by executed probes.]
9. **A usage error is not an envelope.** `zaxbygraph --db X status --format json` and `zaxbygraph item --number 1 --format json` print argparse usage on stderr, exit 2, and write nothing to stdout, so a JSON consumer sees an empty stream. Common options are accepted only after the subcommand. The digest records about ten engagements losing calls to flag placement and unknown flags. [VERIFIED by executed probes.]
10. **Output shapes differ by command and nothing describes them.** `open` and `churn` return `data` as a bare list; `search` returns `{items, total_matches, …}`; `sql` returns `{columns, rows}`; `related` returns `{nodes, edges}`. The largest failure class in the digest, about 160 calls across about 90 engagements, is agents' own parsers raising `KeyError`/`TypeError` on a shape they guessed. Claim 6 covers the MCP declaration only, and the MCP server was never registered in any recorded session. [Shapes VERIFIED by executed probes; counts from the digest.]
11. **`item` reads one number per call.** It is the most used command (1,309 invocations), mostly inside shell loops over 4–24 numbers, and state checks for a set of numbers are done in `sql` because `item` returns the full body. `item 61 62` fails with `unrecognized arguments`. [VERIFIED.]

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHILE a store has zero items and no full sync has ever completed THE SYSTEM SHALL answer read commands with exit 3 and the no-corpus error, including after a failed first sync.

  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_surface_honesty.py -q -k test_failed_first_sync_is_still_no_corpus`
  - expect: FAIL: `search foo` exits 0 with `ok: true, corpus_items: 0` (observed live).
  - files: tests/test_surface_honesty.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 1.
- [ ] AC2: IF `related`, `path` or `explain` is given an item number that is not stored THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return `not_found`; IF a file argument matches no stored path THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return `reason: "unknown_path"` with case-insensitive and basename suggestions, after normalising backslashes.

  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_surface_honesty.py -q -k test_unknown_inputs_are_named`
  - expect: FAIL: ghost node for `related 99999`; `entries: []` for `file-history cli.py`.
  - files: tests/test_surface_honesty.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 2.
- [ ] AC3: IF `bundle --pool` drops members, or a cursor is malformed THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL say which and why (`dropped: [{number, reason}]`, `bad_request`).
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_surface_honesty.py -q -k test_dropped_pool_members_and_bad_cursors`
  - expect: FAIL: `pool: [], bundles: []` with no reason; `cursor: "abc"` serves page 1.
  - files: tests/test_surface_honesty.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 2.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN `--fields` or `--format jsonl` is passed to any command whose payload carries a list (`search`, `item`, `related`, `similar`, `triage`, `bundle`) THE SYSTEM SHALL project and stream that list.

- [ ] AC7: IF a snapshot source cannot be reached or authenticated THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return `source_unreachable` (exit 1) carrying git's message, distinct from `snapshot_absent`; snapshot envelopes SHALL carry the store's real freshness.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING

- [ ] AC9: WHEN the existing typed-surface test runs THE SYSTEM SHALL pass.

  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_mcp_typed.py -q -k test_tools_declare_schema_and_annotations`

- [ ] AC10: WHEN a `sql` statement compares `items.kind`, `items.state`, `comments.kind`, `edges.rel`, `edges.source` or any `repo` column to a string literal that is not among that column's stored values THE SYSTEM SHALL return the rows unchanged and add a `warnings` entry naming the column, the literal and the stored values (for `repo`, the stored slug that differs only by case).
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_surface_honesty.py -q -k test_out_of_vocabulary_literal_warns`
  - expect: FAIL: `kind='pull_request'`, `state='OPEN'`, `comments.kind='issue'` and a mixed-case repo each return `ok: true`, zero rows, no warning.
  - files: tests/test_surface_honesty.py

- [ ] AC11: IF `sql` fails with an unknown table THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL return a hint listing the store's tables; IF `sql` refuses a `PRAGMA` THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL name `zaxbygraph schema [TABLE]` in the hint.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING

  - expect: FAIL: `no_such_table` and `bad_sql` carry no `hint`.

- [ ] AC12: IF argument parsing fails while a machine format is in effect (`--format json|compact|jsonl`, or stdout is not a TTY) THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL write a `bad_request` envelope to stdout carrying argparse's message and the nearest valid flag, and exit 2; `--db`, `--repo` and `--format` SHALL be accepted before the subcommand as well as after it.

  - expect: FAIL: stdout is empty and stderr holds usage text; `--db X status` fails with `invalid choice`.
  - files: tests/test_surface_honesty.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 9.
- [ ] AC13: WHEN `item` is given several numbers THE SYSTEM SHALL return one row per number in the order given, apply `--fields`, `--max-body-chars` and `--max-comments` to each, and name each number that is not stored instead of failing the call.

- [ ] AC14: WHEN `zaxbygraph schema --output COMMAND` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL print, for every read command, the same schema AC8 declares for its MCP tool, and SKILL.md SHALL carry a per-command shape table that a test compares with it.

**In:** all of the above, plus doc statements the code contradicts: SKILL.md "a broad query is safe to run" and "exit 3 = missing or empty", and AGENTS.md "CI covers 3.11 and 3.12" (CI runs 3.11–3.14).

issue_comments.body:
**Additional evidence from the maintainer's usage log (2026-11-09), relevant to AC3–AC4.** Recorded on the maintainer's Windows machine; not reproducible from the review sandbox, so it is context for the implementer, not a verified claim of this issue.

- `pip install -e .` installs the package but fails to create the console script in `C:\Python311\Scripts` (WinError 2 on the `.deleteme` rename), so `zaxbygraph` is not on PATH and agents fall back to `python -m zaxbygraph`. `pip install --user` works but its Scripts directory was not on PATH.
- A non-editable install leaves a package directory in site-packages that shadows the editable install, so test discovery silently runs stale code.
- Four stale dist-infos (0.1.0–0.4.0) were found side by side.

Implication for `init` and the README install section: prefer an isolated install (`pipx`/`uvx`), have `init`/`doctor` report the path the package was imported from and warn when more than one distribution is present, and document `python -m zaxbygraph` as the always-available form.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**Follow-up from the maintainer's machine (2026-11-10). Two facts for this issue.**

**1. Claim 4, current state of the three skill copies.**

| Copy | Lines | `triage` mentions | sha256 (first 8) | `.zaxbygraph_version` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `~/.zcode/skills` | 350 | 8 | 7e5078bd | 3d3aab0 |
| `~/.agents/skills` | 350 | 8 | 7e5078bd | b47913e |
| `~/.claude/skills` | 141 | 0 | daae4b0d | e2ef892 |
| `origin/main` | 350 | 8 | 1880ef23 | — |

The `.zcode` and `.agents` copies were refreshed by hand on 2026-11-09 and now carry the recipe. Their markers were not updated, so both markers name revisions whose text they no longer hold, and their hash differs from `origin/main` although the line count matches (cause unknown; a line-ending difference is the likely one). The `.claude` copy is still the 2026-09-12 text. No process writes the marker: it comes from ad-hoc shell commands in individual sessions. This supports AC6's content-hash stamp and AC7's check as written; the claim's window (2026-10-30 to 2026-11-08 without the recipe) stands for the `.zcode` copy.

Adoption, from the raw event files: no consumer-repository session ran `triage`, `bundle`, `brief` or `similar`. The only derived command run on a consumer repository was `coupling`, twice, in one trainingapp audit that also probed `--help` for `triage`, `brief` and `similar`. The count is of direct shell commands; aliases and scripted calls are not resolved.

**2. The installed tool is the development working tree.** `pip show` reports an editable install, and `git -C E:\ZCode\zaxbygraph status --short` shows 24 modified tracked files, including `db.py`, `schema.sql`, `sync.py` and `store.py`, plus six untracked test modules: the in-progress Workstream A work. Every session on the machine that runs `zaxbygraph` against a real store therefore runs unreviewed sync and migration code. This is the "version illusion" of claim 1 in its sharpest form: `--version` says 0.4.0 and `rev-parse HEAD` says 6009c30 while the code that runs is neither.

Suggested addition to AC4's README install section, at the implementer's discretion: the documented install for consumer use is a pinned, non-editable one (`pipx install git+…@<tag>`), and development happens in a separate checkout or virtual environment.

item.body:
_Remediation issue. Generated from the first-class review of 2026-11-09 (`docs/reports/2026-11-09-first-class-review.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`): a hands-on run of the tool against this repository's own 63 issues and PRs, plus three independent code reviews whose probes were re-run before filing. Every claim below was re-checked against origin/main 6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7 on 2026-11-09 by an executed probe or a source trace (baseline: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 878 tests ... OK (skipped=3)`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #64._

_Amended 2026-11-10 from the usage-trace addendum (`docs/reports/2026-11-10-usage-trace-addendum.md`, same branch): claim 4 and AC6–AC7 added. Claims 1–3 and AC1–AC5 are unchanged._

## Summary
After this PR, the package version moves with the schema and tool set, a changelog records what changed, the MCP server and the skill report the real version, and a first-time agent has one documented command that installs the tool, checks `gh`, and builds a store, falling back to REST where GraphQL is unavailable. The skill ships inside the package, so the text an agent loads always matches the tool it runs, and a stale installed copy is reported.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **The version has not moved across 30 commits and six schema versions.** `0.4.0` was set when the schema was v5; `CURRENT_USER_VERSION` is now 11. The MCP `serverInfo.version` and the skill's version stamp report the same frozen value, so an agent cannot tell which tool set it has. [VERIFIED: `git log` since the version commit; `git tag` is empty; no CHANGELOG exists.]
   [pyproject.toml#L3](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/pyproject.toml#L3)
   ```toml
   version = "0.4.0"
   ```
   [db.py#L21](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L21)
   ```py
   CURRENT_USER_VERSION = 11
   ```
2. **The only documented install is `pip install -e .` from a clone.** Packaging metadata uses the old license form and has no classifiers. [VERIFIED by reading `pyproject.toml` and README.]
3. **First use fails without guidance.** With no `gh`, an unauthenticated `gh`, or GraphQL unavailable, the first `sync` returns the raw tool error with `code: "runtime"` and no hint. [VERIFIED live for the GraphQL case; the degrade itself is #65.]
4. **The skill agents load is a hand copy that falls behind the tool.** The package ships only `schema.sql`; the README says to install the skill by copying `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md` into a skills directory. The maintainer's usage digest (289 engagements, 196 skill loads) shows three installed copies: `~/.claude/skills` is the v0.1 text of 2026-09-12; `~/.zcode/skills` was measured on 2026-11-08 at revision 3d3aab0 (2026-10-28, 291 lines); `~/.agents/skills` is stamped b47913e (2026-10-23). The triage → bundle → brief recipe first appears in df98847 (2026-10-30): `git show <rev>:skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md | grep -ci triage` is 0 for b47913e and 3d3aab0, and 5 for df98847. From 2026-10-30 to at least 2026-11-08 a session that loaded the skill could not learn that `triage`, `bundle` or `brief` exist, while 150 engagements were asked to choose issues to collate. The digest also records five separate sessions noticing drift and re-copying by hand. [VERIFIED: packaging by reading `pyproject.toml`; revisions against git history; installed stamps from the digest (addendum §4.3).]
   [pyproject.toml#L25-L26](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/pyproject.toml#L25-L26)
   ```toml
   [tool.setuptools.package-data]
   zaxbygraph = ["schema.sql"]
   ```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN the schema version or the MCP tool list changes without a package version bump and a CHANGELOG entry THE SYSTEM SHALL fail a test that pins (version, schema version, tool names) together.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_release.py -q -k test_version_moves_with_schema_and_tools`
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_release.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_release.py
  - why: No pin at base.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN `zaxbygraph --version`, MCP `serverInfo`, `server/discover` and the skill stamp are read THE SYSTEM SHALL report the same version, and `status` SHALL report the store's schema version beside it.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_release.py -q -k test_one_version_everywhere`
  - expect: FAIL: `status` carries no tool or schema version.
  - files: tests/test_release.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 1.
- [ ] AC3: WHEN `zaxbygraph init --repo OWNER/REPO` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL check `gh` presence and authentication with coded errors and hints, build the store (degrading to REST per #65), and print the MCP registration line.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_release.py -q -k test_init_preflight_and_first_sync`
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_release.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_release.py
  - why: No command at base.
- [ ] AC4: WHEN the package metadata is built THE SYSTEM SHALL carry an SPDX license expression, classifiers, and a README install section using a one-line `pipx`/`uvx` command from the repository URL.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_release.py -q -k test_packaging_metadata`
  - expect: FAIL: `license = { text = ... }`, no classifiers.
  - files: tests/test_release.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 2.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN this PR merges THE SYSTEM SHALL be tagged with its version, and the maintainer SHALL record whether to publish to PyPI and the MCP Registry.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(PRODUCT_DECISION)
  - argv: n/a
  - expect: n/a
  - files: n/a
  - why: substitute evidence: the tag on the merge commit, and the maintainer's publish decision recorded on this issue (carried over from #32 AC7; AGENTS forbids storing a publish token in the repository).
- [ ] AC6: WHEN the package is installed THE SYSTEM SHALL contain the skill, and `zaxbygraph skill` SHALL print it and `zaxbygraph skill --install DIR` SHALL write it to `DIR/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md` with a stamp of the package version and the skill's content hash; a test SHALL fail when the packaged skill and `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md` differ.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_release.py -q -k test_skill_ships_with_the_package`
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_release.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_release.py
  - why: No command at base; package data holds only `schema.sql` (claim 4).
- [ ] AC7: WHEN `zaxbygraph doctor` or `zaxbygraph skill --check` runs THE SYSTEM SHALL look for installed copies in the user-level skill directories it documents (`~/.claude/skills`, `~/.agents/skills`, `~/.zcode/skills`, `~/.opencode/skills`) and any `--dir` given, and report each copy whose content hash differs from the packaged skill as `stale`, with the one-line command that refreshes it; it SHALL write nothing without `--install`.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: `python -m pytest tests/test_release.py -q -k test_stale_skill_copies_are_reported`
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_release.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_release.py
  - why: No check at base; three stale copies went unnoticed for weeks (claim 4).

## Scope
**In:** version bump to reflect schema v11/v12 and the current tool set; `CHANGELOG.md` back-filled from merged PR titles; version pin test; `init`; packaging metadata; README install section; the skill as package data with `skill`, `skill --install` and `skill --check`.
**Out:** the REST degrade itself (#65); installing a skill without being asked.

## Sequence
[Workstream D] Releases and first use: #73 only (this issue is D-01). Parallel-safe; rebase on #65 for AC3.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: #65 (AC3 only)
- Schema after: none
- Gated on: AC5

## Files expected to change
`pyproject.toml`, `src/zaxbygraph/__init__.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/cli.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/doctor.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/query.py`, new `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`, `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md`, new `tests/test_release.py`.

## Definition of done
All ACs pass on every CI leg (Windows and Linux). The PR body says `Closes #<n>` and carries `## Closure evidence` with each AC's argv and result.

issue_comments.body:
**Maintainer decisions recorded, 2026-11-11** (given in a Claude Code session after a research pass and an independent critic pass on agent collisions; this comment is the substitute evidence for AC9).

1. **The tool may write to GitHub.** Maintainer, verbatim: "zaxbygraph does not need to stay read only." Writing a claim is now tracked in #77.
2. **Built-in claim window: 72 hours.** The maintainer accepted the revised design that proposed it ("accepted on both items"). Basis: on ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm, across the 43 issues GitHub search returns for `is:issue "Agent claim" in:comments`, 35 have a pull request cross-referenced after the first claim; the time from claim to that pull request has a median of 5.4 hours, a 90th percentile of 19.1 hours and a maximum of 24.4 hours, and none exceeds 72 hours (executed GraphQL probe, 2026-11-11). The measure is the first cross-referencing pull request, which is not always the fixing one.
3. **A release comment format is defined and built in.** Accepted with the same design. A release form is already in use: opencode-swarm issue 3588 carries `**Claim released (scope split):**` at 2026-11-06T18:03:52Z (`gh api repos/ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm/issues/3588/comments`, 2026-11-11). This corrects claim 3 of this issue.
4. **Claims carry a session token.** Accepted with the same design. Every claim found by the probe comes from one login (no issue has claims from more than one), so "the same author" cannot tell sessions apart.
5. **Only an owner, member or collaborator can hold a claim.** Accepted with the same design. The comment's author association is already stored.

The issue body is being amended to match; corrections are kept inline.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

**Maintainer decisions, 2026-11-11** (full record on #77). The maintainer's reply to the recommendations, verbatim: "accept all of the above with your recommendations". What changes here:

For this issue specifically: the recorded claim format in that incident reads verbatim `Claiming for active work (2026-11-11). This issue will be worked in a collated trace with #366 …` — it matches neither built-in pattern (`Agent claim`, `Working this issue`), so under AC4 defaults the AC1 gate would not have gated those issues. AC1/AC2's probe fixtures may want a leg in that third phrasing (it is common across the zmem repo's claim history), or the pattern list in #77's `claims.py` grows to include it.

item.body:
*Provenance: remediation issue, generated from the usage-trace addendum of 2026-11-10 (`docs/reports/2026-11-10-usage-trace-addendum.md` on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`), which tested the 2026-11-09 first-class review against the maintainer's digest of 289 agent engagements (5,069 CLI invocations, 2026-09-12 → 2026-11-09). Every claim about current behaviour below was re-checked against the anchor commit origin/main 6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7 on 2026-11-10 by an executed probe or a source trace (suite baseline recorded 2026-11-09: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → `Ran 878 tests ... OK (skipped=3)`). One issue = one PR. Tracking: #64. The `~/.zcode` and `~/.agents` paths and the digest named below are on the maintainer's machine, outside this repository.*

_Amended 2026-11-10 after a follow-up on the maintainer's machine (addendum §8): claim 3 added; AC3 and AC4 no longer assume a release marker or a known claim lifetime, because neither is defined anywhere; AC9 added as the maintainer decision._

_Amended 2026-11-11 after a research pass and an independent critic pass on agent collisions, re-checked the same day against origin/main 6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7 and with read-only `gh` calls: claim 3 corrected inline; claims 4 and 5 added; AC1, AC3, AC4, AC5 and AC8 changed; AC9 decided (https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/74#issuecomment-6797325536); AC10 added; writing a claim moved from Out to #77. Format only, no change of meaning: the preamble, the claim 1 excerpt (now the full cited range, verbatim), permalinks on claims 2 and 3, bare `argv` values and the AC9 sub-bullets were brought to the issue linter's shape._

_Amended again 2026-11-11 from the maintainer decisions recorded at https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/74#issuecomment-6801349269: #77 is worked first and owns the claim parser, patterns, window and config keys, so this issue now depends on #77 instead of blocking it; AC4's wording and the dependency lines changed; AC3 stands as written._

## Summary
After this PR, `triage` and `bundle` gate out an open issue that another session has announced it is working, name the claim as evidence, and one read command lists the active claims. Agents stop hand-writing claim sweeps in SQL, and stop being offered work that is already taken. The skill states the claim comment format the gate reads, which today is written down nowhere. A claim carries a session token, so the gate can tell apart sessions that all post as one login, and only an owner, member or collaborator can hold one.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **Work selection cannot see a claim.** Sessions on the maintainer's repositories announce work with an issue comment such as `**Agent claim:** Working this issue now (with #3491 as one collated PR …)`. The gates are `blocked`, `assigned`, `linked_pr` and `locked`; none reads comments. Probe on a copy of this repository's store: one comment `**Agent claim:** Working this issue now (collated PR in progress).` dated one hour before the last sync, added to open issue #8. `triage --include-gated` returns `8 ranked=True gates=[]` and `bundle` returns members `[8, 21]`. VERIFIED by executed probe on 6009c30.
   [derive.py#L1667-L1681](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/derive.py#L1667-L1681)
   ```py
               gates.append("blocked")
           if number in assignees:
               gates.append("assigned")
           direct_linked = any(
               states.get(dst, {}).get("state") == "open"
               and states.get(dst, {}).get("kind") == "pr"
               for dst in linked_pr_dsts.get(number, set())
           )
           keyword_linked = bool(keyword_closers.get(number))
           if direct_linked:
               gates.append("linked_pr")
           elif keyword_linked:
               gates.append("linked_pr (append-only evidence; may be stale)")
           if row["locked"]:
               gates.append("locked")
   ```
2. **Agents rebuild the claim sweep by hand, and get it wrong.** The digest's call ledger holds 40 `sql` claim sweeps over `comments` (patterns `Agent claim`, `Working this issue`, `Work started`), each with a hand-picked date cutoff: zero to nine days back, most often three, across the 18 sweeps whose cutoff can be read. Nine bundles were dropped or narrowed because another session owned the work, and two duplicates were caught only after selection. In one engagement (opencode-swarm, 2026-11-03) three sweeps filtered `comments.kind='issue'`; the stored values are `issue_comment` and `review_comment`, so each returned zero rows, the agent reported "NO CLAIMS", and it selected #3539 + #3491 fifteen minutes after a parallel session had claimed them. VERIFIED in the digest ledger (addendum §4.1); the stored vocabulary VERIFIED on 6009c30.
   [store.py#L246-L247](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L246-L247)
   ```py
           ("issue_comment", incoming_issue),
           ("review_comment", incoming_review_comments),
   ```
3. **The claim convention is defined nowhere.** A search of `~/.zcode/skills` and `~/.agents/skills` on the maintainer's machine for `Agent claim` and `Working this issue` returns nothing. No release or abandon comment exists, and no lifetime is stated. Each session infers the format and the cutoff from memory records. VERIFIED on the maintainer's machine, 2026-11-10 (`grep -rn -F`, exit 1); repository-level AGENTS files were not exhaustively searched.
   CORRECTED during review (2026-11-11): a release comment does exist in recorded use. ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm issue 3588 carries `**Claim released (scope split):**` at 2026-11-06T18:03:52Z, between a claim at 2026-11-06T16:42:56Z and a new claim at 2026-11-07T15:48:45Z. The rest of the claim stands: the format is written down nowhere and no lifetime is stated. VERIFIED by `gh api repos/ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm/issues/3588/comments`, 2026-11-11.
   [SKILL.md#L121](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md#L121)
   ```md
   | Which open issues are worth working next, and why | `triage` — ranked candidates with demand/leverage/risk/priority scores; gates name every exclusion — the vocabulary is exactly `blocked`, `assigned`, `linked_pr`, `linked_pr (append-only evidence; may be stale)`, `locked` (match on the literal strings) |
   ```
4. **Every session posts as the same login, so an author cannot identify a claim's holder.** Across the 43 opencode-swarm issues that GitHub search returns for `is:issue "Agent claim" in:comments`, 40 claim comments were found and no issue carries claims from more than one login. A rule that ends a claim on a later comment "by the same author" would let any session's release end every session's claim. The one gate that reads a login today is `assigned`. VERIFIED by an executed GraphQL probe, 2026-11-11.
   [derive.py#L1668-L1669](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/derive.py#L1668-L1669)
   ```py
           if number in assignees:
               gates.append("assigned")
   ```
5. **Anyone can post a claim comment on a public repository, and the association that would tell them apart is stored but unread by the gates.** ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph and ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm are public. The store keeps each comment's author association; in the opencode-swarm store the values are `MEMBER` (5,821), `CONTRIBUTOR` (2,830) and `NONE` (718), and all 39 stored claim comments are `MEMBER`. A claim that names other issues gates each of them (AC2), so one comment from any account could gate many issues for the whole window. VERIFIED by `gh repo view --json visibility` and a read-only query of the store, 2026-11-11.
   [db.py#L1220](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L1220)
   ```py
       ("author_association", "TEXT"),
   ```

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN an open issue carries a comment that matches a claim pattern outside quoted lines and code fences, created within the claim window before the store's last sync time, by an author whose association is `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR`, THE SYSTEM SHALL gate the issue in `triage` and `bundle` with gate `claimed` and report the comment's author, session token (null when the comment carries none), time and URL as evidence.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claims.py -q -k test_claimed_issue_is_gated
  - expect: FAIL: the claimed issue is `ranked: true, gates: []` and is a bundle member (probe-observed).
  - files: tests/test_claims.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 1.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN a claim comment names other issues of the same repository THE SYSTEM SHALL gate each named open issue with the same evidence.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claims.py -q -k test_claim_covers_named_issues
  - expect: FAIL: an issue named in another issue's claim comment is `ranked: true`.
  - files: tests/test_claims.py
  - why: RED at base; the recorded claims name their collated partners (`with #3491 as one collated PR`).
- [ ] AC3: IF a claim is older than the claim window THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL not gate the issue and SHALL report it under `stale_claims` with the claim's age; a later comment on the same issue that matches the release pattern SHALL end the claim at once when it carries the claim's session token, and SHALL end a claim that carries no token only when the release carries none either.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claims.py -q -k test_expired_and_released_claims
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claims.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claims.py
  - why: No claim concept at base. A release form is in recorded use (claim 3, corrected), and the token is what tells sessions apart under one login (claim 4).
- [ ] AC4: WHEN no config file exists THE SYSTEM SHALL apply, through the parser and values #77 defines in `claims.py`, built-in claim patterns (`Agent claim`, `Working this issue`, case-insensitive), the built-in release pattern (a comment that starts with `**Claim released`), the session-token form `session=<token>`, and a built-in window of 72 hours; the config chain SHALL override patterns, release pattern and window; the payload SHALL echo the values in effect beside the weights.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claims.py -q -k test_claim_config_defaults_and_overrides
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claims.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claims.py
  - why: The check file does not exist at base. #77 defines the settings; the gate honouring them and the payload echo are new here.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN `zaxbygraph claims` runs (CLI and MCP) THE SYSTEM SHALL list every active and stale claim on open issues, newest first, with issue number, title, author, author association, `trusted`, session token, time, age and the issues the claim names as parsed fields, and the matched text wrapped in `untrusted_text`, marked `derived: true`.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claims.py -q -k test_claims_command
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claims.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claims.py
  - why: No command at base; replaces the hand-written sweeps of claim 2.
- [ ] AC6: WHEN claim gates are computed twice on the same store THE SYSTEM SHALL return byte-identical output apart from freshness age, measuring the window from the store's last sync time and never from the wall clock.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claims.py -q -k test_claim_gate_is_deterministic
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claims.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claims.py
  - why: AGENTS: the derived tier is deterministic.
- [ ] AC7: WHEN the derived tier runs THE SYSTEM SHALL leave the store byte-identical.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_similar.py -q -k test_derived_tier_never_writes
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_similar.py
  - why: GREEN at base. A claim is computed at query time from stored comments; nothing is written to `edges`, `items` or any persisted table (AGENTS).
- [ ] AC8: WHEN the bundled skill is read THE SYSTEM SHALL state the claim and release comment formats the gate matches, including the session token, and the window in effect, and tell agents to read `claims` (or the `claimed` gate) instead of sweeping `comments` with SQL, and to refresh with `--max-age` before trusting an empty answer.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claims.py -q -k test_skill_names_claims
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claims.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claims.py
  - why: Docs test; this is the first written definition of the convention (claim 3).
- [ ] AC9: WHEN the built-in claim window is chosen THE SYSTEM SHALL ship the value the maintainer records, and the maintainer SHALL say whether a release comment format is to be defined. DECIDED 2026-11-11: 72 hours, and a release format is defined and built in.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(PRODUCT_DECISION)
  - files: n/a
  - substitute evidence: the maintainer's decision recorded on this issue (https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/74#issuecomment-6797325536). Recorded sweeps looked back zero to nine days, most often three; measured time from claim to first cross-referencing pull request tops out at 24.4 hours across 35 claims.
- [ ] AC10: IF a comment that matches a claim pattern is by an author whose association is not `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR`, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL not gate any issue on it and SHALL list it in `claims` with `trusted: false`.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claims.py -q -k test_untrusted_author_does_not_gate
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claims.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claims.py
  - why: No claim concept at base. Without this, one comment from any account could gate every issue it names (claim 5).

## Scope
**In:** the `claimed` gate; named-issue coverage; expiry; built-in and configured patterns; the built-in release pattern and session token; the trusted-author rule; the `claims` command and MCP tool; the skill's definition of the claim format.
**Out:** writing or releasing a claim, the live pre-PR check and the live claims view (#77; the maintainer decided on 2026-11-11 that the tool need not stay read-only toward GitHub); recording whether a proposed bundle was later fixed together (still a proposal in #64; it would need persisted derived output, which AGENTS forbids); work on branches that have no PR and no claim comment (not in the store).

## Sequence
[Workstream B] Work selection that is measured: #68 -> #69 -> #70 -> this issue (B-04). #77 (B-05) merges before this issue.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: #69 (the `gated` report shape and `derive.py`), #70 (`derive.py` and the skill recipe), #77 (the claim parser, patterns, window and config keys in `claims.py`)
- Schema after: none
- Gated on: none (AC9 decided 2026-11-11)
- Blocks: nothing

## Files expected to change
`src/zaxbygraph/derive.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/cli.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py`, `docs/schema.md`, `README.md`, `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md`, new `tests/test_claims.py`.

## Definition of done
All ACs pass on every CI leg (Windows and Linux). The PR body says `Closes #<n>` and carries `## Closure evidence` with each AC's argv and result.

item.body:
*Provenance: remediation issue, generated on 2026-11-10 from the open question recorded on #64 ("whether the `timeline truncated` note is a false report") and in `docs/reports/2026-11-10-usage-trace-addendum.md` §8 on branch `claude/upbeat-fermi-2fqehy`. Every claim below was re-checked against the anchor commit, origin/main 6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7 on 2026-11-10 by a command run in the filing session: live `gh api graphql` reads, read-only (`mode=ro`) reads of the maintainer's stores, a probe run with `PYTHONPATH=src` in a clean clone at that commit, and source traces. The stores and the probe script are local to the maintainer's machine and are not in this repository. One issue = one PR. Tracking: #64.*

## Summary
After this PR, a pull request whose filtered timeline page arrived whole is stored as complete: its reopen events reach `item_events`, no `timeline truncated` note is written for it, no extra request is spent on it, and `status` stops counting it under `truncation_notes`.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **On a pull request, GitHub's `timelineItems.totalCount` ignores `itemTypes`; on an issue it does not.** The sync query filters to three event types and asks for `totalCount`. `VERIFIED` by live reads on 2026-11-10 with the query's own selection, `timelineItems(first:50, itemTypes:[CLOSED_EVENT, CROSS_REFERENCED_EVENT, REOPENED_EVENT]) { totalCount filteredCount pageInfo { hasNextPage } nodes { __typename } }`:

   | Item | Kind | `totalCount` | `filteredCount` | nodes | `hasNextPage` |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph 63 | PR | 42 | 2 | 2 | false |
   | ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm 3628 | PR | 6 | 1 | 1 | false |
   | ZaxbyHub/ragappv3 853 | PR | 18 | 4 | 4 | false |
   | ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm 3165 | issue | 25 | 25 | 25 (page of 50) | false |

   The same issue read without `itemTypes` reports `totalCount: 45`, so the issue-side count is the filtered one. Twelve recently updated opencode-swarm issues all returned `totalCount == filteredCount`. `INFERENCE`: this is GitHub's current behaviour, not a documented contract; it can change, and other GitHub hosts may differ.

   https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py#L193-L195
   ```
   timelineItems(first: 50, itemTypes: %(types)s) {
     totalCount
     pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }
   ```

2. **The initial-page check compares that `totalCount` with the filtered node count, so it calls every such pull-request page unfaithful.** `VERIFIED` by probe in a clean clone at the anchor commit: `_page_rendered_faithfully({"totalCount": 42, "pageInfo": {"hasNextPage": False, ...}, "nodes": [<2 nodes>]}, initial=True)` returns `False`, and `_children_from_node` returns `timeline_incomplete: True` with no `timeline_cursor`.

   https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py#L423-L427
   ```
           and not page_info.get("hasNextPage")
           and comparable
           and total > len(raw_nodes)
       ):
           return False
   ```
   Prior art: the check was added for issue #53 (review PRR-004) to catch a page that drops nodes. This PR keeps that protection and changes only what the node count is compared with. `tests/test_link_stream_malformed.py::test_totalcount_overflow_emits_no_cursor` pins the current comparison with a one-node page and `totalCount=9`; that fixture is exactly the false-positive shape and has to be re-expressed.

3. **In the real stores, every item carrying the note is a pull request, and every one of them was complete.** `VERIFIED` by read-only `fetch_log` reads plus one batched live read per repository, comparing each flagged item with GitHub:

   | Store | Distinct items with `timeline truncated` | Issues among them | Flagged items where `filteredCount == nodes` and `hasNextPage` is false |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | opencode-swarm | 53 | 0 | 53 of 53 |
   | ragappv3 | 46 | 0 | 46 of 46 |
   | trainingapp | 38 | 0 | 38 of 38 |
   | zmem | 22 | 0 | 22 of 22 |
   | zaxbygraph | 6 | 0 | 6 of 6 |

   No flagged item was a real truncation. (`status` counts log rows, not items: 108 note rows on opencode-swarm.) The note is written here:

   https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/sync.py#L1122-L1122
   ```
                               if flags.get("timeline_incomplete"):
   ```

4. **A flagged item never writes its reopen events.** `VERIFIED` by source trace and by one stored case. The flag makes the timeline section incomplete (`sync.py:291`), and `write_item_events` returns before writing when the section is incomplete:

   https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/store.py#L378-L379
   ```
       if timeline is None or not timeline_complete:
           return
   ```
   Stored case: ZaxbyHub/ragappv3 PR 853 has one `ReopenedEvent` on GitHub (row 3 of the table in claim 1), carries the `timeline truncated` note, and has zero `item_events` rows; the ragappv3 store has zero `item_events` rows in total. `export-corpus` reads `item_events` per item (`export.py:503-508`), so the exported corpus is missing these events too. `INFERENCE`: `triage` reads reopen counts for open issues only, so its ranking is probably unaffected; not tested.

5. **Each flagged item costs one extra GraphQL request on every ingest, and the flag never clears.** `VERIFIED` by probe at the anchor commit: `fetch_children` on one such pull request made one `_timeline_page` call with `last: 250`, and the child still carried `timeline_incomplete: True` afterwards. With no cursor the drain loop is skipped, `drained` is false, and the newest-window branch runs:

   https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py#L979-L984
   ```
           drained = last_page_saw_more is False and len(events) <= _MAX_TIMELINE_EVENTS
           if drained:
               child["timeline"] = events
               child.pop("timeline_incomplete", None)
           else:
               newest, info = self._timeline_page(number, kind, f"last: {_TIMELINE_PAGE_MAX}")
   ```
   A flagged item is not re-fetched on later runs for this reason alone (`VERIFIED` by source trace: nothing reads the note or the flag to schedule work); it is re-ingested only when GitHub lists it again.

6. **The Workstream A change does not address this.** `VERIFIED` by read-only inspection of commit 84df673 on branch `fix/65-66-67-sync-integrity` (local to the maintainer's machine at filing time): `git grep filteredCount` over `src` and `tests` finds nothing, and `total > len(raw_nodes)` is still the comparison in `_page_rendered_faithfully`. That commit changes `graphql.py`, so this PR should be based on it once it merges. The comparison as it stands on the anchor commit:

   https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/graphql.py#L425-L425
   ```
           and total > len(raw_nodes)
   ```

## Scope
In:
- What the initial timeline page's node count is compared with, for pull requests and issues.
- The existing tests that pin the current comparison.
- A statement in `docs/schema.md` of what `timeline truncated` means after the change.

Out:
- The same `totalCount` comparison on the comments, reviews, files, closing-reference and link connections. None of them takes a type filter; no defect is claimed there.
- Back-filling reopen events for pull requests already stored. They are written the next time the item is ingested; `sync --force` does it for a whole store. Whether to force that from a migration is a maintainer decision.
- Removing the false notes already in `fetch_log`.
- Everything in #65, #66 and #67.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN the initial timeline page of a pull request reports no next page, returns every node its filter matched, and reports a `totalCount` larger than its node count, THE SYSTEM SHALL carry the timeline as complete, with no `timeline_incomplete` flag.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_timeline_flow.py -q -k test_filtered_pr_timeline_page_is_complete
  - expect: FAIL: `timeline_incomplete` is `True` for a two-node page with `totalCount: 42` (probe-observed).
  - files: tests/test_timeline_flow.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 2.
- [ ] AC2: WHEN such a page is fetched, THE SYSTEM SHALL issue no further timeline request for that item.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_timeline_flow.py -q -k test_filtered_pr_timeline_page_costs_no_extra_request
  - expect: FAIL: one recorded `_timeline_page` call, `last: 250` (probe-observed).
  - files: tests/test_timeline_flow.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 5.
- [ ] AC3: WHEN a sync ingests a pull request whose page of that shape contains a reopened event, THE SYSTEM SHALL store the event in `item_events` and write no `timeline truncated` row to `fetch_log`.
  - class: DISCRIMINATING
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_timeline_flow.py -q -k test_filtered_pr_reopen_event_is_stored
  - expect: FAIL: zero `item_events` rows and one `timeline truncated: retained newest` row (source-traced; observed on a real store).
  - files: tests/test_timeline_flow.py
  - why: RED at base per claim 4.
- [ ] AC4: IF an initial timeline page contains a node that cannot be rendered, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL keep `timeline_incomplete` set and emit no `timeline_cursor`.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_link_stream_malformed.py -q -k test_dropped_node_emits_no_cursor
  - expect: PASS.
  - files: tests/test_link_stream_malformed.py
