item.body:
Closes #65, closes #66, closes #67

PR head: cc4106079a8fe91424836283256029c7aa3cff82

# Workstream A: sync integrity — a long sync no longer skips items, fabricates deletions, or mis-reads closing keywords

## Root Cause

Three independent defects shared one shape: a local, mechanically-derived
graph trusting a source that does not give the guarantees the reader assumes.

- **#65** — GitHub serves the issues listing as fixed page offsets over a
  `sort=updated` order that MOVES: an already-delivered item that is updated
  or deleted shifts every later item up one, so the next page's offset skips
  a live item (`src/zaxbygraph/github.py:list_issues`). Nothing re-checked
  the page just served, and nothing re-walked the window, so the skipped item
  was silently absent from a store that reported itself complete. A rate
  window also restarted the walk from the run-start binding instead of the
  committed watermark, and a GraphQL failure (validation, schema drift, or a
  hung `gh`) aborted the whole run.
- **#66** — reference digits were captured with an unbounded `(\d+)`, so a
  4300+-digit token in a comment body wedged `int()` and killed the run at
  that item forever; a deterministic extraction fault likewise escaped the
  item transaction; the deletion oracle refused every all-gone chunk
  (`deletion probe resolved no nodes for a whole chunk`), so a REAL deletion
  made every subsequent `sync --force` fail; and `sync --numbers` marked
  items deleted from an all-404 batch that was really a repository-level
  access failure.
- **#67** — `closes_keyword` was derived from any text surface, so an issue
  body containing a closing keyword closed its target (GitHub honours closing keywords only in
  PR descriptions and commit messages); code spans, fences, diff hunks,
  quotes, `comment #308` ids and spaced foreign refs all became edges; there
  was no bot identity (`actors.is_bot`) and no indexed branch lookup (the
  per-issue `branch_ref` derivation scanned).

## Fix

- **Listing completeness** (`github.py`, `sync.py`): every run that drains
  the listing walks its window at least twice; each FULL page is re-read
  once and its number set compared (a mismatch ends the pass through
  `ListingShiftedError`); the loop continues until a pass's delivered set
  equals its predecessor's exactly (set equality, not subset — a subset rule
  stops on a pass that lost an item the store still lacks); the 4-pass cap
  fails the run `listing_not_quiescent` with a persisted recovery floor
  (`listing_floor`/`listing_floor_active`), keeps `full_sync_pending`, and
  suppresses the clean finish; the next run re-drains from the earlier of
  the floor and the watermark and clears it on success; a rate-window
  restart re-reads the committed watermark (`_committed_watermark`); a typed
  transport failure or a 401/403/404 on the bulk children query degrades to
  the per-item REST path (`GitHubTransportError`, `_degradable_error`).
- **Torn rows** (`sync.py`): a pull payload newer than its listing row is
  refreshed (bounded at 2 attempts) or SKIPPED into the durable
  `sync_pending(reason='torn')` set — never stored as the mixture — and
  every later non-targeted run retries it first. A 404 during the retry
  resolves as a deletion through the repository-read gate.
- **Deletion verdicts** (`graphql.py`, `sync.py`, `store.py`): the
  PRODUCTION `GraphQLSource.check_deleted` owns chunking and the whole
  truth table (live witness corroborates / dead witness raises / no witness
  = one `probe_repository()` read / one-argument call keeps the base
  refusal); the pass writes its candidate set to `sync_pending` BEFORE the
  probe and marks only after every chunk succeeds; a failed pass is retried
  by a later non-full run over exactly the pending set and clears rows,
  marker and error together; the `--numbers` reachability gate asks the
  repository before any per-item 404 verdict.
- **Reference extraction** (`extract.py`): digit captures capped at 10
  (`_MAX_REF_DIGITS`) so an oversized token matches nothing instead of
  wedging `int()`; `_noise_ranges`/`_is_noise_reference` suppress code
  spans, fenced blocks, diff hunks, quotes, `comment #<id>` and spaced
  foreign refs; `closes_keyword` derives only from PR descriptions and
  retained commit messages (issue bodies, comments and reviews record
  `mentions`).
- **Bot identity and branch lookup** (`store.py`, `db.py`): `actors.is_bot`
  from the `[bot]` suffix, REST `type`, GraphQL `__typename`, or the
  `ZAXBYGRAPH_BOT_LOGINS` exact-login list — max-semantics, never
  downgraded, backfilled by migration v12 from stored payloads; PR
  `head_ref` derives an indexed `branch_token` for the `branch_ref` lookup.
- **Migration v12** (`db.py`, `schema.sql`): guarded column/table adds,
  the `is_bot`/`branch_token` backfills, and a streaming offline
  re-derivation of every `source='keyword'` edge under the #67 rules with
  the malformed-row preservation policy.
- **Surfaces** (`cli.py`, `mcp_server.py`, `query.py`, `doctor.py`): a
  bare `sync` inherits the stored profile (source and patches) instead of
  silently re-stamping; the MCP `sync` tool takes `source` and follows the
  same rule; the result reports `source` and `graphql_probe_failed`;
  `status.coverage.probe_failures` exposes the latest probe failure;
  `doctor --consolidate` folds the earliest unresolved floor and never
  downgrades `is_bot` or drops `sync_pending`.

## Recurrence Prevention (defect class)

- Defect class: **a reader-side guarantee assumed from a source that does
  not provide it** — pagination offsets over a mutable order, an all-nothing
  probe chunk, keyword text that GitHub only honours on some surfaces, and
  unbounded external-text captures.
- Sweep result: 16 predicate hits, 16 disposition rows
  (`.agents/issue-traces/65-66-67-workstream-a-sync-integrity/08a-recurrence-sweep.md`);
  no hit was RECORD/DEFER/DISCLOSE-ONLY. The sweep's 15 named mutants: 14
  KILLED, 1 recorded SUBSUMPTION probe (the frozen C10 input cannot
  discriminate the digit bound; the probe asserts the bound's value
  directly). The 10 review-fix probes in `tests/_probe_review_fixes.py`
  are ALL KILLED with a byte-identical restore.
- Guardrail: the frozen checks (C1 movement detection, C10 bounds, C11
  containment, C12 corroboration, C20 indexed lookup, C21 true-v11
  migration) plus 14 demonstration probes in
  `tests/test_listing_guardrails.py` — each shown to bite by reverting the
  fix it covers.

## Tests

- Frozen acceptance replay: `PYTHONPATH=src bash
  .agents/issue-traces/65-66-67-workstream-a-sync-integrity/repro/replay-all.sh`
  → **22/22 PASS** (16 DISCRIMINATING RED→GREEN, 4 PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN,
  2 NEW-SURFACE ERROR→GREEN, zero VACUOUS), head lines bound to the PR head
  above. `PYTHONPATH=src` is required: without it the editable install makes
  a base leg import the working tree.
- Impacted suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → **Ran 1028
  tests … OK** (`repro/suite-head.log`; base tree 928 in
  `repro/suite-base.log`, its one failure an environment artifact of the
  extracted tree having no git origin).
- Mutation: `python tests/test_mutation_sweep.py` → 15/15 OK;
  `python tests/_probe_review_fixes.py` → 10/10 KILLED.
- Deferred-work scan: run inside `tests/_gen_test_results.py` over the
  diff's `src/` and `tests/` files → zero hits (the assertion fails
  generation if one appears).

## Regression Protection

- `tests/test_sync_integrity.py` (frozen C1–C9), `tests/test_sync_verdicts.py`
  (frozen C10–C14), `tests/test_extract_noise.py` (frozen C16–C21),
  `tests/test_sync_plumbing.py` (frozen C8), `tests/test_sync.py` (C7),
  `tests/test_sync_deletion.py` (C15), `tests/test_relation_registry.py`
  (C22) — 22 checks, 8 CHECK_WRONG amendment waves, semantics digest
  constant since anchor v3.
- New non-frozen coverage: `test_listing_guardrails.py` (14),
  `test_deletion_oracle.py` (10, drives the REAL oracle),
  `test_doctor_v12_carry.py` (8), `test_mutation_sweep.py` (15),
  plus pins in `test_migrations.py`, `test_sync_plumbing_extra.py`,
  `test_github.py` and `test_mcp.py`-adjacent suites.

## External Checkpoint Anchor

- Receipt published on the epic (anchor v10, comment
  [6809481434](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/64#issuecomment-6809481434)):
  `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=65-66-67-workstream-a-sync-integrity manifest=192e841efde3ba38fee36a38dfd7c6e228f4ba2c semantics=6bd191f01f2e5657e279b680bf4027c367bdcee0 tree=7687e720730494cf09167f304040bbd66cc5270b`
- Independent verification: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug
  65-66-67-workstream-a-sync-integrity --receipt '<the literal above>'`
  → exit 0. The superseded v9, v8 and v7 receipts fail closed with
  `anchor manifest digest does not match` (v9 predates the
  swarm-pr-feedback wave; v8 wave 8; v7 wave 7). The semantics digest is
  unchanged since v3 — only per-path blobs moved across the nine waves.
- Local copy/provenance: `repro/anchor-v10-body.md` (the published comment
  is authoritative; the copy is what `08-test-results.md`'s generator
  re-verifies at generation time).

## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence

| Acceptance criterion (from intake) | Evidence (command + output, or test name) |
|---|---|
| AC1 — a run ingests every item even when the listing order moves mid-run | `pytest tests/test_sync_integrity.py -q -k test_listing_survives_mid_sync_update` → RED `Lists differ: [101] != []` → GREEN; replay C1 PASS; guardrails `test_boundary_shift_forces_another_walk`, `test_subset_termination_would_lose_a_live_item`, `test_single_post_verification_recovery` |
| AC2 — a rate-window restart resumes from the committed watermark | replay C2 RED `must resume from the committed watermark; got None` → GREEN; seam `_committed_watermark` |
| AC3 — a GraphQL failure degrades to REST rather than aborting | replay C3 RED `gh: Forbidden (HTTP 403)` → GREEN; `_degradable_error` (typed transport or 401/403/404); trigger semantics disclosed in README. The shipped trigger is the first bulk-children failure — a PROBE-ONLY failure does not switch the run to REST (deliberate: the live introspection-cap failure with working GraphQL is the common case; disclosed here, in README, and in the post-publication section below) |
| AC4 — a bare sync inherits the stored source and patches | replay C4 RED `(0, 'rest') != (1, 'rest')` → GREEN; pins `test_source_name_reports_the_effective_source`, `test_explicit_mcp_source_stamps_the_profile` |
| AC5 — the MCP refresh honours `fetch_source` | replay C5 RED `must be refreshed over REST, not GraphQLSource` → GREEN |
| AC6 — a torn row is never stored as the mixture | replay C6 RED `stale listing snapshot must not be stored…` → GREEN; `test_mid_refresh_degradation_never_stores_a_stale_row` kills `return current` |
| AC7 — the watermark is passed back verbatim and inclusive | replay C7 PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN |
| AC8 — `sync --numbers` never moves the watermark | replay C8 PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN |
| AC9 — the capability probe fits the introspection budget and a probe failure is reported | replay C9 RED `a rendered probe query uses fields( 4 times` → GREEN; `graphql_probe_failed` + `coverage.probe_failures` |
| AC10 — an oversized reference token cannot wedge the run | replay C10 RED `Exceeds the limit (4300 digits)` → GREEN; `_MAX_REF_DIGITS`; M10 subsumption disclosed |
| AC11 — a deterministic extraction fault is contained and logged | replay C11 RED `deterministic extraction fault marker` → GREEN; savepoint `contained()` in `rebuild_edges` |
| AC12 — deletion verdicts need a live witness or one repository read | replay C12 RED `deletion probe resolved no nodes for a whole chunk` → GREEN; `tests/test_deletion_oracle.py` drives the REAL `GraphQLSource.check_deleted` |
| AC13 — a failed deletion pass is not laundered | replay C13 RED `must keep full_sync_pending set` → GREEN; three legs incl. later-success recovery (wave-8 re-freeze) |
| AC14 — repository reachability before `--numbers` verdicts | replay C14 RED `SyncError not raised` → GREEN; `_assert_repository_readable` + `probe_repository` |
| AC15 — the deletion module stays green | replay C15 PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN |
| AC16 — closing keywords only from a PR description and retained commits | replay C16 RED `an issue body must not produce closes_keyword` → GREEN |
| AC17 — references inside code emit nothing | replay C17 RED `[(5, 'body@11')] != []` → GREEN; `_noise_ranges` |
| AC18 — comment ids and spaced foreign refs are dropped | replay C18 RED `[(308, 'body@20')] != []` → GREEN; the two-segment over-suppression documented in docs/schema.md |
| AC19 — `actors.is_bot` exists and never downgrades | replay C19 NEW-SURFACE ERROR → GREEN; `test_extract_noise.py::test_actors_carry_is_bot`, `test_doctor_v12_carry.py::ActorBotCarryTests` |
| AC20 — the branch lookup rides an index | replay C20 RED `RATIO > 1.25` → GREEN; `idx_items_repo_branch` (migration-created) |
| AC21 — migration v12 re-derives keyword edges offline | replay C21 NEW-SURFACE ERROR → GREEN; `test_v12_rederives_keyword_edges`, `IntermediateV12ShapeTests` |
| AC22 — the relation registry still classifies every relation | replay C22 PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN |

## Invariant Audit

From AGENTS.md (the repository's invariant contract), each touched/not
touched with evidence:

- **Every edge is `confidence='EXTRACTED'`; no INFERRED/purpose field** —
  not touched: the v12 re-derivation inserts through the same
  `INSERT … 'EXTRACTED'` shape (`db.py`), and the CHECK constraint still
  enforces the value (suite green; `test_relation_registry.py` C22 green).
- **Node types are `actor|item|label|file|commit` only** — not touched:
  no new endpoint type in `extract.py`/`store.py` (grep of the diff adds
  no endpoint; C22 green).
- **Evidence is a payload, never part of an edge's identity (closes
  exception)** — not touched: the unique key and `ux_edges_closes_pair`
  are unchanged; the v12 re-derive reuses `insert_edge`'s collapse.
- **`closes_keyword` is keyword-derived, `closes` is GitHub-reported** —
  touched, in the CORRECT direction: #67 narrows the keyword side to PR
  descriptions + retained commits and AGENTS.md now states that rule
  explicitly; `closes` is untouched (C16 green).
- **Watermark passed back verbatim and inclusive; never subtracted** —
  not touched: no subtraction anywhere in the diff (C7 green); the floor
  only ever RAISES a non-NULL watermark.
- **Ingest is idempotent; child rows replaced on re-ingest; delete-owned
  edges survive** — touched only by additive paths (the pending set, the
  `branch_token` column); the delete-owned rule is unchanged (C6/C15 green).
- **A storage fault is reported, not swallowed** — not touched:
  `contained()` re-raises `sqlite3.Error` (C11 pins exactly that).
- **The read-only `sql` escape hatch (two independent layers)** — not
  touched: no `set_authorizer`/`query_only`/`ATTACH` line in the diff;
  `query.py`'s only change is a `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM meta` in `_coverage`.
- **`sync_state` counts are finish-time snapshots** — not touched
  (`recount` unchanged).

## Risk and Rollback

- Risk level: medium — a sync-path change with a schema migration (v12,
  additive and guarded) and a new durable table (`sync_pending`).
- Rollback: revert the squash; the migration is forward-only but every
  v12 addition is an additive column/table that a reverted build ignores
  (it reads the columns it knows), and no v11→v12 data is destructive.
- Residual risk: the disclosed double-churn window below; a store created
  by an intermediate build of this unreleased branch converges on open
  (`init_schema`'s guarded `computed_at` ALTER), a branch-local case only.

## Disclosed residual (a condition of the completeness claim)

The completeness guarantee is **coverage of the window this run walked**,
established by the re-walk and bounded by the 4-pass honest failure. What no
bounded-pass rule can close is the **double-churn residual**: the same live
item skipped by boundary churn in two consecutive passes in a row, which then
terminate equal. The store never *loses* an item it already holds (every
pass's deliveries accumulate), but such an item can be absent from a run that
reports complete until a later run re-lists it. Full statement:
`docs/schema.md` → "Listing completeness, the pass cap and the recovery
floor" → "Disclosed residual (a condition of this completeness claim)".

## Open product question (ASK-1, disclosed verbatim)

**RESOLVED 2026-11-12 — RATIFIED by the user, verbatim: "ratify is fine".**
The shipped scoped claim ("coverage of the window this run walked") with the
disclosed double-churn residual below is the confirmed product contract.
Adjudicated through swarm-counsel first per the standing rule (counsel
reframed the options — the original fail-closed alternative was shown to be
mechanism-unavailable — and recommended ratification). The disclosure below
is retained as history.

> ASK-1 | Product scope of the sync completeness guarantee for issue #65's
> listing fix: (a) ship the mitigation (per-boundary page re-request
> verification + set-equality pass loop) with a scoped completeness claim and
> the disclosed residual, (b) fail-closed under any unverified window, or
> (c) pause. The plan critic (round 7, R7-1) requires an explicit product
> decision, not a doc note. | OPEN — escalated via AskUserQuestion
> 2026-11-10; the user did not answer; the harness instructed "continue
> using your best judgment; do not treat it as a rejection or invent a user
> preference". Recorded judgment: option (a) adopted under the standing
> mandate and the non-objection pattern; NO verbatim user instruction
> exists. The PR body must disclose this record verbatim.

The row remains OPEN in
`.zcode/session/tasks/65-66-67-workstream-a-sync-integrity/ask-tracker.md`.
Option (a) — the mitigation with the scoped claim above — is what ships
here; it is a recorded judgment, **not a user consent**, and the disclosure
above is that record. The critic explicitly did not treat the open ASK as a
waiver.

## Post-publication review (swarm-pr-review → swarm-pr-feedback)

**swarm-pr-review** (run `pr76-20261111`): 6 base explorer lanes + all
11 micro risk families (10 dispatched, 1 NOT_TRIGGERED with absence
evidence) + 5 independent reviewer shards + 2 critic passes over the
published head → **45 normalized findings** (40 VERIFIED + 1
NEEDS_MORE_EVIDENCE + 4 REJECTED with executed refutations; the 40
cubic inline claims map 1:1 onto them), verdict REQUEST_CHANGES.

**swarm-pr-feedback** closed them in four fix commits
(`09b60fb`, `e250c10`, `9f7500f`, `7bb9444`) plus evidence-tooling
commits, with a CHECK_WRONG amendment wave (18 pairs, manifest 167 →
185) and the superseding anchor v10; then cubic's own re-review of
those commits posted nine more findings (N1-N9 — marker-only
consolidation laundering, terminal-row freshness shortcut, the
256-char noise-tail bound, the span scanner's unmatched-opener
rescan, host-scoped probe keys, generator path resolution, and
three wording precisions), all fixed in `00f1c7f` with five new
revert-probed pins and independently APPROVED by the delta
reviewer, plus the `d9b765c` precision follow-up and cubic run-3's two
    P3 test-hygiene fixes in `cc41060`. Highlights: the finalizer now
counts ANY open `sync_pending` obligation; a failed torn retry is
recorded (fetch_log + last_error); a faulted re-ingest preserves every
prior owned edge (item-source, link, and actor-inbound classes — three
revert-probed pins); the resumed full sync re-walks so the deletion
oracle sees the whole corpus; a non-dict oracle answer raises; the
listing-walk 404/410 path goes through the repository-read gate;
extraction noise handling is linear with correct fence/span masking;
both gh transports type OSError as transport; doctor consolidate unions
open obligations and re-imposes markers.

**Gates**: independent reviewer round 1–3 NEEDS_REVISION (each fix
re-probed) → **round 4 APPROVE at `7bb9444`**, with the reviewer
re-running the 1023-test suite and the 22/22 replay out-of-tree. The
pinned swarm-critic dispatch wedged twice (600s, disclosed degraded
gate); the **SolCritic fallback** first challenged the closure ledger's
stale statuses (all code/evidence checks passed) and returned APPROVE
after the ledger recorded completed dispositions. Evidence at this head:
suite **1023 OK**, replay **22/22 PASS** bound to this head, manifest
185 rows (22 CHECKPOINT + 163 AMEND), `verify-checkpoint` +
`verify-anchor` exit 0, mutation sweep and review-fix probes executed
by the generator (15/15, ALL KILLED).

**Ruled design questions** (reviewer deferred, critic ruled):
pytest-less checkouts SKIP the mutation sweep with a named reason (CI
installs pytest and runs it) — adequate; the faulted-reingest scope is
whole-item when anything owned exists (conservative, preserves
evidence) — sound.

**Disclosed boundaries from the round**: the listing reachability gate
is fail-open for sources without `probe_repository` (every shipped
source has it — GraphQLSource inherits GhApiSource's); a probe-only
failure never reports `rest (graphql unavailable)` (deliberate — the
live introspection-cap case — README discloses); the pre-existing
probe-failure fetch_log row still defaults to http_status 200 (the
degradation row added here carries the real status); the linear noise
scan has no timing pin (timing tests are flaky; structure reviewed and
measured in the review record).

## Considered, not filed

| # | Item | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tests/test_mutation_sweep.py` M2 carries three unused draft locals (`real`, `real_loop`, `one_pass`) | RECORD — cosmetic, no behavioral effect; the round-4 reviewer raised it below its finding threshold. Re-evaluate if the sweep file is next touched. |
| 2 | `_batch_fully_covered`'s newest-duplicate stamp fold has no dedicated pin | RECORD — a cost-only decision (whether a page's bulk children call is skipped); the per-ROW rule it mirrors is pinned by the replay tests. Disclosed in 08a's sweep preamble. |
| 3 | `_resolve_torn_row`'s no-refresh-seam path is unpinned (reverting `return None` → `return list_raw` keeps the suite green) | RECORD — production exposure is zero (both shipped sources implement the seam) and `return None` is the safe direction; a Protocol-conforming source without the seam leaves its torn number pending rather than storing the mixture. |
| 4 | The targeted-run exclusion from the torn retry has no dedicated test | RECORD — documented in docs/schema.md, matches issue #23's "fetch exactly the numbers named" contract; C6 pins the non-targeted retry instead. |
| 5 | Published anchor v9's evidence line says "1003 OK" while the log it names records 1004 | RECORD — the comment was true at publication and is immutable; `repro/suite-head.log` and `08-test-results.md` carry the current number, and the discrepancy is recorded in 08b. |
| 6 | The `_FOREIGN_SPACED_RE` two-segment rule drops `word/word #N` even when it might be a same-repo path (`src/app #5`) | RECORD — textually indistinguishable from a foreign slug; never fabricating an edge is the conservative direction. Documented in docs/schema.md. |
| 7 | A `>50`-candidate all-gone window costs `ceil(n/50)` repository reads (one per chunk) | RECORD — the chunk is the evidentiary unit (the same candidates are marked together); documented in the `check_deleted` docstring. |
| 8 | The probe-failure fetch_log row still records http_status 200 (pre-existing at base; the NEW degradation row added by this PR carries the real status) | RECORD — pre-existing half of review PRR-030; fixing it would touch a base-behavior row outside this PR's introduced surface without user go-ahead. Re-evaluate when fetch_log provenance is next touched. |
| 9 | `--include-patches` inheritance has no `--no-patches` opt-out (a store that ever stored patches keeps storing them) | RECORD — behavior is deliberate (the MCP docstring states it); adding an opt-out is a product decision (Improvement, listed in the final report). Re-evaluate if patch storage cost is raised. |
| 10 | The listing-walk reachability gate is fail-open for sources without `probe_repository` | RECORD — every shipped source has the probe (GraphQLSource inherits GhApiSource's); a third-party probe-less source keeps the per-item verdict. Re-evaluate if a non-`GhApiSource`-derived source ships. |
| 11 | A probe-only failure never reports `source: rest (graphql unavailable)` (issue #65 AC3's literal wording) | RECORD — deliberate: the live capability-probe failure with working GraphQL is the common case (the open ASK-1's sibling evidence); README and the AC3 row disclose the narrower trigger. Re-evaluate if issue #65's wording is amended. |
| 12 | The linear noise scan (PRR-007) has no timing pin | RECORD — timing assertions are flaky across CI; the structure (byte mask + bounded end-anchored probes) is reviewed and the quadratic→linear change was measured in the review record. Re-evaluate if a deterministic cost oracle is designed. |

## Waivers (or none)

None. Every acceptance criterion closed with evidence; no criterion waived,
no check skipped or weakened (the 9 CHECK_WRONG waves re-froze paths without
changing any `AC/class/check/argv/expect` cell — the semantics digest is
`6bd191f0…`, unchanged since anchor v3). The open ASK-1 above is disclosed,
not a waiver: the critic explicitly did not treat it as user consent.

fix: sync integrity - walk the listing twice, gate deletion verdicts …

…on repository reachability, narrow closing keywords to PR surfaces (closes #65, #66, #67)

#65: the issues listing is served by fixed page offsets over a mutable
sort=updated order, so an updated or deleted item shifts every later item
up one and the next page silently skips a live one. Every run now walks
its window at least twice and continues while a pass's item set differs
from its predecessor's (exact set equality), each full page is re-read
once for boundary verification, a churn that never quiesces fails the run
incomplete with a persisted recovery floor (listing_floor /
listing_floor_active) instead of claiming coverage, a rate-window restart
re-reads the committed watermark, a GraphQL transport failure degrades to
the per-item REST path (GitHubTransportError), a torn row is skipped with
a durable sync_pending retry, and a targeted batch whose every number
answers 404 asks the repository first (probe_repository) before any
per-item deletion verdict.

#66: reference extraction is bounded (digit captures capped, so an
oversized token matches nothing instead of wedging int()), every
deterministic extraction fault is contained and logged instead of
aborting the run, and deletion verdicts come from the oracle only with a
live witness or one repository read - never from an all-nothing chunk.

#67: closing keywords are honoured only where GitHub honours them (a PR
description and retained commit messages), so the same words in an issue
body, comment or review record a mention; reference noise (code spans,
fences, diff hunks, quotes, comment ids, spaced foreign refs) emits
nothing; actors gain is_bot (payload signals + ZAXBYGRAPH_BOT_LOGINS,
never downgraded, backfilled by the v12 migration); PR head_refs gain an
indexed branch_token; and migration v12 re-derives every keyword edge
offline under these rules with the malformed-row preservation policy.

Also: doctor --consolidate folds the earliest unresolved listing floor
and never downgrades is_bot; the targeted finalizer no longer launders
an open deletion pass's error; schema.sql carries the v12 columns.

pull.body:
Closes #65, closes #66, closes #67

PR head: cc4106079a8fe91424836283256029c7aa3cff82

# Workstream A: sync integrity — a long sync no longer skips items, fabricates deletions, or mis-reads closing keywords

## Root Cause

Three independent defects shared one shape: a local, mechanically-derived
graph trusting a source that does not give the guarantees the reader assumes.

- **#65** — GitHub serves the issues listing as fixed page offsets over a
  `sort=updated` order that MOVES: an already-delivered item that is updated
  or deleted shifts every later item up one, so the next page's offset skips
  a live item (`src/zaxbygraph/github.py:list_issues`). Nothing re-checked
  the page just served, and nothing re-walked the window, so the skipped item
  was silently absent from a store that reported itself complete. A rate
  window also restarted the walk from the run-start binding instead of the
  committed watermark, and a GraphQL failure (validation, schema drift, or a
  hung `gh`) aborted the whole run.
- **#66** — reference digits were captured with an unbounded `(\d+)`, so a
  4300+-digit token in a comment body wedged `int()` and killed the run at
  that item forever; a deterministic extraction fault likewise escaped the
  item transaction; the deletion oracle refused every all-gone chunk
  (`deletion probe resolved no nodes for a whole chunk`), so a REAL deletion
  made every subsequent `sync --force` fail; and `sync --numbers` marked
  items deleted from an all-404 batch that was really a repository-level
  access failure.
- **#67** — `closes_keyword` was derived from any text surface, so an issue
  body containing a closing keyword closed its target (GitHub honours closing keywords only in
  PR descriptions and commit messages); code spans, fences, diff hunks,
  quotes, `comment #308` ids and spaced foreign refs all became edges; there
  was no bot identity (`actors.is_bot`) and no indexed branch lookup (the
  per-issue `branch_ref` derivation scanned).

## Fix

- **Listing completeness** (`github.py`, `sync.py`): every run that drains
  the listing walks its window at least twice; each FULL page is re-read
  once and its number set compared (a mismatch ends the pass through
  `ListingShiftedError`); the loop continues until a pass's delivered set
  equals its predecessor's exactly (set equality, not subset — a subset rule
  stops on a pass that lost an item the store still lacks); the 4-pass cap
  fails the run `listing_not_quiescent` with a persisted recovery floor
  (`listing_floor`/`listing_floor_active`), keeps `full_sync_pending`, and
  suppresses the clean finish; the next run re-drains from the earlier of
  the floor and the watermark and clears it on success; a rate-window
  restart re-reads the committed watermark (`_committed_watermark`); a typed
  transport failure or a 401/403/404 on the bulk children query degrades to
  the per-item REST path (`GitHubTransportError`, `_degradable_error`).
- **Torn rows** (`sync.py`): a pull payload newer than its listing row is
  refreshed (bounded at 2 attempts) or SKIPPED into the durable
  `sync_pending(reason='torn')` set — never stored as the mixture — and
  every later non-targeted run retries it first. A 404 during the retry
  resolves as a deletion through the repository-read gate.
- **Deletion verdicts** (`graphql.py`, `sync.py`, `store.py`): the
  PRODUCTION `GraphQLSource.check_deleted` owns chunking and the whole
  truth table (live witness corroborates / dead witness raises / no witness
  = one `probe_repository()` read / one-argument call keeps the base
  refusal); the pass writes its candidate set to `sync_pending` BEFORE the
  probe and marks only after every chunk succeeds; a failed pass is retried
  by a later non-full run over exactly the pending set and clears rows,
  marker and error together; the `--numbers` reachability gate asks the
  repository before any per-item 404 verdict.
- **Reference extraction** (`extract.py`): digit captures capped at 10
  (`_MAX_REF_DIGITS`) so an oversized token matches nothing instead of
  wedging `int()`; `_noise_ranges`/`_is_noise_reference` suppress code
  spans, fenced blocks, diff hunks, quotes, `comment #<id>` and spaced
  foreign refs; `closes_keyword` derives only from PR descriptions and
  retained commit messages (issue bodies, comments and reviews record
  `mentions`).
- **Bot identity and branch lookup** (`store.py`, `db.py`): `actors.is_bot`
  from the `[bot]` suffix, REST `type`, GraphQL `__typename`, or the
  `ZAXBYGRAPH_BOT_LOGINS` exact-login list — max-semantics, never
  downgraded, backfilled by migration v12 from stored payloads; PR
  `head_ref` derives an indexed `branch_token` for the `branch_ref` lookup.
- **Migration v12** (`db.py`, `schema.sql`): guarded column/table adds,
  the `is_bot`/`branch_token` backfills, and a streaming offline
  re-derivation of every `source='keyword'` edge under the #67 rules with
  the malformed-row preservation policy.
- **Surfaces** (`cli.py`, `mcp_server.py`, `query.py`, `doctor.py`): a
  bare `sync` inherits the stored profile (source and patches) instead of
  silently re-stamping; the MCP `sync` tool takes `source` and follows the
  same rule; the result reports `source` and `graphql_probe_failed`;
  `status.coverage.probe_failures` exposes the latest probe failure;
  `doctor --consolidate` folds the earliest unresolved floor and never
  downgrades `is_bot` or drops `sync_pending`.

## Recurrence Prevention (defect class)

- Defect class: **a reader-side guarantee assumed from a source that does
  not provide it** — pagination offsets over a mutable order, an all-nothing
  probe chunk, keyword text that GitHub only honours on some surfaces, and
  unbounded external-text captures.
- Sweep result: 16 predicate hits, 16 disposition rows
  (`.agents/issue-traces/65-66-67-workstream-a-sync-integrity/08a-recurrence-sweep.md`);
  no hit was RECORD/DEFER/DISCLOSE-ONLY. The sweep's 15 named mutants: 14
  KILLED, 1 recorded SUBSUMPTION probe (the frozen C10 input cannot
  discriminate the digit bound; the probe asserts the bound's value
  directly). The 10 review-fix probes in `tests/_probe_review_fixes.py`
  are ALL KILLED with a byte-identical restore.
- Guardrail: the frozen checks (C1 movement detection, C10 bounds, C11
  containment, C12 corroboration, C20 indexed lookup, C21 true-v11
  migration) plus 14 demonstration probes in
  `tests/test_listing_guardrails.py` — each shown to bite by reverting the
  fix it covers.

## Tests

- Frozen acceptance replay: `PYTHONPATH=src bash
  .agents/issue-traces/65-66-67-workstream-a-sync-integrity/repro/replay-all.sh`
  → **22/22 PASS** (16 DISCRIMINATING RED→GREEN, 4 PRESERVING GREEN→GREEN,
  2 NEW-SURFACE ERROR→GREEN, zero VACUOUS), head lines bound to the PR head
  above. `PYTHONPATH=src` is required: without it the editable install makes
  a base leg import the working tree.
- Impacted suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → **Ran 1028
  tests … OK** (`repro/suite-head.log`; base tree 928 in
  `repro/suite-base.log`, its one failure an environment artifact of the
  extracted tree having no git origin).
- Mutation: `python tests/test_mutation_sweep.py` → 15/15 OK;
  `python tests/_probe_review_fixes.py` → 10/10 KILLED.
- Deferred-work scan: run inside `tests/_gen_test_results.py` over the
  diff's `src/` and `tests/` files → zero hits (the assertion fails
  generation if one appears).

## Regression Protection

- `tests/test_sync_integrity.py` (frozen C1–C9), `tests/test_sync_verdicts.py`
  (frozen C10–C14), `tests/test_extract_noise.py` (frozen C16–C21),
  `tests/test_sync_plumbing.py` (frozen C8), `tests/test_sync.py` (C7),
  `tests/test_sync_deletion.py` (C15), `tests/test_relation_registry.py`
  (C22) — 22 checks, 8 CHECK_WRONG amendment waves, semantics digest
  constant since anchor v3.
- New non-frozen coverage: `test_listing_guardrails.py` (14),
  `test_deletion_oracle.py` (10, drives the REAL oracle),
  `test_doctor_v12_carry.py` (8), `test_mutation_sweep.py` (15),
  plus pins in `test_migrations.py`, `test_sync_plumbing_extra.py`,
  `test_github.py` and `test_mcp.py`-adjacent suites.

## External Checkpoint Anchor

- Receipt published on the epic (anchor v10, comment

## Disclosed residual (a condition of the completeness claim)

The completeness guarantee is **coverage of the window this run walked**,
established by the re-walk and bounded by the 4-pass honest failure. What no
bounded-pass rule can close is the **double-churn residual**: the same live
item skipped by boundary churn in two consecutive passes in a row, which then
terminate equal. The store never *loses* an item it already holds (every
pass's deliveries accumulate), but such an item can be absent from a run that
reports complete until a later run re-lists it. Full statement:
`docs/schema.md` → "Listing completeness, the pass cap and the recovery
floor" → "Disclosed residual (a condition of this completeness claim)".

+    actually served, which is how a duplicate page is produced. The
+    boundary verification is counted two ways: ``boundary_probes`` (how
+    often the same page was re-requested) and ``boundary_mismatches`` (how
+    often that re-read disagreed with the page just served).
+    Children and releases answer empty; anything else is unexpected."""
+

+        self.repo = repo
+        self.page_override = page_override or {}
+        self.listing_requests = 0
+        self.boundary_probes = 0
+        self.boundary_mismatches = 0
+        #: Every ``since=`` the walk bound, in request order — the guardrails
+        #: assert WHICH window a run drained from, not just that it ran.
+        self.since_seen: list[str | None] = []
+        self._last_served: tuple[int, frozenset[int], int] | None = None
+
+    def _ordered(self, since: str | None) -> list[dict]:
+        rows = sorted(self.items.values(), key=lambda r: (r["updated_at"], r["number"]))
+        if since:
+            rows = [r for r in rows if r["updated_at"] >= since]
+        return rows
+
+    def _window(self, params: dict) -> list[dict]:
+        per_page, page, since = (int(params.get("per_page", self.PAGE)),
+                                 int(params.get("page", 1)), params.get("since"))
+        page = self.page_override.get(page, page)
+        ordered = self._ordered(since)
+        return [deepcopy(r) for r in
+                ordered[(page - 1) * per_page:page * per_page]]
+
+    def __call__(self, path, paginate=False, _enrich_rate=True):

+            self.listing_requests += 1
+            if self.on_request is not None:
+                self.on_request(self.listing_requests, self)

+            self.since_seen.append(params.get("since"))
+            page = int(params.get("page", 1))
+            served = self._window(params)
+            if (
+                self._last_served is not None
+                and self._last_served[0] == page
+                and self._last_served[2] >= self.PAGE
+            ):

+                # and only a FULL page is followed by one — a short page
+                # ends the walk, so a later request for the same page
+                # number is a new pass, not a re-read.
+                self.boundary_probes += 1

+                    self.boundary_mismatches += 1

+            )
+            return served

+            return []  # child fetches and releases: empty answers
+        raise AssertionError(f"unexpected gh api path: {path!r}")
+

+    src = GhApiSource(*repo.split("/", 1), gh_bin="gh")
+    src._api = transport  # inject at the _api transport seam
+    return src
+
+
+def _stored(conn, repo: str) -> set[int]:
+    return {int(r[0]) for r in conn.execute(
+        "SELECT number FROM items WHERE repo = ?", (repo,))}
+
+

**AC13 live probe transcript, 2026-11-11** (run with the maintainer's go-ahead against a private probe repository; the probe script is in a session scratch directory, not in this repository).

**Method.** One throwaway issue. Four reader threads (two REST `GET .../issues/1/comments`, two GraphQL `issue.comments(last:100)`) listed the comments continuously while batches of comments were posted concurrently with `gh api -X POST`. A "stale read" is a listing that was *requested after* a POST had already returned and that does not contain that comment. `gh` 2.92.0, one machine, one login.

**Run 1** (6 rounds of 4 concurrent posts, started 2026-11-11T13:57:14Z)
```
posts ok=24 failed=0; polls rest=227 graphql=199; poll errors=0
poll round-trip seconds: min=0.28 median=0.43 max=1.90
POST round-trip seconds: min=0.63 median=0.71 max=0.94
[rest] comments never listed=0
[rest] POST-returned -> first listing that contains it (upper bound, includes poll time): median=0.02s max=0.37s
[rest] stale reads (listing requested AFTER the POST returned, comment missing): 0
[graphql] comments never listed=0
[graphql] POST-returned -> first listing that contains it (upper bound, includes poll time): median=-0.04s max=0.18s
[graphql] stale reads (listing requested AFTER the POST returned, comment missing): 0
id order vs created_at: 24 comments, 17 adjacent pairs share a created_at second, 0 pairs where the higher id has an EARLIER created_at
pairs where a POST that STARTED after another had RETURNED got a lower id: 0
```

**Run 2** (8 rounds of 6 concurrent posts, started 2026-11-11T13:58:21Z)
```
posts ok=48 failed=0; polls rest=275 graphql=243; poll errors=0
poll round-trip seconds: min=0.30 median=0.47 max=1.31
POST round-trip seconds: min=0.64 median=0.86 max=1.19
[rest] comments never listed=0
[rest] POST-returned -> first listing that contains it (upper bound, includes poll time): median=0.06s max=0.38s
[rest] stale reads (listing requested AFTER the POST returned, comment missing): 0
[graphql] comments never listed=0
[graphql] POST-returned -> first listing that contains it (upper bound, includes poll time): median=0.07s max=0.36s
[graphql] stale reads (listing requested AFTER the POST returned, comment missing): 0
id order vs created_at: 48 comments, 38 adjacent pairs share a created_at second, 0 pairs where the higher id has an EARLIER created_at
pairs where a POST that STARTED after another had RETURNED got a lower id: 0
```

**What this shows**
- Across 72 comments and 944 listings, no listing requested after a POST returned was missing that comment, on REST or GraphQL. The longest observed delay before a just-posted comment appears in a listing is therefore zero at this probe's resolution (a listing takes about 0.3 to 0.5 seconds).
- `created_at` has one-second resolution: 55 of 70 adjacent pairs share a second. Creation time alone cannot order concurrent claims, so the tie-break on comment id is needed, not optional.
- Comment ids never ran against creation order, and a POST that started after another had returned never received a lower id.

**What it does not show**
- One repository, one machine, one login, two minutes of one day. It says nothing about listing lag during a GitHub incident or from another region, and it did not test `gh issue comment` (the probe used `gh api`).
- Strict id monotonicity is observed here, not documented by GitHub as a guarantee.

**Proposed value for AC13 (not yet decided by the maintainer):** a default settle delay of 2 seconds, configurable. The observed need is zero; 2 seconds is margin for conditions this probe did not cover, and it is small against a claim that lives for hours.

**Maintainer decisions, 2026-11-11.** Five open items on #74, #77 and #64 were put to an independent critic agent, then to the maintainer as one recommendation per item. The maintainer's reply, verbatim: "accept all of the above with your recommendations". The items as accepted:

1. **Settle delay (AC13): 2 seconds by default, configurable.** The live probe on this issue saw no listing lag, so AC13 as first written was satisfied by zero. The delay is kept to cover a competing claim whose POST is still in flight; the longest POST round trip in the probe was 1.19 seconds. The read after posting stays.
2. **Queue order: this issue is worked ahead of #70, once PR #76 has merged.** PR #76 is open and changes `src/zaxbygraph/cli.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py` and `src/zaxbygraph/github.py` (`gh pr view 76 --json files`, run 2026-11-11), which this issue also changes. This issue does not change `src/zaxbygraph/derive.py`. The dependency between #74 and #77 is reversed: this issue owns the claim parser, the built-in patterns, the 72-hour window and the config keys, and #74 uses them. #74 keeps its slot.
3. **Claim comments without a session token keep gating for the claim window** and are ended by a release that carries no token, as #74 AC3 already says. This issue now says how `claim` and `release` treat them.
4. **Skill wording: `claim` before work and `pr-guard` before `gh pr create` are required steps.** `claim` itself posts nothing and reports `not_applicable` when the config chain turns claims off, or when the session's login would not be a trusted claim author on the repository. Claims are on by default (opt-out).
5. **Epic #64 gains rows for #75 and #77**, and its title and closure line are corrected to cover them.

Also accepted, from the critic's review of this issue: separate exit codes for taken, lost race and GitHub unreachable; a hint to re-sync the refused issues; claims posted in ascending issue order with one retry after a random delay; one repository-wide comment listing for `claims --live`; and the takeover path written down (the token is public, so any session can release any claim).

Not settled, and marked so in the body: how `claim` learns before posting whether its login would be a trusted author. **Same-day collision case study + one pattern gap (executed evidence, 2026-11-11).** A parallel-work collision of exactly this class ran to completion today on zaxbysauce/zmem while this issue was being amended — it empirically confirms several design choices here and surfaces one gap in the built-in claim patterns.

The incident (all times UTC): Session A claimed zmem #455+#366 at 13:08:52Z/13:09:01Z and ran a full issue-tracer chain; Session B started ~13:15Z (same login, separate clone `zmem-dev`), read A's claim comments at intake ~13:25Z **and proceeded** — misattributing them to its own earlier session (the collation-decision memory injected at SessionStart made "A is my past" the coherent reading). Both sessions published: PR #456 at 17:13Z, PR #457 at 18:58Z, both closing both issues. Claim-to-PR ~4.1h (consistent with claim 3's 5.4h median).

Data points for the design:

1. **The built-in claim patterns miss a format in recorded use.** A's claims read verbatim `Claiming for active work (2026-11-11). This issue will be worked in a collated trace with #366 …` — neither `Agent claim` nor `Working this issue` matches it, so under Design 8/AC4 defaults the `claimed` gate would NOT have gated these issues. Suggest adding a third built-in pattern (`Claiming for active work`, case-insensitive) or at least documenting it as the config-chain example; it is the second-most-common phrasing in the zmem repo's claim history.

2. **The enforcement point must be the tool's refusal, not the agent's judgment — this case is the empirical justification for Designs 10+11.** Session B *saw* the claim and rationalized proceeding (same login, shared memory, user instruction matching the claimed work). A required `claim` step that returns `taken` (exit code) removes exactly that judgment call. Advisory formats cannot fix this failure mode; the recorded opencode-swarm #3341 collision and this one both show the losing session had visibility of the claim and proceeded anyway (there via two "user-authorized" claims, here via lineage misattribution).

3. **Rival artifacts posted to the same issue thread were invisible to both sessions.** Both sessions published `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1` anchor comments on zmem #455 sixteen minutes apart (14:15:53Z and 14:31:45Z, different slugs), and A posted a superseding v2 at 15:54Z below B's — neither session ever re-read the thread. Generalizes Design 3's live-read-before-write: any protocol-critical publication step (anchor comments, PR bodies) benefits from the same fetch-before-post check, not only `claim`.

4. **Tokenless claims were the incident's shape.** A's 13:08 claims carry no session token, so Design 9's tokenless semantics (a tokenless release ends them) and Design 13's takeover path are the operative resolution paths for this class. Confirms both are load-bearing, not edge cases.

5. **pr-guard (Design 5) would have caught PR #457 pre-open** — both PRs list both issues as closing references, and at 18:58Z PR #456 was open with no release comment on either issue.

Cross-referencing #74 (read-side gate): the same pattern gap applies to AC1's probe fixtures — the recorded zmem claim format above would pass through ungated.

Provenance: timestamps verified via `gh api repos/zaxbysauce/zmem/issues/455/comments` and `gh pr view 456/457` on 2026-11-11; the Session B side is this reporter's own session.

*Provenance: generated on 2026-11-11 from a research and independent-critic pass on agent collisions, run in a Claude Code session on the maintainer's machine. Every claim about current behaviour below was re-checked against the anchor commit origin/main 6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7 on 2026-11-11 by an executed probe or a source trace; claims about recorded use were re-checked the same day with read-only `gh` calls against ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm. One issue = one PR. Tracking: #64. The probe scripts named below live in a session scratch directory and are not in this repository.*

_Amended 2026-11-11 from the maintainer decisions recorded at https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/77#issuecomment-6801348954: Design 3 and 4 changed and Design 7 to 13 added; AC2, AC3, AC11 and AC13 changed; AC14 to AC18 added; this issue now owns the claim parser, patterns, window and config keys, is worked ahead of #70 once PR #76 merges, and blocks #74 instead of depending on it._

## Summary
After this PR, an agent takes a claim on one or more issues with one command that looks at GitHub live before it writes, backs off when another session got there first, and says so in its exit code. A second command releases the claim, a third refuses to let a second pull request be opened for an issue that already has one, and a live view lists who holds what without waiting for a sync. Agents stop hand-posting claim comments in a format each session invents, and the read side in #74 gets a claim format it can tell sessions apart by.

## Problem (claims to verify)
1. **There is no way to take or release a claim through the tool.** The CLI registers no `claim`, `release` or `pr-guard` command, and the MCP server lists no such tool. A search of `src/zaxbygraph/*.py` at the anchor commit for a parser or tool named `claim`, `claims`, `release` or `pr-guard` returns nothing (`grep -n -E`, exit 1). Agents post the claim by hand with `gh issue comment`. VERIFIED by source trace at the anchor commit.
   [cli.py#L2207](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/cli.py#L2207)
   ```py
       sp = sub.add_parser("sync", help="Fetch issues/PRs into the local graph")
   ```
2. **The recorded collisions are hours apart, and the existing gate cannot see them.** On ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm issue 3341, one claim comment was posted at 2026-11-09T13:10:01Z (cluster 3358 + 3337 + 3341) and a second at 2026-11-09T22:05:34Z (cluster 3341 + 3337 + 3362). Pull request 3631 was opened at 2026-11-10T01:26:58Z and pull request 3632 at 2026-11-10T02:58:14Z; both list issues 3337 and 3341 as closing references. Both claims say "user-authorized", so whether the overlap was intended is unknown; the timescale is not. The `linked_pr` gate reads pull requests already in the store, so it could not have gated the second claim: no pull request existed yet. VERIFIED by `gh api repos/ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm/issues/3341/comments` and `gh pr view 3631` / `gh pr view 3632` with `closingIssuesReferences`, 2026-11-11.
   [derive.py#L1670-L1679](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/derive.py#L1670-L1679)
   ```py
           direct_linked = any(
               states.get(dst, {}).get("state") == "open"
               and states.get(dst, {}).get("kind") == "pr"
               for dst in linked_pr_dsts.get(number, set())
           )
           keyword_linked = bool(keyword_closers.get(number))
           if direct_linked:
               gates.append("linked_pr")
           elif keyword_linked:
               gates.append("linked_pr (append-only evidence; may be stale)")
   ```
3. **A claim lives for hours, never days.** Across the 43 opencode-swarm issues that GitHub search returns for `is:issue "Agent claim" in:comments`, 35 have a pull request cross-referenced after the first claim. The time from first claim to that pull request has a median of 5.4 hours, a 90th percentile of 19.1 hours and a maximum of 24.4 hours; none exceeds 72 hours, and two issues have no pull request after the claim. The measure is the first cross-referencing pull request, which is not always the fixing one. VERIFIED by an executed GraphQL probe (`claims.py ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm 5`), 2026-11-11.
   [derive.py#L1667-L1669](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/derive.py#L1667-L1669)
   ```py
               gates.append("blocked")
           if number in assignees:
               gates.append("assigned")
   ```
4. **A stale store hides a fresh claim for up to fifteen minutes.** A read on the MCP surface answers from the store and only then starts a sync, so a claim posted inside that window is invisible to `triage` and `bundle`. No recorded collision has been traced to this window; the one fifteen-minute case in #74 claim 2 came from a wrong column value in a hand-written sweep. VERIFIED by source trace at the anchor commit.
   [SKILL.md#L97-L98](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md#L97-L98)
   ```md
   - Stale reads (default threshold 15 minutes) answer immediately and start one
     background sync; `freshness.refreshing: true` tells you new data is landing.
   ```
5. **Every session posts as the same login.** In the same probe, 40 claim comments were found and no issue carries claims from more than one login (`issues_multi_claim_authors: 0`); the claims on issues 3341 and 3588 are all by one login with association `MEMBER`. An author field therefore cannot say which session holds a claim. VERIFIED by the executed probe and by `gh api` on issues 3341 and 3588, 2026-11-11.
   [db.py#L1220](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/db.py#L1220)
   ```py
       ("author_association", "TEXT"),
   ```
6. **A new write tool would be advertised as read-only.** Tool annotations are set by one rule that names `sync` as the only writer, so a `claim` tool added to the list would carry `readOnlyHint: true` and a client could approve it without asking. VERIFIED by source trace at the anchor commit.
   [mcp_server.py#L1312](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py#L1312)
   ```py
       _tool["annotations"] = {"readOnlyHint": _tool["name"] != "sync"}
   ```
7. **The skill tells agents that every work-selection command is read-only.** That sentence becomes false once a claim can be written. VERIFIED by source trace at the anchor commit.
   [SKILL.md#L154-L157](https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/blob/6009c30269f77e3c0d3cfddaa583db2530f56ba7/skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md#L154-L157)
   ```md
   Everything this workflow returns is **candidates, not facts**: scores are
   heuristics over stored evidence (reactions, participants, blocking,
   re-opens, reverts, co-change), every command is read-only, and the store
   never records a ranking decision. Missing features are reported as `null`
   ```

## Design
The claim is an issue comment. GitHub stamps the comment's creation time, which is the only server-assigned time available, so order and expiry are read from it.

1. Claim comment, one per named issue: `**Agent claim:** session=<token> issues=#a,#b` followed by optional free text. The token is an identifier, not a secret: `claim` generates it (or takes `--session`), prints it, and `claims --live` shows it, so a session that lost its token can read it back.
2. Release comment: `**Claim released:** session=<token>` followed by optional free text.
3. `claim N...` reads the named issues' comments and the open pull requests that close them, live through `gh`, without a store sync. It refuses when any named issue has an active claim from another session or an open closing pull request. Otherwise it posts the claim on the named issues in ascending issue number, waits the settle delay (Design 7), and reads again. Per issue, the earliest active claim wins: creation time, then comment id, an order every reader computes the same way from the same listing. A session that lost any named issue releases every claim it just posted. It then waits a random one to five seconds, reads once more, and posts again, once, only if no named issue has an active claim or an open closing pull request; otherwise it exits with the lost-race code.
4. A claim is active when its author association is `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR`, it is younger than the claim window (72 hours by default, Design 8), no release carries its token, and the issue is open with no open closing pull request.
5. `pr-guard N...` is the last check before `gh pr create`.
6. A git-ref lock was considered and rejected for this PR: the recorded collisions are minutes to hours apart (claims 2 to 4), a ref carries no server time to expire by, and a local test showed two claimers pushing the same commit both exit 0. It stays out unless the comment protocol is shown to race in practice.
7. Settle delay: 2 seconds by default, set by the config chain or `--settle-seconds`. The live probe on this issue saw no listing lag (0 stale reads in 944 listings), so the delay is not there for lag. It covers a competing claim whose POST is still in flight when this session reads; the longest POST round trip in the probe was 1.19 seconds.
8. This PR owns the claim vocabulary, in the new `claims.py`: the built-in claim patterns (`Agent claim`, `Working this issue`, case-insensitive), the built-in release pattern (a comment that starts with `**Claim released`), the session-token form `session=<token>`, the 72-hour window, the settle delay, and a switch that turns claims off for a repository. The config chain overrides each. #74 reads the same parser and values.
9. A claim comment without a session token, by a trusted author and inside the window, is an active claim held by no token. `claim` refuses on it like any other. `release --tokenless` posts `**Claim released:**` with no token and ends every tokenless claim on that issue; it does not end a claim that carries a token, and a release that carries a token does not end a tokenless claim. This is the rule #74 AC3 states for the gate.
10. Every claim command ends with one outcome in its envelope: `claimed`, `not_applicable`, `taken`, `lost_race` or `github_unreachable`. The first two exit 0. Each of the last three has its own non-zero exit code. A refusal names the `sync --numbers` command line for the refused issues, because the store does not show the refusing claim until those issues are synced. Until #74 lands, `triage` and `bundle` do not gate on a claim at all, so the caller must leave the refused issues out of its next pick itself.
11. `claim` is a required step in the skill, and the command decides whether it applies. It posts nothing and reports `not_applicable` when the config chain turns claims off, or when the session's login would not be a trusted claim author on the repository (Design 4), since every reader would ignore that claim. Claims are on by default. UNKNOWN: how to learn the second condition before posting. GraphQL `viewerPermission` answered `ADMIN` on this repository and `READ` on `cli/cli` for the session's login (run 2026-11-11); how that maps to a comment's author association has not been probed, and the PR must record the probe that settles it.
12. `claims --live` lists claims with one paginated repository-wide call, `repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/comments?since=<start of the window>`, instead of one call per open issue. That call was run on 2026-11-11 against ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm with `since=2026-11-04T00:00:00Z` and returned 24 comments that start with `**Agent claim`.
13. Takeover: the session token is printed in the claim comment, so any session can run `release` with another session's token. That is the takeover path for a claim whose session has ended, and the skill says so. Nothing in this PR stops a session from releasing a live claim; the protocol is cooperative.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AC1: WHEN `zaxbygraph claim` names open issues that have no active claim and no open closing pull request, THE SYSTEM SHALL post one claim comment per named issue in the Design 1 format, print the session token and the comment URLs, and exit 0.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_claim_posts_on_every_named_issue
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No command at base (claim 1).
- [ ] AC2: IF the live read before posting finds an active claim from another session (a claim without a token counts, Design 9), or an open pull request that closes a named issue, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL post nothing, name the holder's session token (null when the claim carries none) or the pull request number, report outcome `taken` with the `sync --numbers` command line for the refused issues, and exit with the code reserved for `taken`.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_claim_refuses_taken_issue
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No command at base; this is the live read that claims 2 and 4 show is missing.
- [ ] AC3: IF the read after posting finds an earlier active claim from another session on any named issue, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL post a release carrying its own token on every issue it posted to, name the winner, try again at most once as Design 3 describes, and exit with the code reserved for `lost_race` when it does not end up holding every named issue.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_claim_loser_releases_everything
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No command at base. All-or-nothing across a bundle, with the order taken from comment creation time and then comment id.
- [ ] AC4: IF posting a claim fails on one named issue after succeeding on others, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL release the claims it posted, exit non-zero, and list any comment it could not release.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_partial_post_is_rolled_back
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No command at base. A half-posted bundle would gate issues nobody is working.
- [ ] AC5: WHEN `zaxbygraph release` names issues and a session token, THE SYSTEM SHALL post one release comment in the Design 2 format on each named issue that carries an active claim with that token, and exit non-zero without posting when none does.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_release_matches_token
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No command at base. The token is what tells sessions apart under one login (claim 5).
- [ ] AC6: WHEN `zaxbygraph pr-guard` names issues, THE SYSTEM SHALL read open pull requests live, exit non-zero listing each open pull request that closes a named issue, and exit 0 when there is none.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_pr_guard_finds_open_closer
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No command at base. Pull request 3632 was opened ninety-one minutes after 3631 for the same two issues (claim 2).
- [ ] AC7: WHEN `zaxbygraph claims --live` runs, THE SYSTEM SHALL list active and expired claims read from GitHub at call time, marked `live: true` and `derived: false`, with ages measured from the wall clock, and SHALL leave the store byte-identical.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_claims_live_view
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No command at base. The live view is separate from the deterministic `claims` listing in #74.
- [ ] AC8: WHEN a claim comment's author association is not `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR`, THE SYSTEM SHALL not treat it as an active claim in `claim`, `release` or `claims --live`, and SHALL list it as `trusted: false`.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_untrusted_author_cannot_hold_a_claim
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No command at base. On a public repository anyone can post a comment that names many issues.
- [ ] AC9: WHEN any claim command returns text taken from a comment, THE SYSTEM SHALL wrap it in `untrusted_text` and return issue numbers, session token, author, association and time as separate parsed fields.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_comment_text_is_wrapped
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No command at base. Comment text is written by whoever can comment.
- [ ] AC10: WHEN the MCP tool list is read, THE SYSTEM SHALL list `claim` and `release` with `readOnlyHint: false` and SHALL keep `readOnlyHint: true` on every tool that has it at base.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_mcp_write_tools_are_not_read_only
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No tool at base; the single annotation rule would mark a new tool read-only (claim 6).
- [ ] AC11: WHEN the bundled skill is read, THE SYSTEM SHALL state the claim and release formats including the tokenless forms, make `claim` before work and `pr-guard` before `gh pr create` required steps, say that `claim` reports `not_applicable` where claims do not apply, say that a session may release another session's claim by its token and that this is for a claim whose session has ended, and no longer say that every work-selection command is read-only.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_skill_requires_claim_and_pr_guard
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: Docs test; the sentence in claim 7 is false after this PR.
- [ ] AC12: THE SYSTEM SHALL leave the store byte-identical when the derived tier runs.
  - class: PRESERVING
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_similar.py -q -k test_derived_tier_never_writes
  - expect: OK
  - files: tests/test_similar.py
  - why: GREEN at base. Claims are GitHub comments; nothing is persisted in the store by this PR.
- [ ] AC13: WHEN the built-in settle delay between posting and re-reading is chosen, THE SYSTEM SHALL ship the value the maintainer records. DECIDED 2026-11-11: 2 seconds, configurable; claims are ordered by creation time and then comment id.
  - class: NON-EXECUTABLE(PRODUCT_DECISION)
  - files: n/a
  - substitute evidence: the maintainer's decision recorded on this issue (https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/77#issuecomment-6801348954) and the live probe transcript (https://github.com/ZaxbyHub/zaxbygraph/issues/77#issuecomment-6797834458): 72 concurrent comments and 944 listings with no stale read, a longest POST round trip of 1.19 seconds, creation times at one-second resolution, and no comment id against creation order. The suite must not call live GitHub (CONTRIBUTING repo notes).
- [ ] AC14: WHEN no config file exists, THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the built-in claim patterns (`Agent claim`, `Working this issue`, case-insensitive), the built-in release pattern (a comment that starts with `**Claim released`), the session-token form `session=<token>`, a window of 72 hours, a settle delay of 2 seconds and claims switched on; the config chain SHALL override each, and every claim command's payload SHALL echo the values in effect.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_claim_config_defaults_and_overrides
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No setting at base. This PR owns the values; #74 reads them (Design 8).
- [ ] AC15: IF the config chain turns claims off, or the session's login would not be a trusted claim author on the repository, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL post nothing from `claim`, report outcome `not_applicable` with the reason, and exit 0.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_claim_not_applicable_posts_nothing
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No command at base. A claim every reader ignores is only noise on someone else's repository (Design 11); how the second condition is learned before posting is unknown and the PR records the probe that settles it.
- [ ] AC16: WHEN a claim command ends, THE SYSTEM SHALL report exactly one outcome of `claimed`, `not_applicable`, `taken`, `lost_race` or `github_unreachable`, exit 0 for the first two, and use a different non-zero exit code for each of the last three; IF GitHub cannot be reached before posting THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL post nothing.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_outcomes_have_distinct_exit_codes
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No command at base. A caller must tell a taken issue from an outage without parsing text.
- [ ] AC17: WHEN `zaxbygraph release --tokenless` names issues, THE SYSTEM SHALL post one release comment with no token on each named issue that carries an active tokenless claim, SHALL leave a claim that carries a token active, and SHALL not let a release that carries a token end a tokenless claim.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_tokenless_claim_and_release
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No command at base. None of the 24 claim comments posted on ZaxbyHub/opencode-swarm since 2026-11-04 carries a `session=` token (Design 12's call, re-run 2026-11-11), and #74 AC3 gates on them.
- [ ] AC18: WHEN `claim` names several issues, THE SYSTEM SHALL post in ascending issue number, and after a lost race SHALL post again at most once, after a random delay and only when a fresh read shows no named issue taken.
  - class: NEW-SURFACE
  - argv: python -m pytest tests/test_claim_cmd.py -q -k test_claims_post_in_issue_order_and_retry_once
  - expect: `ERROR: file or directory not found: tests/test_claim_cmd.py` (pytest exit 4): the check file does not exist at base.
  - files: tests/test_claim_cmd.py
  - why: No command at base. Two sessions with overlapping bundles can each lose one issue to the other and both back off; a fixed order and one delayed retry let one of them through.

## Scope
**In:** the `claim`, `release`, `pr-guard` and `claims --live` commands and the matching MCP tools; the claim and release comment formats; the live read before and after posting; rollback of a partly posted bundle; the trusted-author rule; the claim parser, built-in patterns, window, settle delay and config keys; tokenless claims and their release; outcomes and exit codes; the `not_applicable` case; MCP annotations; the skill and README text.
**Out:** the `claimed` gate in `triage` and `bundle` and the deterministic `claims` listing (#74); a git-ref lock (Design 6); background renewal of a claim (nothing runs between agent turns); deleting or editing other sessions' comments; assigning issues.

## Dependencies
- Depends on: PR #76 merged (it changes `src/zaxbygraph/cli.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py` and `src/zaxbygraph/github.py`, which this PR also changes)
- Schema after: none
- Gated on: none (AC13 decided 2026-11-11)
- Blocks: #74 (it reads the parser and values this PR defines)

## Files expected to change
`src/zaxbygraph/cli.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/mcp_server.py`, `src/zaxbygraph/github.py`, a new `src/zaxbygraph/claims.py`, `skills/zaxbygraph/SKILL.md`, `README.md`, `tests/fixtures.py`, new `tests/test_claim_cmd.py`.

## Definition of done
All executable ACs pass on every CI leg (Windows and Linux), and the AC13 transcript is on this issue. The PR body says `Closes #<n>` and carries `## Closure evidence` with each AC's argv and result.

item.title: Agents take, release and check work claims through one command, and a second pull request for a claimed issue is caught before it is opened

issue_comments.body:
# Closure ledger — PR #78 feedback round (final)

Head at publish: bdc859b + the one reviewed feedback commit on top. Sources: swarm-pr-review
(55 reviewer-confirmed findings), cubic review (10 violations, 2026-11-13T04:42Z), Copilot
review (2 open issues, 2026-11-13T13:44Z). 45 root clusters; every external claim is inside
a root; none dropped.

## Dispositions

- **40 FIX** — all applied and falsification-verified: battery 184 passed / 52 subtests, 64
  targeted probe legs across 4 scripts, all green; the load-bearing legs are now committed
  as `tests/test_feedback_regressions.py` (ROOT-1/2/4/5/6/8/9/10/11/12/13/15/24 families).
- **5 RECORD** — one row each in the PR body's "Considered, not filed" table (frozen-contract
  design boundaries and disclosed trade-offs; re-evaluation triggers named).
- Stage B gate: 44/45 PASS, 1 FAIL (ROOT-042: the live PR body's ext-test count publishes
  corrected with the body update after push — a GitHub-side edit by design).
- Closeout review: 44 APPROVE, 1 NEEDS_REVISION (same ROOT-042).
- Closeout critic round: NEEDS_REVISION → 5 tree findings (X-1..X-5) + 2 reply obligations
  (X-6) — ALL applied:
  - X-1: the ROOT-13 live_prs split double-counted one bot PR once per edge; replaced with
    count-once `omitted_prs`; regression test FIRST (reproduced 2≠1 on the pre-fix tree).
  - X-2: the ROOT-38 env-knob test dropped `importlib.reload` (forked exception classes,
    breaking frozen C1 when ordered first); mock.patch.dict now.
  - X-3: the ROOT-29 doc wording "`0` uncaps" was false; README + SKILL.md corrected.
  - X-4: the AC14 evidence row now reads PARTIAL GREEN (row_fields + CLI-only derived
