fix: the query surface is bounded, honest, and typed (issues #71, #72)

Closes #71, closes #72

## Root Cause

Two independent root causes on the agent-facing read surface (full analysis in the trace's
04-root-cause.md). RC-1 (#71): each read command re-decided its own bounds — `run_sql`
(query.py:1348-1384) enforced rows-only with no deadline, byte budget, cell cap, or bytes
encoding; MCP stale reads re-armed a background refresh after every failure and the runner's
failure wrote `last_error` into a healthy store's sync_state (retry storm + poisoning);
`roots/list` was sent to clients that never declared the capability (server hang); item/related
rendering was unbounded (item 51 measured 109,292 chars with `truncated: false`; related depth
5 = 511 KB). RC-2 (#72): empty/error/shape semantics were per-command accidents — a failed
first sync answered empty-success; ghost nodes for unstored numbers; `--fields`/`jsonl`
no-ops; search counts depended on `--limit`; every snapshot pull failure mapped to
`snapshot_absent`; all 16 MCP `outputSchema`s were one permissive object; sql literals
compared to stored vocabularies silently returned zero rows; argparse errors bypassed the
envelope; `item` read one number per call. Nothing model-written is in the graph; this PR
only changes how reads answer.

## Fix

Minimal per-seam patches across cli.py, query.py, mcp_server.py, derive.py, snapshot.py
(+6657/-374 total over the branch; seven commits: 25276f6 implementation, b7fd1d2 + 34f162f
review rounds, be2a369 final-critic r1, bdc859b the r2 boundary fixes, 2e7a5a6 the feedback
round (swarm-pr-review 55 findings, cubic 10, Copilot 2 -> 45 roots: 40 FIX, 5 RECORD),
and the cubic round-2 commit resolving 11 further cubic threads: 10 FIX, 1 invalid
(dismissed with probe evidence: offset+limit at ceiling binds fine, rc=0)):

- `run_sql(conn, sql, limit, repo, deadline=5.0, max_bytes=1048576)`: progress-handler deadline
  (env `ZAXBYGRAPH_SQL_TIMEOUT_S`) + serialized-size budget + 4 KiB cell caps + bytes→hex; a
  truncated-statement completion pass (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (<stmt>)`) runs under the same
  deadline because SQLite steps SELECTs lazily (measured: 2M-row CTE ≈ 0.3 s at C speed);
  `timeout` is a new coded error at BOTH adapters (never `runtime`); `no_such_table` carries a
  store-tables hint; PRAGMA refusals hint `zaxbygraph schema [TABLE]`; out-of-vocabulary
  literals add a `warnings` entry (enum columns + every repo column discovered PRAGMA-FREE via
  sqlite_master + zero-row SELECT + cursor.description — the default-deny authorizer is never
  suspended).
- MCP refresh isolation: a production wrapper snapshots the store's sync_state row before each
  stale refresh and RESTORES it on any failure (covering every nested write site by
  restoration, not flag-threading); a `_SNAPSHOT_READ_FAILED` sentinel refuses the destructive
  restore when the pre-run read failed; failure backoff (`ZAXBYGRAPH_REFRESH_BACKOFF_S`,
  default 300 s) suppresses re-arms; `refreshing:true` on started AND joined-in-flight reads
  (preserving C9), `refresh_failed` names the reason while suppressed; explicit MCP `sync`
  keeps normal error recording.
- Roots capability gating: `roots/list` is sent only to sessions that declared
  `capabilities.roots` (per-session, captured at initialize); undeclared sessions resolve via
  pin/cwd and a declared session's round-trip still resolves (frozen positive contrast).
- Bounds: `item`/`get_item` default body ≤ 20 KiB, comments ≤ 5, reviews ≤ 5 with
  `comments_omitted`/`reviews_omitted` and `truncated:true`; `related` max_nodes=100 +
  max_bytes=1 MiB (typed MCP args); `--no-bots`/`exclude_bots` filter bot-authored
  comments/reviews/items IN THE SQL pre-ranking across search (all three FTS arms), item, and
  brief, with per-surface `bots_omitted`.
- Honesty: no-corpus = live repo-scoped COUNT == 0 AND `last_full_sync_at IS NULL` (shared
  `corpus_state` at both adapters — the cached item_count snapshot is never consulted);
  `related`/`path`/`explain` unstored numbers → `not_found` (CLI + MCP); `file-history`
  normalizes separators then exact-case matches, missing → `unknown_path` with
  case-insensitive/basename suggestions (CLI + MCP); `bundle --pool` reports
  `dropped: [{number, reason}]`; MCP cursors validated (`bad_request`, never silent page 1).
- Output controls: `--fields`/`--format jsonl` on search, item (single and multi), related, similar,
  triage, bundle via a per-command list-key registry; `item N1 N2 …` returns a bare list of
  per-number rows (unstored → per-row `not_found`, reserved `not_found: true` marker survives
  projection); usage errors answer `bad_request` envelopes on stdout under machine formats
  (help/version still exit 0; dual-placement globals via SUPPRESS on subparser copies).
- Search: limit-independent `strict_matches`/`broadened_matches` counts; `total_matches` =
  broadened total; three-tier ranking (item-text surface > comment-only; phrase > scattered;
  bm25 + stable tie-break); snippet fallback chain item→comment→review (bot-filtered before
  selection); `--offset` walks the deduplicated strict-first stream; overshoot pages report
  `truncated: true` with NO `next_cursor` (a self-referential cursor would trap followers).
- Final-critic round: usage-error machine-format detection falls back to
  sys.argv (real entry points pass no list) and honours `--format=json`;
  every stdout write is translated at the boundary (`_write_stdout`), so a
  mid-render dead pipe on a LARGE output reaches the quiet BrokenPipe exit
  too; single-number `item --fields` now projects the item dict (no flag →
  byte-identical); README/SKILL.md state the new `--fields`/`jsonl` truth.
- Snapshot honesty: unreachable/unauthenticatable sources → `source_unreachable` (exit 1)
  carrying git's actionable `fatal:`/`error:` lines; reachable-without-refs stays
  `snapshot_absent` (exit 2); publish/pull envelopes carry the store's real freshness.
- Typed MCP: one shape registry (`_TOOL_SHAPES`) drives per-tool `outputSchema` (real row
  shapes incl. brief's untrusted wrapper object and sql warnings rows), `schema --output
  COMMAND`, and the SKILL.md shape table; BrokenPipeError exits quietly via a protected stdout
  flush + dup2 to os.devnull (Windows EINVAL handled narrowly at the stdout boundary only).

## Recurrence Prevention (defect class)

- Defect class: a read-path site that executes or renders unbounded user-supplied queries or
  payloads without a bound, or answers ok:true for an input that does not name a stored object.
- Sweep result: 86 hits dispositioned (08a-recurrence-sweep.md — predicate lines carry hit
  counts; one disposition row per hit): 70 `.fetchall()` sites all bounded by owner/schema/sql;
  both `fetchmany` call sites bounded; all six number-keyed read commands answer coded
  not_found/unknown_path/per-row markers post-fix.
- Guardrail: the frozen 21-check surface suite (two new files) + the pre-existing read-only
  guard battery + the exit-class census (extended for `source_unreachable`); demonstrated
  biting on the original defects (C1-C24 RED→GREEN at the certified replay).

## Tests

- Regression test: `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/test_surface_safety.py tests/test_surface_honesty.py -q -p no:randomly` → 21 passed (frozen; RED at base per repro/*.base.log)
- Additional pins: `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/test_surface_schemas_ext.py -q -p no:randomly` → 23 passed, 13 subtests (all 16 tools' real shapes; reviewer, critic and bot falsifiers)
- Impacted suite: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -b` → 1084 tests OK (feedback
  round adds tests/test_feedback_regressions.py: 12 committed pins for the load-bearing
  probe legs, incl. the regression-first count-once bot-PR test and the MCP sql budget
  wiring leg; suite was 1064 at base)
- Preserving trio: `PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest tests/test_query.py tests/test_mcp.py tests/test_mcp_typed.py -q -p no:randomly -k "test_run_sql_negative_limit_is_clamped or test_stale_read_answers_now_and_refreshes_in_background or test_tools_declare_schema_and_annotations"` → 3 passed
- Certified replay: `PYTHONPATH=src bash .agents/issue-traces/71-72-workstream-c-query-surface/replay-all.sh` → 24/24 PASS re-certified at merge head b0dd283 (initial certification at 34f162f, re-certified at 2e7a5a6, 6040513, and b0dd283 after each feedback commit per the replay-after-last-commit rule)
- Deferred-work scan: scan-deferred.sh → clean

## Regression Protection

- tests/test_surface_safety.py + tests/test_surface_honesty.py: 21 frozen checks authored
  arm's-length at the red checkpoint (anchor v4 published on #71, comment 6830629789)
- tests/test_surface_schemas_ext.py: all-16-tool schema validation + the review-round
  falsifiers (reviews-arm join predicate; overshoot no-cursor; bot-item omission via human
  review; max-body-chars 0 semantics)
- Review falsifiers executed before fixing: two Important defects found only by delta probing

## External Checkpoint Anchor

- Receipt published before implementation: `issue-tracer-checkpoint-v1 slug=71-72-workstream-c-query-surface manifest=3964690e4d37ef124060d73cdf958c19fbe3ea43 semantics=1409fd633677365c099e415fa256824a3d100280 tree=34c817aa84b9fb69b61a63c47992c80283f0f474`

- Independent verification: `repro-check.sh verify-anchor --slug 71-72-workstream-c-query-surface --receipt '<published literal>'` → PASS (executed by plan-critic r4, implementation reviewer r1-r3, and this trace)
- Local copy/provenance: .agents/issue-traces/71-72-workstream-c-query-surface/repro/checkpoint.manifest (non-authoritative)

## Acceptance Criteria -> Evidence

| Acceptance criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| #71 AC1 sql deadline + timeout error (CLI+MCP) | C1 GREEN (repro/C1.head.log); live probe: recursive CTE → coded timeout ~5.2 s |

Minimal per-seam patches across cli.py, query.py, mcp_server.py, derive.py, snapshot.py
(+6657/-374 total over the branch; seven commits: 25276f6 implementation, b7fd1d2 + 34f162f
review rounds, be2a369 final-critic r1, bdc859b the r2 boundary fixes, 2e7a5a6 the feedback
round (swarm-pr-review 55 findings, cubic 10, Copilot 2 -> 45 roots: 40 FIX, 5 RECORD),
and the cubic round-2 commit resolving 11 further cubic threads: 10 FIX, 1 invalid
(dismissed with probe evidence: offset+limit at ceiling binds fine, rc=0)):

- `run_sql(conn, sql, limit, repo, deadline=5.0, max_bytes=1048576)`: progress-handler deadline
  (env `ZAXBYGRAPH_SQL_TIMEOUT_S`) + serialized-size budget + 4 KiB cell caps + bytes→hex; a
  truncated-statement completion pass (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (<stmt>)`) runs under the same
  deadline because SQLite steps SELECTs lazily (measured: 2M-row CTE ≈ 0.3 s at C speed);
  `timeout` is a new coded error at BOTH adapters (never `runtime`); `no_such_table` carries a
  store-tables hint; PRAGMA refusals hint `zaxbygraph schema [TABLE]`; out-of-vocabulary
  literals add a `warnings` entry (enum columns + every repo column discovered PRAGMA-FREE via
  sqlite_master + zero-row SELECT + cursor.description — the default-deny authorizer is never
  suspended).
- MCP refresh isolation: a production wrapper snapshots the store's sync_state row before each
  stale refresh and RESTORES it on any failure (covering every nested write site by
  restoration, not flag-threading); a `_SNAPSHOT_READ_FAILED` sentinel refuses the destructive
  restore when the pre-run read failed; failure backoff (`ZAXBYGRAPH_REFRESH_BACKOFF_S`,
  default 300 s) suppresses re-arms; `refreshing:true` on started AND joined-in-flight reads
  (preserving C9), `refresh_failed` names the reason while suppressed; explicit MCP `sync`
  keeps normal error recording.
- Roots capability gating: `roots/list` is sent only to sessions that declared
  `capabilities.roots` (per-session, captured at initialize); undeclared sessions resolve via
  pin/cwd and a declared session's round-trip still resolves (frozen positive contrast).
- Bounds: `item`/`get_item` default body ≤ 20 KiB, comments ≤ 5, reviews ≤ 5 with
  `comments_omitted`/`reviews_omitted` and `truncated:true`; `related` max_nodes=100 +
  max_bytes=1 MiB (typed MCP args); `--no-bots`/`exclude_bots` filter bot-authored
  comments/reviews/items IN THE SQL pre-ranking across search (all three FTS arms), item, and
  brief, with per-surface `bots_omitted`.
- Honesty: no-corpus = live repo-scoped COUNT == 0 AND `last_full_sync_at IS NULL` (shared
  `corpus_state` at both adapters — the cached item_count snapshot is never consulted);
  `related`/`path`/`explain` unstored numbers → `not_found` (CLI + MCP); `file-history`
  normalizes separators then exact-case matches, missing → `unknown_path` with
  case-insensitive/basename suggestions (CLI + MCP); `bundle --pool` reports
  `dropped: [{number, reason}]`; MCP cursors validated (`bad_request`, never silent page 1).
- Output controls: `--fields`/`--format jsonl` on search, item (single and multi), related, similar,
  triage, bundle via a per-command list-key registry; `item N1 N2 …` returns a bare list of
  per-number rows (unstored → per-row `not_found`, reserved `not_found: true` marker survives
  projection); usage errors answer `bad_request` envelopes on stdout under machine formats
  (help/version still exit 0; dual-placement globals via SUPPRESS on subparser copies).
- Search: limit-independent `strict_matches`/`broadened_matches` counts; `total_matches` =
  broadened total; three-tier ranking (item-text surface > comment-only; phrase > scattered;
  bm25 + stable tie-break); snippet fallback chain item→comment→review (bot-filtered before
  selection); `--offset` walks the deduplicated strict-first stream; overshoot pages report
  `truncated: true` with NO `next_cursor` (a self-referential cursor would trap followers).
- Final-critic round: usage-error machine-format detection falls back to
  sys.argv (real entry points pass no list) and honours `--format=json`;
  every stdout write is translated at the boundary (`_write_stdout`), so a
  mid-render dead pipe on a LARGE output reaches the quiet BrokenPipe exit
  too; single-number `item --fields` now projects the item dict (no flag →
  byte-identical); README/SKILL.md state the new `--fields`/`jsonl` truth.
- Snapshot honesty: unreachable/unauthenticatable sources → `source_unreachable` (exit 1)
  carrying git's actionable `fatal:`/`error:` lines; reachable-without-refs stays
  `snapshot_absent` (exit 2); publish/pull envelopes carry the store's real freshness.
- Typed MCP: one shape registry (`_TOOL_SHAPES`) drives per-tool `outputSchema` (real row
  shapes incl. brief's untrusted wrapper object and sql warnings rows), `schema --output
  COMMAND`, and the SKILL.md shape table; BrokenPipeError exits quietly via a protected stdout
  flush + dup2 to os.devnull (Windows EINVAL handled narrowly at the stdout boundary only).

## Recurrence Prevention (defect class)

- Defect class: a read-path site that executes or renders unbounded user-supplied queries or
  payloads without a bound, or answers ok:true for an input that does not name a stored object.
- Sweep result: 86 hits dispositioned (08a-recurrence-sweep.md — predicate lines carry hit
  counts; one disposition row per hit): 70 `.fetchall()` sites all bounded by owner/schema/sql;

  guard battery + the exit-class census (extended for `source_unreachable`); demonstrated

Use a LEFT JOIN and a `WHERE` predicate that keeps rows with no actor record / NULL author while still excluding bots.

Both values are parsed and bound separately as 64-bit SQLite integers; offset+limit (~4.29e9) stays far below the 2^63 bind range, so there is no overflow path. The ceiling tests (test_feedback_regressions.py test_search_offset_ceiling_answers_envelopes) pin the envelope behavior at and past the limit ceiling.

Fixed in commit 6040513: tests/test_feedback_regressions.py::test_mcp_sql_budget_wired now drives the MCP sql tool (repo + statement args) under ZAXBYGRAPH_SQL_MAX_BYTES=2000 over 5x900B rows and asserts truncated:true, total_rows=5, and fewer shipped rows than the corpus - the MCP adapter is falsification-pinned, not just the CLI one.

Fixed in commit 6040513: SKILL.md now states the shipped selection truth - comments use the first/last/maintainer preference (survivors chronological, up to 5), reviews keep the first 5 in submitted order - instead of 'most relevant'.

Fixed in commit 6040513: the README --no-bots row now states the per-command behavior - item filters only the requested item's comments and reviews (the item itself is always returned), search also drops bot-authored items, brief also drops bot-authored linked PRs and the analog. A bot-authored item lookup stays found-with-filtered-nested-rows.

Fixed in commit 6040513: query.item now runs _require_bot_flags BEFORE the item lookup, so a missing item with exclude_bots on a pre-v12 store answers the same structured bad_request as search/brief instead of a misleading not_found. Consistency verified by the existing v11-gate regression pin.

Fixed in commit 6040513: the ceiling fixture is 10,050 matching rows (the minimum that still exercises the 9,990 + 50 > 10,000 mint boundary and keeps item_count consistent), halving the leg's scan cost. The committed leg runs in ~1s locally.

Fixed in commit 6040513: _contain_refresh_failure's _log wraps now catch (OSError, ValueError) - a closed stderr stream raises ValueError ('I/O operation on closed file'), not OSError, and could previously abort failure bookkeeping after the backoff had armed.

Recorded, not fixed in this PR - same disposition as the identical Copilot-1 finding: the 'Considered, not filed' row in the PR body covers it (slugs are stored lowercase; lower() normalizes legacy mixed-case input; correctness unaffected; the expression index is a schema migration outside this read-surface PR, re-evaluation trigger: any schema-v13 migration or a recorded zero-row-slow complaint).

Fixed in commit 6040513: _actionable_stderr strips complete ANSI CSI/OSC sequences (_strip_ansi) BEFORE the printable filter - the filter was eating the ESC bytes and leaving '[31m'/'0;title' fragments behind. Verified by probe: no '31m', no '0;title', printable-only, capped. Regression leg strengthened to assert the fragments are gone.

Fixed in commit 6040513: the README search-cost sentence now says at most FOUR small indexed queries (row, item snippet, comment snippet, review snippet) - the review snippet lookup was added by this PR.

Fixed in commit 6040513: the README item section documents the actual selection rule - comments return the first, last, and maintainer entries first (survivors chronological, up to 5); reviews keep the first 5 in submitted order.

Scoped in commit b0dd283: the README --no-bots row now states the actual brief behavior - a bot-ranked analog is dropped AFTER ranking (a bot analog in the top slot leaves the packet analog-less rather than promoting the runner-up). Filtering before analog ranking would change selection semantics owned by the derive config, so the documentation now scopes the claim to the shipped behavior instead.

Qualified in commit b0dd283: the wording now marks the 5-entry comment/review caps as defaults (comments up to 5 by default, --max-comments K overrides the count and 0 returns none; reviews keep the first 5 in submitted order, MCP get_item max_reviews overrides). Both README and SKILL.md updated.

## Summary

`snapshot pull` refuses two things before it replaces the destination store — a multi-repo destination, and a destination whose local watermark is newer than the snapshot's. On Python 3.14 a per-file stat `OSError` on the destination disables **both** refusals, and the unconditional `os.replace` in `_install` then destroys the other repos' corpora, or overwrites a newer local store with an older snapshot. After this PR, a destination whose metadata cannot be inspected is refused with a coded envelope, and the destination store is provably untouched.

## Purpose
The #21 program delivered what it specified. This review treated all of it as unproven and found that the tool's core promises do not yet hold:

1. **The store is not yet trustworthy as evidence.** A long sync can silently skip items, one comment can wedge sync for good, and `sync --numbers` can mark live items deleted.
2. **The headline feature does not work out of the box.** On this repository `triage` ranks the two finished tracking epics (#8, #21) first and `bundle` proposes them as a bundle. In a backtest over eight real multi-issue fix PRs, default bundles were 18% precise, and the built-in `eval` could not see it.
3. **The agent surface has sharp edges.** One `sql` query can hang the MCP server; a failed background refresh marks a healthy store broken; the most common read costs up to 27k tokens, mostly bot text; several empty or wrong answers look like success.

Several of these trace to the October plan's own design (co-change as an anchor, evaluation from `closes` only, closing keywords from comments, no notion of a tracking issue or a bot). The children say so where it applies.

# Workstream A: sync integrity — a long sync no longer skips items, fabricates deletions, or mis-reads closing keywords

## Root Cause

Three independent defects shared one shape: a local, mechanically-derived
graph trusting a source that does not give the guarantees the reader assumes.

- **#65** — GitHub serves the issues listing as fixed page offsets over a
  `sort=updated` order that MOVES: an already-delivered item that is updated
  or deleted shifts every later item up one, so the next page's offset skips
  a live item (`src/zaxbygraph/github.py:list_issues`). Nothing re-checked
  the page just served, and nothing re-walked the window, so the skipped item
  was silently absent from a store that reported itself complete. A rate
  window also restarted the walk from the run-start binding instead of the
  committed watermark, and a GraphQL failure (validation, schema drift, or a
  hung `gh`) aborted the whole run.
- **#66** — reference digits were captured with an unbounded `(\d+)`, so a
  4300+-digit token in a comment body wedged `int()` and killed the run at
  that item forever; a deterministic extraction fault likewise escaped the
  item transaction; the deletion oracle refused every all-gone chunk
  (`deletion probe resolved no nodes for a whole chunk`), so a REAL deletion
  made every subsequent `sync --force` fail; and `sync --numbers` marked
  items deleted from an all-404 batch that was really a repository-level
  access failure.
- **#67** — `closes_keyword` was derived from any text surface, so an issue
  body containing a closing keyword closed its target (GitHub honours closing keywords only in
  PR descriptions and commit messages); code spans, fences, diff hunks,
  quotes, `comment #308` ids and spaced foreign refs all became edges; there
  was no bot identity (`actors.is_bot`) and no indexed branch lookup (the
  per-issue `branch_ref` derivation scanned).

## Fix

- **Listing completeness** (`github.py`, `sync.py`): every run that drains
  the listing walks its window at least twice; each FULL page is re-read
  once and its number set compared (a mismatch ends the pass through
  `ListingShiftedError`); the loop continues until a pass's delivered set
  equals its predecessor's exactly (set equality, not subset — a subset rule
  stops on a pass that lost an item the store still lacks); the 4-pass cap
  fails the run `listing_not_quiescent` with a persisted recovery floor
  (`listing_floor`/`listing_floor_active`), keeps `full_sync_pending`, and
  suppresses the clean finish; the next run re-drains from the earlier of
  the floor and the watermark and clears it on success; a rate-window
  restart re-reads the committed watermark (`_committed_watermark`); a typed
  transport failure or a 401/403/404 on the bulk children query degrades to
  the per-item REST path (`GitHubTransportError`, `_degradable_error`).
- **Torn rows** (`sync.py`): a pull payload newer than its listing row is
  refreshed (bounded at 2 attempts) or SKIPPED into the durable
  `sync_pending(reason='torn')` set — never stored as the mixture — and
  every later non-targeted run retries it first. A 404 during the retry
  resolves as a deletion through the repository-read gate.
- **Deletion verdicts** (`graphql.py`, `sync.py`, `store.py`): the
  PRODUCTION `GraphQLSource.check_deleted` owns chunking and the whole
  truth table (live witness corroborates / dead witness raises / no witness
  = one `probe_repository()` read / one-argument call keeps the base
  refusal); the pass writes its candidate set to `sync_pending` BEFORE the
  probe and marks only after every chunk succeeds; a failed pass is retried
  by a later non-full run over exactly the pending set and clears rows,
  marker and error together; the `--numbers` reachability gate asks the
  repository before any per-item 404 verdict.
- **Reference extraction** (`extract.py`): digit captures capped at 10
  (`_MAX_REF_DIGITS`) so an oversized token matches nothing instead of
  wedging `int()`; `_noise_ranges`/`_is_noise_reference` suppress code
  spans, fenced blocks, diff hunks, quotes, `comment #<id>` and spaced
  foreign refs; `closes_keyword` derives only from PR descriptions and
  retained commit messages (issue bodies, comments and reviews record
  `mentions`).
- **Bot identity and branch lookup** (`store.py`, `db.py`): `actors.is_bot`
  from the `[bot]` suffix, REST `type`, GraphQL `__typename`, or the
  `ZAXBYGRAPH_BOT_LOGINS` exact-login list — max-semantics, never
  downgraded, backfilled by migration v12 from stored payloads; PR
  `head_ref` derives an indexed `branch_token` for the `branch_ref` lookup.
- **Migration v12** (`db.py`, `schema.sql`): guarded column/table adds,
  the `is_bot`/`branch_token` backfills, and a streaming offline
  re-derivation of every `source='keyword'` edge under the #67 rules with
  the malformed-row preservation policy.
- **Surfaces** (`cli.py`, `mcp_server.py`, `query.py`, `doctor.py`): a
  bare `sync` inherits the stored profile (source and patches) instead of
  silently re-stamping; the MCP `sync` tool takes `source` and follows the
  same rule; the result reports `source` and `graphql_probe_failed`;
  `status.coverage.probe_failures` exposes the latest probe failure;
  `doctor --consolidate` folds the earliest unresolved floor and never
  downgrades `is_bot` or drops `sync_pending`.

## Disclosed residual (a condition of the completeness claim)

The completeness guarantee is **coverage of the window this run walked**,
established by the re-walk and bounded by the 4-pass honest failure. What no
bounded-pass rule can close is the **double-churn residual**: the same live
item skipped by boundary churn in two consecutive passes in a row, which then
terminate equal. The store never *loses* an item it already holds (every
pass's deliveries accumulate), but such an item can be absent from a run that
reports complete until a later run re-lists it. Full statement:
`docs/schema.md` → "Listing completeness, the pass cap and the recovery
floor" → "Disclosed residual (a condition of this completeness claim)".
